Overview serves connector, semiconductor, packaging, automotive, pharmaceutical, aerospace, renewable energy, food, and textile manufacturers, and integrates with factory-floor systems (PLCs, ERPs, SCADA) over MQTT and digital I/O rather than a public REST API. Backed by GV and Homebrew. Profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Robco
providers.description: RobCo is a Munich- and Austin-based industrial robotics company building software-defined, modular robotic automation delivered as Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) with zero upfront capital expenditure. Its modular robot arms (up to 8 axes, 40 kg payload, 2.5 m reach, 0.1 mm repeatability), the Alfie autonomous robot, the RobFlow no-code programming platform, RobCo Studio configuration and simulation tooling, and the RobVision AI vision system let manufacturers automate machine tending, palletizing, materials handling, and finishing tasks. RobCo serves manufacturing, food and beverage, logistics, automotive, wood, and defense customers, and is backed by Lightspeed, Sequoia Capital, Lingotto, Kindred Capital, and Promus Ventures.

providers.name: Sphero
providers.description: Sphero designs programmable robots and STEAM (science, technology, engineering, arts and math) learning tools for K-12 education. Its product line spans indi, Mini, Snap, BOLT+, littleBits, RVR+ and Blueprint robots, paired with standards-aligned curriculum (NGSS, CSTA, ISTE) delivered through Sphero Central. For developers and educators, Sphero publishes a public robot-control SDK (sdk.sphero.com) that programs Sphero RVR+ / RVR robots from development boards — Raspberry Pi, micro:bit and Arduino — using Python, Node.js/TypeScript and C++. Sphero exposes robot-control SDKs and a locally-run Node.js RESTful interface rather than a hosted public web API. This profile is maintained by API Evangelist as part of the APIs.io network.

providers.name: Brain Corp
providers.description: Brain Corp builds BrainOS, an autonomy platform that powers commercial service robots for floor care, inventory scanning, and remote site management across retail, warehouses, education, airports, malls, healthcare, and hospitality. The product portfolio includes the BrainOS Sense Suite, Clean Suite, ShelfOptix scanning-as-a-service, RFID localization, and remote site management tools. Brain Corp integrates with OEM partners and operators rather than offering a public developer portal, and does not publish open APIs.

providers.name: Northrop Grumman
providers.description: Northrop Grumman Corporation is a US global aerospace, defense and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, organized into four segments: Aeronautics Systems, Defense Systems, Mission Systems and Space Systems. It builds autonomous aircraft, strategic bombers and long-range strike weapons, missile defense and integrated battle command systems, radar and electronic warfare sensors, cyber and command-and-control mission software, solid rocket motors, and space vehicles and launch systems for US Department of Defense, intelligence-community, NASA and allied customers. It publishes no public developer program, API portal or machine-readable API contract; its external integration surfaces are the ADFS-authenticated OASIS supplier tools on myngc.com, available only to registered suppliers under contract.

providers.name: Sunday Robotics
providers.description: Sunday Robotics is a consumer robotics company building Memo, an autonomous home robot that handles household chores such as clearing dishes, loading the dishwasher, pulling espresso shots, and folding laundry. The robot is trained on human demonstrations captured with the company's proprietary Skill Capture Glove and runs on the ACT family of robot foundation models. Founded as a physical-AI company and backed by Bain Capital Ventures, Sunday is pre-launch with a beta program opening in late 2026. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation; this record captures its public web and security surface only.

providers.name: Tutor Intelligence
providers.description: Tutor Intelligence builds AI-powered robotic workers for industrial and logistics operations, delivered as robots-as-a-service. Its flagship Cassie palletizing robot handles material-handling tasks — palletizing, depalletizing, and case picking — in warehouses and factories without facility retrofits, and a humanoid robot, Sonny, is slated for late 2026. The company pairs on-robot autonomy with a human-in-the-loop teleoperation and data model, priced per robot-hour with no long-term contracts, and is backed by Union Square Ventures. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface is published as of this profiling; the company's public GitHub organization hosts internal tooling and open-source forks rather than a first-party product API.

providers.name: Wisk Aero
providers.description: Wisk Aero is an autonomous, all-electric eVTOL air taxi developer and a wholly-owned subsidiary of The Boeing Company. Wisk is developing its Generation 6 aircraft, a four-passenger self-flying eVTOL designed to operate under human supervisor oversight from a multi-vehicle supervision center, pursuing certification under three FAA programs: Type Certification, Production Certification, and Operation Certification. Wisk evolved from earlier Kitty Hawk programs and has logged over 1,750 autonomous test flights across five aircraft generations since 2010. Announced launch communities include Houston, Texas and Brisbane, Australia (in support of the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games). In March 2026 Wisk was selected by the White House to help lead the safe U.S. introduction of autonomous air taxi flight. Wisk is hardware- and operations-focused, with no public consumer or developer APIs.

providers.name: Robotiq
providers.description: Robotiq designs and manufactures collaborative robotics hardware and software — adaptive grippers, vacuum grippers, force-torque sensors, wrist cameras, and pre-engineered workcells for palletizing, machine tending, screwdriving, and assembly. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Lévis, Quebec, Canada, the company helps manufacturers automate repetitive tasks by embedding task intelligence ("Intelligence Made Physical") directly into end-of-arm tooling for platforms such as Universal Robots, FANUC CRX, and Omron/Techman. Robotiq publishes open-source ROS drivers and a C++ gripper SDK through its GitHub organization, but it does not operate a public web/REST API — this profile captures its developer-facing identity, open-source SDKs, and domain security posture rather than a hosted API surface.

providers.name: Udacity
providers.description: Udacity is an online tech-upskilling platform offering project-based Nanodegree programs, individual courses, and enterprise workforce development across Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Agentic AI, Data Science, Cloud Computing, Cybersecurity, Programming, Autonomous Systems, Product Management, and DevOps. Founded by Sebastian Thrun out of the Stanford CS221 free online AI course in 2011, Udacity pioneered the Nanodegree credential and partnered with industry leaders (AWS, Google, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Mercedes-Benz) to co-develop curriculum. In 2024 Accenture acquired Udacity for approximately $1B and folded the platform into LearnVantage, Accenture's enterprise learning and skilling business. Udacity reports 25M+ learners globally and remains best known for its Self-Driving Car, Deep Learning, and Generative AI Nanodegrees, with hands-on projects reviewed by human mentors and career services. Udacity does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — enterprise customers integrate via Accenture LearnVantage sales channels rather than self-service APIs. Its public GitHub organization (github.com/udacity) hosts 1,100+ open-source classroom and course-content repositories (e.g. deep-learning-v2-pytorch, self-driving-car, cd13303-genai-c1-classroom) used as Nanodegree exercises, not as official platform APIs.

providers.name: Drag Bot
providers.description: drag&bot is a web-based industrial robotics software platform for the intuitive setup, programming, and operation of industrial robots without prior robotics or coding skills. Founded in Stuttgart in 2016 and acquired by KEBA in 2021, it lets production workers assemble robot programs by dragging and dropping reusable Function Blocks. The platform is built on ROS (Robot Operating System), making it vendor-neutral across robot brands such as KUKA, ABB, Universal Robots, FANUC, Denso, Kinova, and Aubo, as well as a wide range of grippers and peripheral tools. Developers extend the platform with Python/JSON Function Blocks and ROS-based Components (hardware drivers), and integrate with factory equipment over Modbus TCP/IP and MQTT. drag&bot has been integrated into KEBA's Kemro X automation platform. Its programmatic surface is exposed as ROS services, topics, and messages rather than a public REST/HTTP API.

providers.name: Heven AeroTech
providers.description: Heven AeroTech (formerly Heven Drones) is a Dulles, Virginia headquartered manufacturer of hydrogen fuel-cell powered, runway-independent unmanned aircraft systems built for defense, national security and public safety missions. Founded in 2019, the company designs its own hydrogen propulsion stack and ships six named airframes — Raider, Z1, H2D55, Refueler, Atlas and Urban X — marketed on multi-hour endurance, low thermal and acoustic signature, and rapid payload and hydrogen-tank swaps. The Z1 is listed as a Blue UAS Select platform and the H2D55, Raider and Z1 are advertised as NDAA compliant. Heven operates sites in Dulles VA, Bingen WA, Mevo Carmel Israel and Mumbai India, and raised a $100M Series B led by IonQ. Heven AeroTech is a hardware manufacturer: it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: AMP Robotics
providers.description: AMP Robotics (operating as AMP Sortation) is an artificial-intelligence company for the waste and recycling industry that designs, builds, and operates advanced, cost-competitive facilities to process single-stream recycling and municipal solid waste. Its Smart Sortation technology suite combines computer vision (real-time material characterization), high-speed air-jet sortation (Jet and MicroJet), and robotic-arm sortation (Delta) to raise material-recovery rates, cut contamination, and extend landfill life. The flagship AMP ONE platform delivers fully automated, facility-scale sortation processing from 10K to 1M+ tons annually for waste haulers, material-recovery facilities, and municipalities. AMP Robotics is a Google Ventures (GV) portfolio company. No public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal is published; this profile is maintained for network discovery and identity.

providers.name: Carbon Robotics
providers.description: Carbon Robotics is a Seattle-based physical-AI and agricultural robotics company building autonomous systems that help farmers cut costs and reduce chemical use. Its flagship LaserWeeder G2 uses computer vision and high-power lasers to eliminate weeds without herbicides, and its Carbon Autonomy product adds remote-supervised autonomy to compatible John Deere tractors. The underlying Carbon AI Large Plant Model is trained on 150 million labeled plants across 15 countries and 100+ crops. Carbon Robotics operates a customer grower cloud portal and Starlink-connected fleet control, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or developer portal as of this profiling.

providers.name: Robocurve
providers.description: Robocurve is a San Francisco Public Benefit Corporation (Y Combinator Summer 2026) building open-source tools and independent benchmarks to help society understand what AI and robots can actually do in the physical world. Its flagship framework, Inspect Robots ("the Inspect AI for robotics"), runs any vision-language-action policy on any embodiment against any benchmark with full trace logs and live Rerun visualization, and integrates with ROS, Isaac Lab, and LeRobot. World Evals is its curated catalog of physical-world benchmarks (KitchenBench, DataCenterBench). Everything ships MIT-licensed as Python packages with a command-line interface rather than a hosted REST API.

providers.name: Xpeng
providers.description: XPENG (Xiaopeng Motors) is a Chinese smart electric-vehicle company headquartered in Guangzhou that designs and manufactures smart EVs (G6, G7, G9, P7/P7+, X9, MONA M03) with in-house advanced driver-assistance and in-car software, listed on the NYSE (XPEV) and HKEX (9868). Surfaced as a portfolio company of hongshan and idg-capital. XPENG publishes no public developer API: its open platform (open.xiaopeng.com) is geo-restricted and account-gated, and no public API docs, specs, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: True Anomaly
providers.description: True Anomaly is a defense-technology company building spacecraft, software, and payloads for space superiority. Its products include Jackal, a multirole space-superiority platform positioned as a tactical fighter-interceptor for contested orbital environments, and Mosaic, an autonomy software platform that transforms commander intent into autonomous action. The company serves U.S. government and allied defense customers from facilities in Centennial and Colorado Springs, Colorado; Long Beach, California; and Washington, DC. True Anomaly publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; its only machine-readable public surface is an RFC 9116 security.txt vulnerability-disclosure contact.

providers.name: Bright Machines
providers.description: Bright Machines is a San Francisco-based software-defined manufacturing company founded in 2018 by Amar Hanspal and Lior Susan that builds a full-stack intelligent automation platform for electronics and AI-infrastructure assembly. Its Microfactory pairs modular Bright Robotic Cells with Brightware, a platform operating system that orchestrates hardware, runs a machine-vision "Smart Skills" perception stack, and provides manufacturing-execution services for work orders, material management and real-time production KPIs. Bright Data, the company's data layer, unifies component, process and enterprise-system data through secure APIs and auditable data flows, and Bright Designer turns product CAD into assembly-ready digital twins using NVIDIA Omniverse on Microsoft Azure. The company has raised roughly $279M from Eclipse, BlackRock, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Jabil and others. All platform and data interfaces are delivered to customers under commercial engagement; Bright Machines publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contracts.

providers.name: Coco Robotics
providers.description: Coco Robotics is a Santa Monica, California urban robotics company operating a fleet of zero-emission, remotely-supervised sidewalk delivery robots ("Cocobots") for last-mile food, grocery and retail delivery. Merchants do not integrate with Coco directly: Coco is consumed as a delivery service provider through Uber Eats, DoorDash, Wolt and Olo Dispatch, and the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or webhooks of its own. Its public software surface is limited to a marketing site, a customer order-tracking web app, and a GitHub organization of forked ROS and infrastructure tooling.

providers.name: Detect
providers.description: Detect Technologies is an IIT Madras-incubated industrial AI company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Chennai, India. Its 360-degree Workplace Intelligence Platform, T-Pulse, combines proprietary IoT sensors, drones, robotics and machine vision with industrial AI to deliver automated inspections, predictive maintenance, gas and oil leak detection, structural health monitoring, and real-time workplace safety, operations and security monitoring for enterprises such as Shell, Vedanta, Adani Group and Hindustan Zinc. Backed by Accel and Elevation Capital. The company does not publish a public API or developer program; this profile captures its public identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Kodiak AI
providers.description: Kodiak AI, Inc. (formerly Kodiak Robotics) is a Mountain View, California company building the Kodiak Driver, an AI-powered ground autonomy system for driverless trucking and defense vehicles. Founded in April 2018 by Don Burnette, Kodiak develops a purpose-built autonomous driving stack — sensor pods, 4D radar, sparse maps, and fallback systems — that integrates into third-party driving platforms rather than shipping a vehicle of its own. The company runs commercial driverless freight lanes in Texas, Oklahoma, Ohio and Indiana with partners including Atlas Energy Solutions, Maersk, Martin Brower, Roehl Transport, JB Hunt and Werner, and it adapts the same driver to defense and industrial missions with General Dynamics Land Systems, Textron Systems and the US Army. Kodiak raised a $125M Series B in 2021 with Lightspeed Venture Partners, Battery Ventures, CRV, SIP Global Partners and others participating, and became a public company through a business combination with Ares Acquisition Corporation II. Kodiak publishes a corporate web presence, a news/RSS feed and an llms.txt for agents, but does not currently operate a public developer program, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Merlin Labs
providers.description: Merlin (Merlin Labs, Inc., NASDAQ: MRLN) is a Boston-headquartered aerospace and defense company founded in 2018 that builds takeoff-to-touchdown flight autonomy for legacy and next-generation aircraft. Its product is the Merlin Pilot, an aircraft-agnostic, AI-powered autonomy stack that pairs machine-learning mission planning with deterministic, hardcoded fallback flight systems, and that has flown hundreds of autonomous flights from test facilities in Kerikeri (New Zealand), Quonset Point (Rhode Island) and Bedford/Hanscom (Massachusetts). Merlin is a prime contractor to USSOCOM for C-130J autonomy, works with the U.S. Air Force on KC-135 tanker autonomy, and collaborates with Northrop Grumman, Honeywell, GE Aerospace and Israel Aerospace Industries. The company holds a New Zealand Part 146 aircraft design organization designation and reached Stage of Involvement 3 (SOI 3) with the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand in August 2026. Merlin became publicly traded in March 2026 through a business combination with Inflection Point Acquisition Corp IV. Merlin sells embedded flight-autonomy software to aircraft OEMs, primes and government programs; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Miso Robotics
providers.description: Miso Robotics is a Pasadena, California kitchen-automation company that builds AI-powered robotics and restaurant operations software for commercial food service. Its flagship product, Flippy, is an autonomous fry station that uses computer vision and NVIDIA-accelerated motion planning to identify food items, detect doneness and run up to 100 baskets per hour on existing commercial fryers from Frymaster, Henny Penny and Pitco. Miso also ships Zippy (built on the acquired Zignyl platform), a real-time digital shift manager for forecasting, scheduling, task management, incentives and payroll that connects to restaurant point-of-sale systems. Customers include White Castle, Jack in the Box, CaliBurger and Auntie Anne's. Miso publishes no public developer API, no OpenAPI/AsyncAPI contract and no SDKs; its integrations are delivered as private partner connections (Toast, PAR and other POS vendors) arranged through sales, and its public GitHub organization carries ROS/robotics and cloud-infrastructure forks used internally rather than a client-facing API surface.

providers.name: Skyryse
providers.description: Skyryse is an El Segundo, California aviation technology company founded in 2016 by Mark Groden and Mitch Adler that builds SkyOS, a universal operating system for flight. SkyOS is a retrofittable hardware and software stack that replaces complex mechanical flight controls with a triply redundant, software-driven system, letting a pilot fly an airplane or helicopter with a single control stick and touchscreens. The platform delivers simplified flight controls, inherent stability, automated maneuvers, emergency autorotation, automated zero-visibility landing, envelope protection, and optionally piloted capability. Skyryse also produces Skyryse One, a SkyOS-powered production helicopter, and Skylar, a universal AI flight assistant. Customers and partners span the U.S. military, law enforcement, Cal Fire, emergency medical services, disaster response, and private operators. In February 2026 the company raised over $300 million in Series C funding at a $1.15 billion post-money valuation, co-led by Autopilot and Fidelity Investments. Skyryse operates as a certified-avionics and aircraft manufacturer and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Verve Motion
providers.description: Verve Motion is a wearable robotics company spun out of the Harvard Biodesign Lab that builds SafeLift, a soft powered exosuit for industrial workers who lift repetitively. Inertial sensors woven into the suit detect lifting motion and trigger assistive force that the company says takes up to 40% of the strain off a worker's back, while Verve Logic — its cloud platform — collects the resulting movement data and reports ergonomic risk, unsafe-posture trends and exosuit utilization to safety managers. SafeLift is sold as a subscription bundling the exosuit, the Verve Logic data portal and Verve Care support, and is distributed in part through partners such as HexArmor. Verve Motion publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the Verve Logic portal at logic.vervemotion.com is a customer-only single-page application that disallows crawling in robots.txt.

providers.name: Botrista
providers.description: Botrista, Inc. is a San Francisco based beverage-automation company founded in 2017 that builds the DrinkBot robotic beverage dispenser and the CloudBar cloud platform behind it. The DrinkBot automates craft beverages — infused teas, flavored lemonades, iced coffees and mocktails — dispensing a drink in roughly twenty seconds from a touchscreen order, and every unit is internet connected so it pulls recipes, reports consumption, tracks ingredient levels and pushes maintenance alerts back to Botrista. CloudBar is the operator-facing web application used by restaurant, campus dining, convenience and theme-park operators to manage recipes, inventory replenishment and sales/menu performance analytics across a fleet of machines, alongside a separate Botrista Data Portal. Botrista sells beverage automation as a service rather than as a developer platform: as of this profiling pass it publishes no public developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract, and POS integrations are handled case-by-case through its commercial team.

providers.name: Fetch Robotics
providers.description: Fetch Robotics is a provider of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for the manufacturing, distribution, and fulfillment industries, enabling customers to optimize warehouse and material-handling workflows through robotic automation. Its Fetch and Freight robots are programmed through a ROS (Robot Operating System) interface — standard ROS topics, services, and actions conforming to ROS Enhancement Proposals (REPs) — rather than an HTTP/REST API, and the first-party client, driver, and simulation libraries are published as open source in the fetchrobotics GitHub organization. Fetch Robotics was acquired by Zebra Technologies in August 2021 for approximately $290M; fetchrobotics.com now redirects to Zebra and the autonomous-mobile-robot product line is being wound down (2025-2026), though the open-source ROS packages remain available.

providers.name: Juxta
providers.description: Juxta is a San Francisco positioning-technology company building a hardware-free Universal Positioning System (UPS) that delivers real-time indoor and outdoor tracking for people, assets, and robots with sub-meter accuracy indoors and roughly 3-meter accuracy outdoors. Rather than relying on satellites, beacons, or cameras, Juxta uses the inertial (IMU) sensors already present in mobile devices, robots, and machinery combined with machine-learning "synthetic fingerprinting" to map and track subjects in GPS-denied environments such as warehouses, hospitals, underground facilities, and battlefields. Its drag-and-drop deployment ingests a floorplan, satellite image, or CAD file and goes live in hours, priced by mapped area and assets tracked. Juxta serves defense, logistics and robotics, and healthcare, and is backed by Y Combinator and other early-stage investors. Access today is through a partner portal and booked demo; no public developer API is documented.

providers.name: Modular Robotics
providers.description: Modular Robotics is a Boulder, Colorado hardware and educational-robotics company best known for Cubelets, magnetic modular robot construction blocks organized into SENSE, THINK, and ACT categories, and the MOSS building system. It also produces the Dexter Industries STEM product line, including the GoPiGo Raspberry Pi robot, BrickPi (LEGO Mindstorms plus Raspberry Pi), GrovePi, and the micro:bit GiggleBot. The company sells physical robotics kits and companion apps such as the browser-based Cubelets Console with Blockly and C coding rather than a public HTTP API; programmatic access is provided through first-party open-source Python driver libraries published on PyPI and maintained under the official DexterInd GitHub organization.

providers.name: Sanctuary AI
providers.description: Sanctuary AI is a Vancouver, British Columbia humanoid robotics company on a mission to create and deploy industrial-grade general-purpose humanoid robots to help address growing labor challenges. Its flagship product is Phoenix, a bipedal humanoid robot designed for dull, dirty, and dangerous work in automotive, manufacturing, and logistics environments. Phoenix is driven by Carbon, Sanctuary AI's proprietary AI control system that mimics human cognitive subsystems — memory, sight, sound, and touch — to translate natural-language tasks into dexterous physical actions. The company is vertically integrated, designing everything from motors and actuators through to generative AI algorithms in-house. Co-founded by James Wells (CEO) and Olivia Norton (CTO/CPO), Sanctuary AI has a private GitHub organization with no public repositories, no developer portal, no public API, no SDK, and no published OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specifications. The commercial model is hardware sales and enterprise deployments; Carbon is a proprietary on-board system and there is no public developer surface.

providers.name: Arrive AI
providers.description: Arrive AI (Nasdaq: ARAI) is an autonomous last-mile delivery company headquartered in Fishers, Indiana, founded by Dan O'Toole and originally operating as DroneDek. Its patented Autonomous Last Mile (ALM) platform is anchored by the Arrive Point, an AI-powered smart mailbox that accepts and dispatches parcels to and from drones, ground robots and human couriers, with temperature-controlled compartments, real-time tracking, smart logistics alerts and chain-of-custody controls aimed at healthcare, pharmacy and e-commerce logistics. The company markets hardware plus a network service; as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Capstan Medical
providers.description: Capstan Medical is a Santa Cruz, California medical device company founded in 2020 out of the Occam Labs incubator by Dan Wallace, with Maggie Nixon as CEO. The company is developing a surgical robotics platform for structural heart disease, merging robotic catheter navigation with next-generation transcatheter mitral and tricuspid valve implants so heart valves can be repaired or replaced without open heart surgery. In 2025 Capstan completed what it describes as the world's first robotic catheter mitral valve replacements in humans, and it raised a $110M Series C led by Eclipse with participation from Intuitive Ventures and Yu Galaxy, bringing total funding past $150M ahead of a second-generation system planned for 2026. Capstan is pre-commercial and regulated medical device focused: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API contracts.

providers.name: Segway-Ninebot
providers.description: Segway-Ninebot is a global personal-transportation and robotics company, formed when Ninebot acquired Segway in 2015. It designs and manufactures electric kickscooters (the world's top-selling e-kickscooter brand, 13M+ units sold across 100+ countries), self-balancing personal transporters, e-bikes, and — through its Robotics division — RMP mobile-robot chassis and delivery/service robots (Nova Carter, NVIDIA Isaac-powered developer kits). Backed by HongShan. Its public developer surface is limited to Segway Robotics' open-source ROS / NVIDIA Isaac integration packages on GitHub; no first-party REST or OpenAPI product API is currently published.

providers.name: ARX Robotics
providers.description: ARX Robotics is a European defense technology company building autonomous unmanned ground systems and the software that runs them. Its flagship Mithra OS is an AI-driven autonomy platform that turns legacy and modern military vehicles into software-defined, autonomous units, while its Gereon RCS line delivers scalable robotic ground vehicles for reconnaissance, firepower, clearance, surveillance, cargo, and casualty evacuation across defense and commercial missions. Headquartered in Munich with offices in Berlin, the UK, and Ukraine, ARX operates one of Europe's largest autonomous defense systems production facilities and has delivered unmanned ground systems to Ukraine. The company is venture-backed (a €31M Series A extended by €11M, with HV Capital among its investors) and partners with RENK, DEUTZ, Helsing, and Quantum Systems to strengthen Europe's technological resilience and defense sovereignty. ARX publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web presence and an llms.txt it publishes for AI agents.

providers.name: Atalanta
providers.description: Atalanta is a mathematical AI company building provably correct decision-making for the world's most important missions. Its flagship platform, Argo, is described as the first software understanding platform - it uses mathematical proof and formal verification to establish safety, security, and performance guarantees for software-defined and autonomous systems at operational speed, moving beyond the limits of traditional testing. Argo identifies failure modes before deployment and verifies compliance with critical constraints across energy (nuclear and grid control systems), space (satellite and communications networks), and defense (complex military systems and data isolation). Atalanta was founded by Anjana Rajan and Jonathan Ring, is headquartered in Washington, D.C., and is backed by Felicis and In-Q-Tel.

providers.name: Berkshire Grey
providers.description: Berkshire Grey is a Bedford, Massachusetts-based AI and robotics company that builds integrated pick-and-place, parcel sortation, trailer-unloading, and shuttle-sortation systems for eCommerce fulfillment, retail replenishment, and parcel logistics operations. Its product portfolio is organized around four flagship robotic systems — Core robotic picking system, Dispatch parcel sorter, Scoop trailer unloader, and Stride shuttle sorter — supported by the BG Flex mobile robotic platform and a centralized operating environment that orchestrates fleets of industrial-grade mobile robots for induct, transport, sort, sequence, and fulfill workflows including buy-online-pickup-in-store, curbside, and store replenishment. The company holds 700+ awarded patents (300+ pending) and has deployed solutions with Global-100 retailers and logistics service providers including Walmart, Target, and FedEx, with FedEx expanding from small-parcel sortation into broader AI robotic package-handling capabilities. Berkshire Grey originally went public via SPAC merger with Revolution Acceleration Acquisition Corp in 2021, then entered into a definitive merger agreement with SoftBank Group in 2023 (approximately $375M / $1.40 per share) and is now operated as a private SoftBank portfolio company. Integration with warehouse-management systems is delivered through a proprietary RESTful API surfaced via professional services and a 24/7 remote monitoring and predictive-maintenance support model; the API, BG-OS platform, and any associated SDKs are not publicly documented, and Berkshire Grey does not operate a public developer portal, downloadable SDK, or open-source release for its robotic operating environment.

providers.name: Edge Case Research
providers.description: Edge Case Research (operating as "Edge Case", ecr.ai) is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania company founded in 2013 that provides functional safety engineering, risk management and safety-assurance software for autonomous and other "frontier technology" systems. Its DevSafeOps methodology carries safety through the whole product lifecycle — hazard identification in design, verified safety evidence in build, and continuous safety monitoring in operations — and its nLoop live-safety-case platform assembles evidence from design, simulation, test and field operations into an auditable, continuously updated safety case. The company works across aerospace and defense, automotive and autonomous trucking, space, oil and gas, and supply chain and logistics, and publishes the Open Autonomy Safety Case framework as SACM XML on GitHub. Edge Case publishes no public product API or OpenAPI; the only machine-readable surface reachable on its own host is the Wix-provided site MCP endpoint advertised in its llms.txt.

providers.name: Field AI
providers.description: FieldAI builds general-purpose robot intelligence through its Field Foundation Models (FFMs) and EDGE brain — a new class of physics-first, risk-aware foundation models for embodied AI. FieldAI's embodiment-agnostic autonomy lets robots navigate dynamic, unstructured environments without maps, GPS, or predefined trajectories, and has been proven across quadrupeds, humanoids, wheeled robots, and passenger-scale vehicles. Founded in 2023 (formerly AI for Humanity) and based in Mission Viejo, California, the company is led by veterans from DeepMind, Google Brain, Tesla Autopilot, NASA JPL, and SpaceX, and serves construction, energy, mining, logistics, manufacturing, power and utility, agriculture, and federal applications. FieldAI has raised over $405M from investors including Bezos Expeditions, Canaan Partners, Khosla Ventures, Temasek, Intel Capital, Hyundai Motor Company, and Prysm Capital.

providers.name: TRIDITIVE
providers.description: TRIDITIVE is an automated additive manufacturing company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Meres, Asturias, Spain, with offices in Hartford, Connecticut and London. It builds the AMCELL family of automated industrial 3D printing machines (Amcell 1300, 4300, 8300, Bulkam), the Traced traceability system, and the EVAM Software platform for additive manufacturing workflow management, digital warehousing, and on-demand production of polymer and metal parts. A Techstars portfolio company, TRIDITIVE publishes no public API, developer portal, or client SDKs as of July 2026.

providers.name: Aante
providers.description: Aante (爱安特) is a Chinese factory-automation (FA) parts distributor and one-stop industrial e-commerce procurement platform, operated by Aante (Changzhou) Precision Machinery Co., Ltd. (爱安特（常州）精密机械有限公司) and headquartered in Changzhou, Jiangsu. Established in 2002 as the successor to Sandi Automation, it sells linear motion, transmission, standard, machined, framing, motion-unit, electrical and pneumatic components across 96 product categories and roughly two million SKUs, distributing 30+ international brands including SMC and THK alongside its own Aante-branded line. It serves customers in semiconductors, new energy, 3C electronics, photovoltaics, LCD, automotive, medical and food manufacturing from three production bases and 30+ service centers, and in 2026 acquired software firm Zhuiguang Geometry to pair components with design software. The storefront at ant-fa.com is a Chinese-language Nuxt commerce site; no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract is published.

providers.name: Hippo Harvest
providers.description: Hippo Harvest is a controlled-environment agriculture company based in Pescadero, California, founded in 2019, that grows USDA-certified-organic leafy greens in modular greenhouses run by custom autonomous mobile robots and machine learning. Its closed-loop, direct-to-root watering and nutrient system is published by the company as using 92% less water, 55% less fertilizer and 94% less land than conventional field agriculture, while pricing to compete with field-grown product. Hippo Harvest sells packaged salad greens (spring mix, spinach, 50/50 blend, butter lettuce) into grocery retail rather than selling software: the robotics, computer vision and growing-control stack is internal operating infrastructure, not a product. It raised a $21M Series B led by Standard Investments in February 2024 and a $30M Series C led by Cox Farms in July 2026, and is permitting a 30-acre facility in Hollister, California. No public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind was found on any host the company controls.

providers.name: Intrinsic
providers.description: Intrinsic is a Mountain View, California industrial robotics software company spun out of Alphabet's X "moonshot factory" and led by CEO Wendy Tan White. Its mission is to make industrial robots radically easier to program, use, and innovate with so that automation is accessible to a much broader range of businesses. Intrinsic's flagship product is Intrinsic Flowstate, an all-in-one web-based developer environment for designing, building, simulating, and deploying production-grade robotics solutions, paired with Intrinsic Intelligence — a portfolio of AI-powered capabilities including pose estimation, motion planning, grasp planning, and sensor-guided control — and IntrinsicOS, a robot operating system that spans cloud to edge. Developers extend Flowstate by writing Skills and Services in Python and C++ via the open-source Intrinsic SDK (Apache-2.0), or compose them visually via behavior trees in the Flowstate Process Editor. The platform integrates deeply with ROS through Intrinsic's 2022 acquisition of Open Source Robotics Corporation (OSRC) — the commercial arm of Open Robotics — while ROS, Gazebo, and Open-RMF stewardship remain with the independent OSRF non-profit. Flowstate is currently in a gated beta / trusted-tester program; production access is granted to enterprise customers, systems integrators, and participants in programs such as the AI for Industry Challenge. Pricing is not publicly disclosed and there is no self-service developer signup.

providers.name: Photoneo
providers.description: Photoneo is a Slovak (Bratislava, founded 2013) machine-vision company and a global pioneer of high-resolution structured-light 3D measurement. Its flagship products are the PhoXi 3D Scanner family and the MotionCam-3D, a parallel structured-light camera that captures moving scenes in real-time 3D, together with AI-enabled software such as Bin Picking Studio, Locator, and Palletizing for robotic automation. Rather than a hosted web/REST API, Photoneo exposes a developer surface through the PhoXi Control software and its official C++, C#, and Python device APIs, GenICam/GigE Vision standard connectivity, TCP/IP robot interfaces (UR, ABB, FANUC, Staubli, Mitsubishi, Kawasaki, Yaskawa), and a set of BSD-licensed example repositories on GitHub. Documentation lives in the Photoneo Knowledge Base (docs.photoneo.com) and the 3D scanning wiki. Photoneo (now part of the Brightpick Group) was acquired by Zebra Technologies.

providers.name: Agile Medical
providers.description: Agile Medical — 敏捷医疗科技（苏州）有限公司, trading under the AGIBOT brand — is a Chinese surgical robotics manufacturer founded in September 2020 and headquartered in Suzhou, Jiangsu, with R&D offices in the Suzhou Industrial Park Dushu Lake innovation district and Shanghai Zhangjiang. Its flagship AGIBOT endoscopic (laparoscopic) surgical robot system pairs a surgeon console, an eight-degree-of-freedom patient-side platform and an imaging processing platform that ingests third-party ultrasound, CT and endoscopic sources. The system received NMPA Class III medical device approval in March 2025 and is in clinical use for minimally invasive urology, gynecology, general, hepatobiliary and thoracic procedures. The company closed a several-hundred-million-RMB Series B in October 2025. It sells regulated capital equipment to hospitals and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Clarapath
providers.description: Clarapath is a medical robotics company headquartered in Hawthorne, New York that automates the tissue sectioning step of the clinical histopathology workflow. Its FDA-registered SectionStar platform pairs patented tape-transfer sectioning with precision robotics, integrated optics and sensors, and computational quality control to turn paraffin blocks into standardized slides with quantitative quality metrics. The company also ships the TrimStar Pro trimming system, a HistoStation data repository for sample and image traceability, remote Telehistology operation, and histology consulting services for hospital, reference, and veterinary laboratories.

providers.name: Cobalt AI
providers.description: Cobalt AI (formerly Cobalt Robotics) is a San Francisco based physical security automation company whose Cobalt Monitoring Intelligence platform uses AI handlers to investigate security events across access control systems and video feeds, determine root cause, and trigger automated responses so security teams focus on genuine threats instead of alarm triage. Its offerings include the Cobalt Command Center remote monitoring service and an indoor autonomous security robot, with integrations spanning LenelS2, Genetec, Avigilon, Brivo, Eagle Eye Networks, Milestone, Okta, ServiceNow, Salesforce, and Slack. The company was founded in 2016, backed early by Bloomberg Beta and Sequoia, and acquired in 2024 by Dean Drako, who rebranded it to Cobalt AI.

providers.name: Whill
providers.description: WHILL, Inc. designs and manufactures enhanced personal mobility solutions — electric power chairs and mobility scooters, including the Model C2, Model F, the Modo Breeze ultralight foldable wheelchair, and the Model R three- and four-wheel scooters — and operates an autonomous personal mobility service that has completed over 700,000 rides worldwide across airports and other venues. WHILL was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this writing it is a consumer hardware and mobility-service company and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile is maintained as a company record and will be enriched if WHILL launches a developer program.

providers.name: Cornerstone Robotics
providers.description: Cornerstone Robotics (CSR) is a Hong Kong-headquartered surgical robotics manufacturer founded in 2019 at Hong Kong Science Park, building the Sentire Endoscopic Surgical System (C1000) — a multi-specialty, minimally invasive robot-assisted surgery platform developed entirely in-house and indicated for general surgery, gynecology, thoracic and urology. The Sentire system has received regulatory clearance in China (NMPA), the European Union and Singapore, and has completed multicenter clinical trials in China and the United Kingdom. The company operates three global R&D hubs, six business centers and a 30,000 square meter manufacturing facility, and sells a regulated physical medical device rather than software: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, no SDKs and no machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: RightHand Robotics
providers.description: RightHand Robotics builds autonomous piece-picking robotic systems for order fulfillment. Its RightPick platform combines computer vision, machine learning, and adaptive grasping hardware to pick and place millions of SKUs at cycle times as fast as three seconds across e-commerce, pharmaceutical, apparel, health & beauty, and grocery operations. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of GV, Menlo Ventures, and SoftBank Vision Fund. RightHand Robotics does not publish a public web API; integration, deployment, and operator documentation is provided to authorized customers and partners through a login-gated partner portal (rhrdocs.com). The public GitHub organization hosts open-source ROS packages and C control libraries for the earlier ReFlex robotic hand hardware rather than web-API client SDKs.

providers.name: Unspun
providers.description: Unspun is a fashion-technology company building Vega, the world's first 3D weaving machines, which transform yarn directly into finished woven garments in about twenty minutes for automated, localized, on-demand apparel manufacturing. Founded by Beth Esponnette, Walden Lam, and Kevin Martin and operating from Oakland, California and Hong Kong, the company pairs its weaving hardware with software for custom-fit patternmaking and design automation, working with manufacturers and brands to eliminate overproduction, with a mission of reducing global human carbon emissions by one percent. Unspun is backed by DCVC and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Agile Robots
providers.description: Agile Robots SE is a Munich-based robotics and artificial intelligence company founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center (DLR) Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics. The company develops force-sensitive industrial and service robots, robotic arms (Diana series), grippers and hands (Agile Hand), mobile robotics, and the AgileCore / AgileAI software platform that lets system integrators and operators build and deploy AI-driven automation for the automotive, consumer electronics, healthcare, and service industries. Headquartered in Munich's Sendling district with manufacturing across Europe, China, and India, Agile Robots reached unicorn valuation in a 2021 Series C and is backed by investors including Hongshan (Sequoia Capital China). This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Agile Robots does not currently publish a public developer portal, REST API, or first-party SDKs.

providers.name: Elroy Air
providers.description: Elroy Air develops autonomous vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) cargo aircraft for defense, commercial, and rapid-response logistics. Its flagship Chaparral is a hybrid-electric aircraft designed to carry up to 300 pounds of cargo across roughly 300 miles with no crew onboard, taking off and landing vertically and cruising autonomously between points. Founded in 2016 and based in San Francisco, the company works with partners including FedEx, NASA, the U.S. Air Force, and Lockheed Martin, and was selected for the U.S. Department of Transportation eVTOL Integration Pilot Program. Elroy Air is a hardware and autonomy company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with identity and domain-security data.

providers.name: Lightberry
providers.description: Lightberry is a San Francisco robotics software company (Y Combinator Fall 2025) that builds conversational AI "personality" software for humanoid and quadruped robots. Its platform lets a robot listen, speak, see its surroundings, and act on natural-language instruction without the owner writing any code, emphasizing emotional intelligence, contextual awareness, and autonomy rather than a simple speech-to-text voice pipeline. Lightberry ships pre-installed on robots sold through its partnership with Unitree, and the company runs a manufacturer-compatibility program with robot makers including Fourier, Booster Robotics, and High Torque. Its published documentation today covers device setup (power-on, WiFi provisioning, starting a conversation) plus an MCP architecture note describing a Model Context Protocol server that routes tool calls to individual Lightberry devices, which each expose a REST endpoint. There is no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or OpenAPI definition at this time.

providers.name: Plus One Robotics
providers.description: Plus One Robotics is a San Antonio, Texas warehouse-automation company founded in 2016 by Erik Nieves and Shaun Edwards that builds AI-powered computer-vision software and robotic work cells for parcel handling, depalletizing, palletizing and induction. Its PickOne perception system tells a robot arm how to grasp each item and verifies placement, while Yonder provides supervised autonomy — remote human "Crew Chiefs" who take over when the robot hits an exception. Packaged work cells DepalOne and InductOne wrap that stack in deployable hardware. The company reports more than 1.5 billion lifetime picks across robots fielded in 15 countries, with additional offices in Eindhoven (Netherlands) and Boulder, Colorado. Plus One Robotics publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; product integration is handled through its partner channel and a login-gated partner portal.

providers.name: Starship Technologies
providers.description: Starship Technologies is an autonomous last-mile delivery company that operates a global fleet of self-driving, sidewalk-going delivery robots. Founded in 2014 by Skype co-founders Ahti Heinla and Janus Friis, the company runs commercial robot delivery on university campuses, in residential neighborhoods, on industrial sites and for grocery and restaurant partners across the United States, the United Kingdom, Estonia, Finland, Germany and Denmark, and has completed more than 10 million autonomous deliveries. Its commercial product, Delivery by Starship, is a delivery-as-a-service offering that partners integrate into their own ordering apps: Starship states that its APIs let a partner create delivery jobs, load robots, obtain status updates and handle delivery cancellations, backed by a developer toolkit, documentation, ready-made components and support. That developer surface is not published to the open web — Starship provides it to partners after a commercial conversation via business@starship.co, so no public specification, reference or portal exists to profile.

providers.name: TurbineOne
providers.description: TurbineOne builds a frontline AI/ML platform that turns raw sensor data into real-time detection, classification, and targeting at the edge for defense and national-security missions. Its product suite spans Frontline Perception (edge computer vision on live sensor feeds), Frontline Command, Frontline Autonomy, a Model Hub for managing and deploying ML models, and EdgeWorks, a program that brings warfighters, mission teams, and engineers together to develop and validate mission capabilities for contested, disconnected environments. The company was founded on expertise in artificial intelligence, mesh networking, and sensing technology, and positions its work as "Responsible AI for our nation's heroes." It is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. TurbineOne publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its public identity, GitHub organization, and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Verdant Robotics
providers.description: Verdant Robotics is an agricultural robotics company building precision farming systems for specialty crop growers. Its flagship SharpShooter uses "Aim & Apply" technology - machine learning and computer vision that identify crops and weeds in real time, build a three-dimensional map of the field, and deliver microliter-precise applications directly onto weeds without contacting the crop, doing over 240 targeted applications per second. The Robotics-as-a- Service platform reduces herbicide use by up to 99% and manual labor costs by up to 85% across carrots, leafy greens, cabbage, onions, and grass seed and sod production. Founded by leaders from the self-driving vehicle industry and commercial agriculture, Verdant is backed by DCVC. This profile was surfaced as a DCVC portfolio company; Verdant publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation - its GitHub organization hosts robotics tooling and forks (cbuf message serialization, Jetson build scripts, YOLO/ultralytics forks) rather than a product API.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Hexagon Manufacturing Intelligence
providers.description: Hexagon Manufacturing Intelligence is a division of Hexagon AB providing metrology, quality management, and manufacturing intelligence software and hardware. Products include PC-DMIS (CMM measurement software), WORKXPLORE (CAD viewer), SFx (smart factory platform), and HxGN Smart Quality. The division offers APIs and SDKs for automating CMM measurement programs, integrating quality data into MES and ERP systems, and building custom metrology applications.

providers.name: Jaipur Robotics
providers.description: Jaipur Robotics is a Manno, Switzerland based deep-tech company building advanced computer vision and deep learning solutions for the waste-to-energy sector. Its product, Jaipur Intelligence, applies patent-pending image recognition to plant bunkers and truck unloading bays to detect oversized and dangerous items, map the calorific value (LHV) of incoming waste in real time, and track crane operations — helping operators cut emissions, improve waste mixing and combustion stability, and minimize unplanned shutdowns. The company operates a gated customer application at app.jaipurrobotics.com and is backed by Techstars, Innosuisse, Venture Kick, CSEM and others. It currently publishes a marketing site and a customer login only; there is no public developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable API specification.

providers.name: Prenav
providers.description: PRENAV, Inc. is a Belmont, California company that automates the visual inspection of large civil and industrial structures using commercially available drones, photogrammetry and deep learning. Its PRENAV.XYZ web platform stitches thousands of drone photographs into a high-resolution 3D point-cloud digital twin, then runs machine-learning models over that twin to detect cracking in concrete, spalling, exposed rebar, cracks in steel and rust, resolving features under 0.2mm and tracking change over time. A second line, Synthetic Imagery as a Service, procedurally renders thousands of annotated photoreal defect images each month to augment a customer's own AI training sets. PRENAV publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API description; the product is sold as an enterprise service through a contact form.

providers.name: Applied EV
providers.description: Applied EV (formerly AEV Robotics, legal entity Applied Electric Vehicles Ltd) is an Australian software-defined vehicle company founded in Melbourne in 2015 by Julian Broadbent and Shane Ambry. It builds the Blanc Robot, a cabinless autonomous-ready electric platform for logistics, industrial, mining and agricultural transport; the Digital Backbone, a safety-rated ASIL-D programmable vehicle control system; and an Internet-of-Vehicles (IoV) Cloud Platform the company markets as API-first. The IoV platform is advertised as a set of vehicle APIs — Access Manager for identity and access management, a Vehicle Task API, a Vehicle Mission API, a Drive API for autonomous driving and motion control, a Pod and Accessory API, and Virtual Vehicles for simulation — together with a Vehicle Management System for fleet telemetry, diagnostics, mapping, mission creation and over-the-air software updates. No public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract is served: the developer host resolves but refuses public connections, and the marketing pages route every developer path to an enquiry form.

providers.name: Freedom Robotics
providers.description: Freedom Robotics is a San Francisco-based robotics infrastructure company founded in 2017 that builds mission-critical software to help robotics companies build, operate, support, and scale heterogeneous robot fleets. Its cloud platform — sometimes referred to as Mission Control — provides device and fleet management, remote teleoperation (Pilot), live data streaming, smart alerts and notifications, fleet maps and heatmaps, deployment and service management, remote development, and analytics across cobots, industrial robots, AMRs, drones, and custom hardware. The platform is robot- and OS-agnostic, installs on a device in seconds via a single-line Freedom Agent installer, and integrates with ROS, ROS 2, Python, microcontrollers, Protobuf, Docker, and the cloud offerings of AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. Freedom exposes a public REST API at api.freedomrobotics.ai covering accounts, devices, alerts, statistics, uploads, tokens, users, user groups, and zones, plus a Python SDK (freedomrobotics.link) with Link, MicroLink, message, log, image, and command-callback primitives for programmatic control and telemetry of large numbers of robots. The company has raised approximately $17M in venture funding and operates on a per-robot subscription model (publicly cited at roughly $300 per robot per month) with custom enterprise plans negotiated through sales.

providers.name: Hadrian
providers.description: Hadrian (Hadrian Automation) is a Los Angeles-area precision-manufacturing company founded in 2020 by Chris Power, building software-driven, AI-powered factories that produce high-tolerance machined components for the aerospace and defense industrial base — including parts for rockets, satellites, jets, drones, and missiles. The company's core software stack is Opus, described as a full-stack, AI-powered Factory Autonomy platform that interprets legacy engineering designs, automates CNC machining, inspection, tool-path optimization, adaptive programming, scheduling, and quality assurance, and enables new operators to be productive in 30 days or less. Hadrian operates multiple factories — Factory 2 (F2) and Factory X (FX) in Torrance, California, and Factory 3 (F3) in Mesa, Arizona — and offers three commercial models: precision component manufacturing, Manufacturing-as-a-Service (dedicated automation cells for a single customer), and Factories-as-a-Service (turnkey factory design and operation). Customers and partners include major aerospace and defense primes such as Lockheed Martin. Hadrian has also launched an additive manufacturing division to expand U.S. defense production capacity. The Opus platform is internal-only — Hadrian sells finished precision parts and factory capacity, not software access — and there is no public developer API, SDK, GitHub organization, or open-source release for Opus or any Hadrian system.

providers.name: SVT Robotics
providers.description: SVT Robotics builds the SOFTBOT Platform, a software integration and orchestration foundation for warehouse automation and the supply chain. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Norfolk, Virginia, the company lets enterprises connect industrial systems, robotics, AMRs, and warehouse management software through standardized, prebuilt SOFTBOT Connectors — reducing integration complexity and enabling real-time visibility, faster automation deployments, and a resilient data backbone for automation and AI. Customers include DHL Supply Chain, Barrett Distribution Centers, and the Hagen Group. The provider operates a developer documentation hub for the SOFTBOT integration API (docs.svtrobotics.com, currently password-protected) and a public status page; no public OpenAPI, SDK, or open API surface was discoverable at enrichment time.

providers.name: Haber
providers.description: Haber (Elixa Technologies Private Limited), headquartered in Pune, India with a US presence in Chicago, is an industrial AI company delivering AI-led automation for smart manufacturing across heavy industries including pulp, paper, packaging and tissue, metals and mining, food and beverages, oil and gas, and water/utility institutions. Its product suite spans eLIXA, an IIoT-powered process intelligence platform; Mt. Fuji for historical data storage, visualizations, digital twins and predictive interventions; Kaiznn, an optimization engine for trim-loss reduction, inventory and production scheduling; plus Kensei and FiMorph. The platform emphasizes real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and enterprise-grade security (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022). Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and enriched into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Agtonomy
providers.description: Agtonomy is a physical-AI and automation software company, founded in 2021 by growers and technologists, that embeds machine vision, connectivity, and AI directly into agricultural and off-road equipment from manufacturers such as Bobcat, Kubota, and Clemens. Its platform combines GPS guidance, computer vision, and fleet intelligence so a single operator can plan, remotely monitor, and review autonomous tasks like mowing, hauling, spraying, and cultivation across 10+ tractors at once. The TeleFarmer product controls these field missions through an intuitive app, helping growers address labor shortages and rising operational costs. Backed by investors including GV and Allison Transmission, Agtonomy operates primarily across the western United States with expansion into the Southeast US and Australia. This profile was surfaced as a GV portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Agtonomy publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Astrobotic
providers.description: Astrobotic Technology is a Pittsburgh-based space robotics company building lunar landers, rovers, and lunar surface infrastructure for NASA and commercial customers. Its product lines include the Peregrine and Griffin lunar landers, the CubeRover and Polaris rover families, LunaGrid lunar surface power, the Xodiac reusable suborbital rocket lander test platform, and spacecraft navigation, machine vision and computing systems. The company sells payload delivery to the Moon under NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program, alongside the consumer MoonBox service. Voyager Technologies completed its acquisition of Astrobotic on 13 July 2026 and the business now operates as Voyager Lunar Systems from its Pittsburgh headquarters. Astrobotic sells missions and hardware, not software: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Bedrock Robotics
providers.description: Bedrock Robotics develops advanced autonomy for the built world, retrofitting existing heavy construction machinery with an autonomous kit the company calls the Bedrock Operator. The system adds machine intelligence to equipment such as excavators and dozers so jobsites can run around the clock with reduced human intervention, compressing project timelines, improving safety by removing operators from hazardous work, and enabling remote progress tracking. Backed by 8vc and Emergence Capital, the company raised a $270M Series B. Bedrock is a robotics and physical-autonomy company; it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time. This profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network and captures its public web and security posture.

providers.name: Blue Water Autonomy
providers.description: Blue Water Autonomy is a Boston-based defense technology company building autonomous warships for open-ocean operations, with the goal of revitalizing U.S. shipbuilding through scalable, reliable, uncrewed naval vessels. Founded in 2025 by Rylan Hamilton (ex-U.S. Navy officer and founder of 6 River Systems), Scott N. Miller (ocean engineer and early iRobot engineer), and Austin Gray (former Navy intelligence officer), the company unveiled its 190-foot Liberty Class autonomous ship platform for the U.S. Navy in February 2026. Backed by a $50M Series A led by GV, Blue Water Autonomy operates from offices in Boston MA, Washington DC, Morgan City LA, and San Diego CA. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Chemify
providers.description: Chemify is a Glasgow-based programmable-chemistry company, spun out of the University of Glasgow in 2022 by chemist Lee Cronin, that digitizes the creation of molecules through what it calls "Chemputation." The platform fuses AI/ML-driven molecular design, a universal chemical programming language, and robotic synthesis so pharmaceutical, biotech, and industrial partners can move from a novel concept to a makeable compound end to end. In 2025 Chemify opened its first Chemifarm, a fully automated chemistry facility in Glasgow's Maryhill district that pairs its molecular-design engine with industrial-scale robotic synthesis, and closed a $50M Series B co-led by Wing Venture Capital and Insight Partners, with backing from DCVC. Chemify does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; engagement runs through its partner program.

providers.name: Conceivable Life Sciences
providers.description: Conceivable Life Sciences is a fertility technology company founded in 2021 that builds AURA, an AI-powered, end-to-end automated in vitro fertilization (IVF) laboratory. AURA combines six integrated robotic workstations, advanced optics, machine vision and AI inference to automate more than 200 manual embryology steps — sperm preparation, oocyte retrieval and denudation, ICSI, dish preparation, embryo culture and vitrification — so that embryologists supervise rather than perform each micromanipulation. The company raised a $50M Series A in September 2025 (bringing total funding to $70M), opened the first automated IVF lab in Mexico City, and has partnered with IVI RMA Global to deploy AURA in a US clinic. Its public surface is a corporate and scientific one — research papers, patents, press and clinical trial registrations — with no developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Forterra
providers.description: Forterra is a defense autonomy company headquartered in Clarksburg, Maryland, that builds combat-proven autonomous mission systems for ground operations in contested, GPS-denied, off-road environments. Founded in 2002 as Robotic Research and rebranded as Forterra, it retrofits existing military and commercial vehicles with self-driving capability through its AutoDrive autonomous driving system, the TerraLink modular vehicle-management and command-and-control platform, and the OASIS open architecture that lets the government and third-party developers add sensors, effectors, and payloads without vendor lock-in. Additional offerings span resilient communications, sensing, and ruggedized edge-compute hardware. The company is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Enlightenment Capital and supplies autonomy to multiple active U.S. Department of Defense programs. Forterra does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or self-service developer portal; its systems are delivered as government and defense-integration programs.

providers.name: Geek+
providers.description: Geek+ (Geekplus, HKEX: 2590) is a global leader in AI-driven autonomous mobile robot (AMR) solutions for warehouse and logistics automation. Founded in 2015, it delivers end-to-end smart-warehouse systems spanning shelf-to-person (PopPick), tote-to-person (RoboShuttle), pallet-to-person (Skycube) storage and retrieval, robot-arm picking, sorting, and intralogistics transport. Its All-in-One Software Suite (Robot Management System, Warehouse Execution System, Intelligent Warehouse Management System, data and simulation platforms) exposes open REST APIs and SDKs so customers and partners can integrate robot fleets with major WMS, ERP, and MES platforms including SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Manhattan Associates, and Blue Yonder. Geek+ serves 3PL, retail, e-commerce, apparel, grocery, healthcare and pharma, manufacturing, automotive, electronics, and cold-chain logistics across 40+ countries, with 950+ deployed warehouses. In 2025 it became the world's first publicly listed AMR warehouse robotics company on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

providers.name: Glydways
providers.description: Glydways is an autonomous urban-transit company building on-demand, high-capacity mobility networks that combine small self-driving electric vehicles (Glydcars), an AI fleet-orchestration layer, and dedicated narrow guideways separated from regular road traffic. The system is designed to move up to 10,000 people per hour while cutting construction cost by roughly 90% and operating cost to about 30% of conventional transit, with launch projects underway in Atlanta, Contra Costa County, California, and at San Jose Airport. Backed by Khosla Ventures, Glydways was surfaced through the venture portfolio and added to the API Evangelist network. As an autonomous-transit infrastructure company it publishes a corporate and news presence but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Iconbuild
providers.description: ICON Technology, Inc. (iconbuild.com) is an Austin, Texas construction technologies company using large-scale robotics, advanced materials, and software to build homes and structures. ICON develops the Vulcan and Phoenix 3D-printing robots, proprietary Lavacrete and CarbonX building materials, and design/build tooling (including its CODEX architectural catalog and ICON Prime), and has printed communities across the US as well as researched off-world construction with NASA (Project Olympus). Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This is a physical construction / building-technology company; as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or /.well-known discovery surface, so no API artifacts were harvested.

providers.name: Nanotronics
providers.description: Nanotronics (rebranded to CubeFabs in 2025) builds AI-driven inspection, process-control, and automation systems for advanced industrial manufacturing, with a focus on semiconductors, data centers, EV/automotive, and aerospace/defense. Its "AI factory" platform combines optical imaging, machine learning, and robotics to improve manufacturing precision, yields, and cost efficiency for customers including Hologic, Broadcom, Coherent, and Standard BioTools. Surfaced as a founders-fund portfolio company; no public developer/API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Niricson Software
providers.description: Niricson Software Inc. is an infrastructure technology company making concrete infrastructure safer through AI-powered digital condition assessment. Its patented AUTOSPEX platform uses machine learning and multi-sensor data fusion (visual, thermal, and acoustic) to automatically detect, quantify, and track defects such as cracks, spalling, delamination, and alkali-aggregate reaction in dams, spillways, bridges, and airfields. Data is collected with its DRONIC architecture and NCX acoustic drone payload, which simulates the traditional concrete hammer-sounding test to identify subsurface delamination up to eight inches deep. Asset owners and civil engineers access results through the login-gated, web-based AUTOSPEX platform to interact with defect maps and compare surveys over time. Niricson operates across the USA, Canada, Australia, and India, and is a Techstars portfolio company. It exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Omnitron Sensors
providers.description: Omnitron Sensors designs advanced MEMS (micro electro mechanical systems) sensors using innovative 3D manufacturing techniques, aiming to deliver high-performance, low-cost sensing with major gains in precision and reliability. Its technology targets AI data centers, autonomous systems and vehicles, environmental and climate monitoring, and extended reality (XR) devices. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network, the company is a hardware/semiconductor business with no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Re:Build
providers.description: Re:Build Manufacturing is a U.S.-based industrial engineering and manufacturing company that takes complex products from concept to full-rate production through integrated design, engineering, and scalable domestic manufacturing. Founded to rebuild American manufacturing capacity, the company operates a family of specialized engineering and production businesses across more than 14 U.S. locations, spanning aerospace and defense, electrification, energy and environment, medical devices, and robotics and automation. With 400+ engineers and roughly one million square feet of industrial footprint, Re:Build partners with startups and established manufacturers to develop, industrialize, and produce advanced physical products. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment confirms it is an industrial/manufacturing company with no public API, developer, or machine surface at this time.

providers.name: Reach
providers.description: Reach Power (Reach Labs) is a Y Combinator-backed (S2015) wireless power company building long-range wireless energy distribution networks, aiming to "do for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented, AI-driven power-beaming systems use adaptive metamaterial antennas to steer electromagnetic waves and deliver electricity through the air to multiple devices simultaneously, scaling from microwatts to kilowatts across both mobile and stationary transmitters. Reach serves defense and intelligence, manufacturing and logistics, and public safety markets, powering autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, sensors, and drones. Partners and customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, NASA, DARPA, the U.S. Army and Air Force, Aisin/Toyota, and Panasonic. The company is headquartered in San Francisco. As of this profile, Reach publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API platform.

providers.name: Recycleye
providers.description: Recycleye is a London-based company building AI-powered sorting equipment and analytics for waste management and material recovery businesses worldwide. Its products include Recycleye QualiBot robotic sorting cells, Recycleye QuantiSort optical sorting technology, and Recycleye Insights, a data analytics platform that uses computer vision (WasteNet) to identify and categorize waste streams. The company sells hardware and software into recycling operations to improve purity, recovery rates, and profitability. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC. As of this enrichment pass Recycleye publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK; this profile captures its identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: Ripcord
providers.description: Ripcord is a document digitization and data-extraction company that uses proprietary robotics and AI to turn paper and digital records into structured, actionable business data. Its pipeline runs in three stages — robotic digitization (scanning paper to high-quality digital files), intelligence (AI classification, extraction, validation and enrichment), and action (accessing the resulting data through existing enterprise systems or Ripcord's Canopy cloud content-management platform). Ripcord serves manufacturing, financial services, insurance, real estate, energy, public sector, HR, food & beverage, and accounts-receivable management, with customers including Coca-Cola Bottlers, BP, UCLA, MUFG Bank, Agilent, and the IRS. Integration with enterprise systems (ERP, ECM, RPA, BI) is offered through direct engagement rather than a public developer API. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of GV and Lux Capital.

providers.name: Robust.AI
providers.description: Robust.AI is a robotics company building Carter, an AI-powered collaborative mobile robot for warehouse fulfillment and manufacturing environments. Founded by Rodney Brooks (co-founder of iRobot and Rethink Robotics) and colleagues, the company designs human-centered autonomous material-handling robots that work alongside people with minimal infrastructure change, no capital expenditure, and rapid ROI. Robust.AI is backed by Playground Global and was recognized among Fast Company's World's Most Innovative Companies of 2026. This is a physical-robotics company; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or GitHub surface.

providers.name: SmartMore
providers.description: SmartMore Corporation (思谋科技) is a Hong Kong- and Shenzhen-headquartered industrial AI and machine vision company founded in 2019, building products and solutions for smart manufacturing and digital innovation. Its flagship SMore ViMo platform bundles ViMo Cloud, ViMo Deeplearning and ViMo Studio into a low-code industrial vision stack covering data management, model training, visual solution design and production-line deployment, and is sold alongside first-party hardware — industrial smart cameras, barcode readers (VS600/VS800P/VS1000/VS2000), vision sensors (VN2000/VN4000) and lenses — through the SmartMoreInside sub-brand. The company also markets digital platforms (Light3D, Data, Gauge, AIoT) and industrial large models (IndustryGPT, SMore LrMo). SmartMore states it has filed 400+ global patent applications with 200+ granted, served 200+ enterprise customers, and reached unicorn status on a Series B that exceeded USD 200 million in 2021, with R&D and business centers in Hong Kong, Shenzhen, Shanghai, Suzhou, Tokyo, Beijing, Hangzhou and Singapore. As of this pass the company publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract; ViMo model export to an SDK is described in marketing copy but is delivered with the licensed product rather than documented publicly.

providers.name: Vita Inclinata
providers.description: Vita Inclinata Technologies is a Colorado-based hardware company that builds physics-based load stabilization systems for helicopter hoists and construction cranes, eliminating the dangerous spin and sway of suspended loads. Its ecosystem spans Vita Aerospace (helicopter and rescue hoist stabilization), Vita Industrial (crane and construction load control), Air Rescue Systems (hoist training and products), and the Vita Rescue System used in military MEDEVAC operations. The company is Techstars-backed.
