It was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network; as a physical-hardware manufacturer it currently publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: Zeitview
providers.description: Zeitview (formerly DroneBase) is an AI-powered aerial inspection and asset intelligence platform. It combines a managed network of drone and aircraft pilots with computer-vision analytics and lifecycle asset-management software to deliver inspection imagery, condition assessments, and actionable intelligence for wind energy, solar, utilities, oil & gas, construction, commercial real estate, and property management. As of this profile the company operates a customer web platform, support center, and blog but does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; data access is arranged through direct customer engagement.

providers.name: ANYbotics
providers.description: ANYbotics is a Swiss deep-tech robotics company that builds ANYmal, an autonomous four-legged inspection robot used to automate routine and hazardous industrial inspections across power and utilities, oil and gas, mining, chemicals, and metals. Its platform pairs the legged robot with inspection-management software and analytics to increase plant uptime, cut costs, and remove workers from dangerous areas. ANYbotics is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. No public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface is exposed; this API Evangelist profile currently captures the company's published security and trust posture.

providers.name: CMR Surgical
providers.description: CMR Surgical is a British medical-device company headquartered in Cambridge, UK, founded in 2014 (as Cambridge Medical Robotics). It develops Versius, a small, modular and portable robot-assisted surgical system used across urology, general, gynaecological and thoracic surgery, and Versius Plus, its next-generation platform cleared by the US FDA in December 2025. More than 45,000 patients have been treated globally, making Versius one of the most widely used soft-tissue robotic surgery platforms. CMR reached unicorn status in 2019 and raised a $600M Series D at a $3B valuation in 2021, backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, GE Healthcare, ABB Technology Ventures and others. Its digital ecosystem (Versius Connect, Versius Team, Versius Clinical Insights) is a login-gated clinical surface; CMR publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs or developer portal.

providers.name: Divergent
providers.description: Divergent Technologies, Inc. is a Torrance and Long Beach, California manufacturer that built the Divergent Adaptive Production System (DAPS), an end-to-end software-hardware production system for industrial digital manufacturing. DAPS pairs AI-driven generative design software with in-house metal additive manufacturing — the Monolith One printer, compatible with aluminum, nickel, steel and titanium alloys — and automated fixtureless robotic assembly, so complex multi-part structures can be engineered, printed and assembled without fixed tooling. Founded in 2013 by Kevin and Lukas Czinger, the company is a Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and has expanded into aerospace and defense, including selection under the US Air Force Eglin Wide Agile Acquisition Contract. Divergent sells manufactured structures and production capacity, not software: it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Dominion Dynamics
providers.description: Dominion Dynamics Inc. is a Canadian defence-technology company (Kanata/Ottawa, Ontario) building the autonomy stack for the Arctic and other extreme, infrastructure-constrained operating environments. It develops integrated autonomy, edge sensing, communications, and command-and-control systems for defence, security, and critical infrastructure. Its AuraNet platform is a peer-to-peer sensor mesh that fuses EO/IR/SAR imagery, SIGINT/EW/RF signals, telemetry, and structured reporting into a unified local intelligence stream that interoperates with existing allied C2 architectures, and its Aurion product is an open-source government procurement intelligence platform built on Canadian federal open data. Founded by Anduril alum Eliot Pence, the company raised a $139M CAD Series A (2026) led by Georgian. This profile currently has no public developer/API surface; the entry captures the company identity, security.txt, and llms.txt the company publishes.

providers.name: Emancro
providers.description: Emancro is an AI robotics company automating hospital logistics. Its flagship product, EASO, is described as the world's first fully autonomous robot for hospital medication logistics: it streamlines supply distribution, restocks medication dispensing cabinets, and retrieves medications from pharmacy storage to reduce errors and free clinical staff to focus on patient care. The technology combines vision-language-action (VLA) models with geometric planning, and Emancro is piloting EASO with leading U.S. hospitals. The company is backed by Amplify Partners. Emancro is a physical-robotics and healthcare-AI company with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Fuchsia
providers.description: Fuchsia is an AI-native hardware certification and compliance platform ("Vanta for hardware") that helps hardware teams get products to market faster by streamlining regulatory testing and certification. The platform maps the applicable standards for a product (FCC, CE, UL, FDA 510(k), ISO, RF & EMC, environmental, and functional-safety categories), auto-generates the lab-ready technical documentation and test plans required for certification, connects teams with qualified testing labs specialized in their product category, and tracks compliance progress to surface blockers early. Fuchsia uses AI agents to manage the compliance workflow end to end — from design through testing and certification — including direct communication with testing labs, aiming to democratize regulatory compliance that has traditionally favored larger companies with dedicated compliance teams. Founded in 2025 and part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, Fuchsia is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and targets robotics, medical-device, IoT, and consumer-hardware builders. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass Fuchsia publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Levita Magnetics
providers.description: Levita Magnetics is a Mountain View, California medical device company, founded by minimally invasive surgeon Dr. Alberto Rodriguez-Navarro and co-founded by Nicolas Luksic, with an additional office in Santiago, Chile. It develops Magnetic Surgery — the Levita Magnetic Surgical System, in which an external magnet placed on the patient's skin controls a shaftless detachable retractor to enable reduced-port laparoscopic procedures — and the MARS (Magnetic-Assisted Robotic Surgery) platform launched in 2023, an FDA-cleared surgical robotic system used in abdominal and, more recently, pediatric procedures. The MARS platform is built on RTI Connext (the DDS real-time connectivity standard) internally, and Levita has demonstrated AI-guided autonomous camera control during surgery. Levita ships regulated surgical hardware and its embedded control software to hospitals; it operates no public developer program, publishes no API documentation, and exposes no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: Noah Medical
providers.description: Noah Medical is a surgical robotics company building the Galaxy System, a robotic-assisted bronchoscopy platform for interventional pulmonology. The system combines advanced imaging, precision targeting, single-use scope technology, and an adaptive workflow to deliver "tool-in-lesion" confidence for diagnosing lung nodules, improving diagnostic yield and workflow efficiency for physicians. Noah Medical is a medical-device manufacturer focused on clinical hardware and does not currently expose a public developer platform, API, or documentation surface; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a healthcare portfolio company backed by Hongshan (HongShan Capital / formerly Sequoia China).

providers.name: REEV
providers.description: REEV is a medical-technology company developing AI-powered wearable robotics for mobility recovery and neurological gait rehabilitation. Its REEV SENSE platform uses smart shoe- and leg-mounted sensors to analyze gait and visualize biomarkers in a mobile app, and its DREEVEN motorized knee-ankle-foot orthosis (KAFO) delivers robotic walking assistance personalized from REEV SENSE gait data. REEV serves outpatient clinics and rehabilitation centers treating stroke, multiple sclerosis, and paraplegia, and is backed by Techstars, NVIDIA Inception, and Bpifrance.

providers.name: Aeterlink Corp.
providers.description: Aeterlink Corp. is a Tokyo-headquartered deep-tech company, originating from Stanford University research, that develops, manufactures and sells spatial (microwave) wireless power transfer systems under the AirPlug brand. AirPlug delivers power to battery-free IoT sensors and devices at distances of roughly 15-20 meters with bidirectional data communication, and is sold into factory automation, building management and medical implant applications. Founded in August 2020, the company operates offices in Tokyo, Indianapolis and Bangkok, and is active in the international standardization of spatial wireless power transfer. Aeterlink publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract; its product materials are distributed by request form.

providers.name: AIM Intelligent Machines
providers.description: AIM (AIM Intelligent Machines) is a Redmond, Washington robotics and artificial-intelligence company building autonomous earthmoving for mining, construction and defense. Its plug-and-play retrofit kit converts existing heavy equipment — excavators, bulldozers, haul trucks — into self-operating machines regardless of make, model, size or age, while preserving the OEM warranty, pairing rugged onboard hardware and 360-degree camera-based perception with a tablet-based control interface and a "Site Intelligence" analytics dashboard for remote fleet tasking, terrain mapping and productivity reporting. Founded in 2021 by engineers from Waymo, SpaceX, Google, Tesla, Apple, Microsoft, Trimble and Hexagon, AIM is backed by General Catalyst (partners Quentin Clark and Max Rimpel), Khosla Ventures, DCVC, Human Capital, Ironspring Ventures and Mantis, and has announced a strategic partnership with Komatsu and a LiDAR partnership with Ouster. AIM sells through equipment dealers rather than a self-serve product, and as of this pass publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind — its entire public web surface is eight marketing and legal pages.

providers.name: Lila Sciences
providers.description: Lila Sciences is an AI company founded in 2023 that is building what it calls Scientific Superintelligence: an autonomous system that runs the scientific method end to end by generating hypotheses, designing experiments, executing them in physical AI Science Factories (autonomous robotic laboratory networks), and learning from the resulting experimental data. Rather than training on internet text, Lila trains a scientific reasoning model on experimental data, coupling it to scalable verifiers and instruments such as molecular dynamics simulators, protein structure predictors, quantum chemistry solvers, and gene editors, then optimizing the policy with reinforcement learning. The company packages this as two commercial offerings: Catalyst, positioned as an operating system for science that accelerates an organization's existing research, and Creation, a partnership model for generating new discoveries, launching products, and founding new companies. Lila works across therapeutics (mRNA, proteins, antibodies, cell therapies, small molecules), advanced materials, chemicals, energy and environment, oil and gas, aerospace and defense, and biotech. It has raised roughly $550M ($200M seed announced March 2025 and a $350M Series A closed in October 2025) from investors including General Catalyst and NVIDIA, at a reported valuation above $1.3B, and collaborates with NVIDIA on the BioNeMo Agent Toolkit. Lila operates from Cambridge MA, San Francisco CA, and London UK. As of this profile Lila publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts; this entry is a company identity record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Oxa
providers.description: Oxa (formerly Oxbotica, rebranded in 2023) is a British autonomous vehicle software company founded in 2014 in Oxford, England by Paul Newman and Ingmar Posner. Oxa builds what it calls Universal Autonomy — self-driving software configurable for almost any vehicle in almost any environment — and sells it as Industrial Mobility Automation for ports, airports, manufacturing yards, solar farms and shuttle networks. Its product line is Oxa Driver (the autonomy stack), Oxa Foundry (a generative-AI training and assurance toolchain, previously marketed as Oxa MetaDriver), Reference Autonomy Designs (modular hardware integration blueprints), and Oxa Hub (a cloud fleet-management suite covering remote assist, task design, workspace mapping, digital twins and in-use monitoring). Oxa Hub is described on the marketing site as offering "an API for optional integration with existing logistics systems", but Oxa publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable specification on any public host. The company raised a $115M Series C in 2023 with participation from Google, and works with Ocado Group, ZF and bp.

providers.name: Reliable Robotics
providers.description: Reliable Robotics is a California-based aerospace company developing continuous autopilot and remote piloting systems that retrofit existing fixed-wing aircraft for automated and remotely supervised flight across all phases (taxi, take-off, cruise, landing). The company has flown automated Cessna 208 Caravan demonstrations including a fully uncrewed take-off and landing in 2023, and is pursuing FAA Part 23 supplemental type certification for its automation system. Reliable Robotics has contracts with the U.S. Air Force AFWERX program and the Defense Innovation Unit to evaluate automated cargo and ISR missions on platforms including the Cessna 208, and has partnered with Textron Aviation on certification work. The company's founders are alumni of SpaceX and Tesla autopilot teams. Reliable Robotics is partner- and government-gated and does not currently offer public consumer or developer APIs.

providers.name: Sealed Air
providers.description: Sealed Air Corporation (SEE) is a global packaging company headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, now privately held following its acquisition by Clayton, Dubilier & Rice. It designs and manufactures food packaging, protective packaging and automated packaging equipment under the Bubble Wrap, Cryovac, AutoBag, Liquibox and NexCel brands, and pairs them with digital services including SEE Smart Service Link for connected-equipment monitoring and prismiq for digital printing and smart packaging. Its developer surface is an Azure API Management program at developer.sealedair.com whose API catalog requires a portal account, so no public OpenAPI, reference or SDK is available to an unauthenticated integrator.

providers.name: Intuition Robotics
providers.description: Intuition Robotics is a Tel Aviv-based AI company (with offices in the United States, Japan, and Greece) building social companion technology for older adults. Its flagship product, ElliQ, is an AI care companion robot that proactively engages users through natural conversation, body language, lights, and sound, powered by a proprietary "Relationship Orchestrator" cognitive-AI platform and multiple large language models to support health, wellness, cognitive engagement, and reducing loneliness. Intuition Robotics publishes no first-party developer API, SDK, or developer portal; the ElliQ product store (elliq.com, on Shopify) does expose an agent-commerce surface via the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), including a published llms.txt and a UCP shopping MCP endpoint for agent-driven catalog search and checkout. Backed by Bloomberg Beta among other investors.

providers.name: Laelaps AI
providers.description: Laelaps AI is a Zurich- and UK-based autonomous security company building what it calls "the brain behind security" — a hardware-agnostic, fail-safe autonomy layer that unifies aerial, ground, and stationary robots together with a site's existing fixed cameras into a single coordinated monitoring force. The platform pairs field foundational models and visual intelligence with multi-agent coordination so that critical infrastructure and commercial and defense sites can be watched continuously, incidents detected and triaged automatically, and robots dispatched to observe and deter without a human operator watching every screen. Founded by Dr. Sophia Belser (CEO), Dr. Maria "Mania" Stamatopoulou (CRO), and Rokas Bendikas (CTO), the company is backed by Speedinvest, Expeditions Fund, Florent Venture Partners, Fund F, ESA BIC Switzerland, and NVIDIA Inception. As of this profile Laelaps AI publishes a three-page corporate website and no public developer surface — no documentation, API reference, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts were found.

providers.name: Stack AV
providers.description: Stack AV is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania autonomous-vehicle company founded in 2023 by Bryan Salesky (CEO), Peter Rander (President) and Brett Browning (CTO) — the leadership team behind Argo AI — and backed by SoftBank Group. The company develops AI-driven autonomy software and hardware for Class 8 commercial freight trucking, targeting driver shortages, vehicle uptime, safety, operating cost and emissions, and in May 2026 unveiled its first autonomous truck built in collaboration with PACCAR and Peterbilt Motors. Stack AV runs a public open-source engineering organization at github.com/stackav-oss (dltype, conch Triton kernels, clockwork, scene-tokens, push-guard, ai-workloads). It publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable API contract as of August 2026 — the product is an autonomous freight service, not a developer platform.

providers.name: Unitree Robotics
providers.description: Unitree Robotics is a Hangzhou, China-based high-performance robot manufacturer founded in 2016 by Wang Xingxing. The company is a global pioneer in the commercial quadruped (robot dog) market and has expanded into bipedal humanoid robots. Its product line includes the Go1, Go2, and Go2-W quadrupeds for consumers, education, and research; the industrial-grade B1 and B2 quadrupeds for inspection, patrol, and logistics; the H1 full-size humanoid; the G1 humanoid for research and developer experimentation; the R1 humanoid; and the Z1 robotic arm. Unitree also produces in-house components including the L1/L2 LiDAR, hand-grade actuators, and dexterous hands (Dex1-1). Unitree's developer surface is SDK-centric — there is no public REST or gRPC cloud API. Robot control happens on-device over DDS (Data Distribution Service) via the unitree_sdk2 (C++) and unitree_sdk2_python libraries, with high-level message bindings published as unitree_ros and unitree_ros2. The company maintains an active GitHub presence at github.com/unitreerobotics with 46+ public repositories covering SDKs, ROS packages, MuJoCo and Isaac Lab simulation environments, reinforcement learning frameworks (unitree_rl_gym, unitree_rl_lab), teleoperation tooling (xr_teleoperate, kinect_teleoperate, televuer), imitation learning (unitree_lerobot), a vision-language-action model (unifolm-vla), and a Unitree App Store template repo. Documentation lives at support.unitree.com/home/en/developer. Unitree's revenue model is direct robot hardware sales via shop.unitree.com and partner distribution; there is no metered API service tier.

providers.name: Aiper
providers.description: Aiper is a consumer robotics company that designs and sells cordless robotic pool cleaners, solar-powered pool skimmers and smart yard-care hardware (the Scuba, Surfer/EcoSurfer, Pilot and IrriSense lines), sold in more than 7,000 stores across 50+ countries with a US base in The Woodlands, Texas. Its devices are paired to the Aiper mobile app, which talks to a regional cloud control plane at apiamerica/apieurope/apiasia.aiper.com plus an AWS IoT MQTT layer. That cloud surface is a private first-party app backend: Aiper publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no SDK and no machine-readable contract, and every anonymous request to those hosts is answered with an authentication error. The only clients that speak it are unofficial, community reverse-engineered Home Assistant and Homebridge integrations.

providers.name: Andromeda
providers.description: Andromeda is a robotics company building personalised humanoid robot companions for aged care and assisted living. Its flagship robot, Abi, adapts to each resident's personality, ability, and language to provide social connection, conversation, and engagement that improves resident mood and wellbeing while extending care-team capacity. Founded by Grace Brown and backed by Forerunner Ventures and Paradigm, Andromeda has deployed Abi across aged-care providers in Australia and the United States (partners include mecwacare and Medical & Aged Care Group) and has been featured by the BBC, CNN, Forbes, and ABC Australia. The company currently publishes a public marketing and news site but no developer platform, API, or public technical documentation.

providers.name: Burnbot
providers.description: Burnbot is a wildfire mitigation and fuels management company that builds autonomous, remotely-operated machines and delivers field services to reduce hazardous vegetation and conduct controlled, precision fuel-reduction burns. Its equipment operates in steep, remote, and hazardous terrain around the clock in most weather conditions, cutting fuel loads without disturbing healthy vegetation or compacting soil, and is used across fire hazard mitigation, systematic fuels management, and timber operations. Burnbot works with utilities, transportation agencies, land managers, and tribal governments including PG&E, Caltrans, the U.S. Forest Service, and CAL FIRE. Burnbot was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. It is a hardware and field-services company with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Hub
providers.description: Hub (Hub.xyz) is a distributed physical-AI data infrastructure company that creates, annotates, and curates custom real-world datasets — egocentric first-person video, image, video, and audio — used to train AI and robotics models. Data is sourced through a global network of 500,000+ retail contributors and verified small and medium businesses across 150+ countries and 100+ languages. Hub offers both off-the-shelf labeled datasets and bespoke, custom-scoped data collection projects quoted within hours, delivered through a fully managed pipeline that couples automation with human-in-the-loop validation for frontier AI labs and Fortune 500 companies.

providers.name: Human Archive
providers.description: Human Archive is a Stanford- and Berkeley-founded, Y Combinator-funded data lab building foundational multimodal datasets for training AI and robotics systems to understand human movement and interaction. It collects and labels first-person video, RGB-D, audio, tactile, and motion-capture data from a network of 100,000+ contributors and 500+ industry partners, and provides dataset access to researchers and enterprise partners through a customer dashboard on request. The company is a B2B data infrastructure provider rather than a self-serve platform, and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation at this time.

providers.name: ICON
providers.description: ICON Technology, Inc. is an Austin, Texas construction-technology company building large-scale robotic 3D printing systems, materials, and software to make home building faster, more affordable, and more resilient. Its flagship Titan 3D construction printer, orchestrated by the proprietary BuildOS software that translates architectural designs into robotic tool paths and manages material flow, can print the wall system of a 2,500 sq. ft. home in under seven days. ICON operates a Design + Build division delivering 3D-printed homes and communities, a Technology division selling its printers and building systems to other builders, the CODEX digital home design catalog, and ICON Prime. The company is privately held and backed by investors including Bond Capital and Pantera Capital. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from a venture-portfolio lead; ICON publishes a marketing and product presence but no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Insitu
providers.description: Insitu Inc. is a wholly owned subsidiary of The Boeing Company that designs, builds, and operates uncrewed aerial systems (UAS) and related intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance technologies for defense and government customers. Its product line includes the Integrator, ScanEagle, and RQ-21A air vehicles alongside imaging payloads, ground control stations, and mission software such as TacitView, the Media Management Suite, and the Tungsten SDK. Insitu delivers end-to-end capabilities for collecting, processing, and distributing information, with more than 1.6 million operational flight hours across 30-plus international customers. Insitu operates as a defense contractor and publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Ocean Aero
providers.description: Ocean Aero is a Gulfport, Mississippi maritime robotics manufacturer that designs, builds and operates the Triton, an environmentally powered Autonomous Underwater and Surface Vehicle (AUSV) that can both sail on the surface and submerge to collect data above and below the waterline and relay it back to shore. The 14-foot platform harvests wind and solar energy, carries pre-packaged or custom payloads for defense, ocean research and offshore energy missions, and is managed through Ocean Aero's own proprietary mission-control GUI with fleet-wide waypoint and payload management. As of this profile Ocean Aero sells vehicles, payloads and mission services — it publishes no public developer program, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: PitPro Automation
providers.description: PitPro Automation is a fleet-maintenance technology company building automated tire-service systems that perform full tire changes and rotations on commercial fleet vehicles in under fifteen minutes. Targeting Class 2 and smaller vehicles, the company serves last-mile delivery, rideshare, utility, telecom, moving, and government fleets with in-bay automation, 24/7 monitoring, and field support. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, PitPro is a hardware-and-software provider focused on reducing fleet downtime; it currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK.

providers.name: Tennibot
providers.description: Tennibot builds AI-powered ball machines and autonomous ball collectors for tennis, pickleball, and padel. Its flagship Partner ball machine and Rover ball collector use computer vision and robotics to deliver realistic drills and eliminate manual ball pickup, controlled through the Tennibot mobile app for iOS and Android. The company, based in Auburn, Alabama and backed by Techstars, sells direct-to-consumer hardware; it ships a companion mobile app but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record; no external API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: TerraFirma
providers.description: TerraFirma, Inc. is a construction technology and physical-AI company building the robotic infrastructure stack for modern heavy-civil construction. Founded in 2024 by former SpaceX engineers and based in Austin, Texas, it combines AI-enabled pre-construction software (Mission Planner), a remote command-and-control center (Mission Control), and retrofitted semi-autonomous heavy machinery — excavators, bulldozers, loaders, graders and rollers operated autonomously, remotely, or traditionally. The company raised roughly $115M including a $100M Series A led by Kleiner Perkins with Bain Capital Ventures. TerraFirma publishes no public developer/API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Zoox
providers.description: Zoox is an Amazon subsidiary developing a purpose-built, bidirectional, symmetrical robotaxi vehicle designed from the ground up for autonomous ride-hailing rather than retrofitted from a conventional car. The vehicle carries up to four riders in a carriage-style seating layout, has no steering wheel or pedals, and is engineered for dense urban operation. Zoox provides the autonomous driving stack, the vehicle hardware, and a consumer ride-hail app. Commercial robotaxi service has launched in Las Vegas and San Francisco, with expansion announced for Austin, Miami, Atlanta, and Los Angeles. Acquired by Amazon in 2020, Zoox does not publish a public developer API or open research dataset; its public surface is product, ride-experience, and safety content. This profile captures the company surface for API Evangelist reference.

providers.name: Open Bionics
providers.description: Open Bionics is a Bristol, UK-based medical technology company that designs and manufactures advanced multi-grip bionic arms for children and adults with upper-limb differences. Its Hero product family (Hero ARM, Hero PRO, Hero RGD, Hero FLEX and Hero GAUNTLET) pairs 3D-printed, lightweight myoelectric prosthetic hands with an ecosystem of MyoPods wireless electrodes and the Sidekick companion app, delivered through a network of specialist prosthetists and clinics in the US and UK. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface.

providers.name: Spartan Radar
providers.description: Spartan Radar is an automotive radar software and sensing company, now operating as the radar technology brand of Pro-Vision Solutions, LLC following its 2025 acquisition. Its Clarify software applies proprietary digital signal processing and machine-learning perception to existing automotive radar sensors, raising resolution 3-8x on commodity silicon (ARM Cortex, Texas Instruments TDA4VM and AWR, NVIDIA Orin and DRIVE, NXP SAF85xx/SAF86xx) without new hardware, and its Hoplo product is a software-defined collision-avoidance and blind-spot warning system for commercial and heavy vehicles across mining, construction, material handling and logistics. Spartan sells to commercial-vehicle OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers and fleet operators as embedded software and hardware; it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: TreeX Robotics
providers.description: TreeX Robotics is an Israeli physical-AI company founded in 2024 that is bringing autonomous robotics to outdoor field operations at scale. TreeX replaces human field crews with fleets of physical AI-powered autonomous workers that perform high-skill field operations as an on-demand labor service, regardless of terrain or ground conditions. The company is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (seed, 2024) and operates in Israel, the United States, and Italy. TreeX publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Westmag
providers.description: Western Magnetics (Westmag) designs and manufactures brushless DC (BLDC) drone motors and robot actuators in South San Francisco, California. Built and scaled in America and NDAA-compliant from day one, Westmag is a vertically integrated motor company spanning design, manufacturing, and supply chain — producing high-volume BLDC drone motors for Group 1, 2, and 3 UAS platforms (20-100mm stators, Kv 100-3,000, outrunner and inrunner) and integrated actuators for humanoid and mobile robots (torque 1-150Nm, 24-48V, gearing 6:1-12:1). Founded by David Hansen (CEO) and Jordan Sanders (COO) and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, Lux Capital, Menlo Ventures, and NFDG. This is a hardware company; it currently exposes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Diligent Robotics
providers.description: Diligent Robotics is an Austin, Texas-based healthcare robotics company founded in 2017 by Andrea Thomaz (CEO) and Vivian Chu (CIO), both trained as roboticists at MIT, Georgia Tech, and the University of Texas at Austin. The company builds Moxi, a socially intelligent mobile manipulator that operates autonomously inside hospitals to handle non-clinical material transport — delivering medications, lab samples, supplies, PPE, and patient items so nurses and clinical staff can focus on patient care. Moxi combines mobile manipulation (grasping, opening doors, riding elevators), social navigation, and human-guided learning, and is deployed 24/7 with minimal facility infrastructure (existing Wi-Fi). Operationally, Moxi has logged 500,000+ deliveries and 100,000+ autonomous elevator rides across customer hospitals including UTMB, Shannon Health, ThedaCare, Carilion Giles Community Hospital, and Medical City Denton. The platform is HIPAA compliant, SOC 2 Type II audited, and TX-RAMP Level 2 certified. Diligent has raised roughly $100M across rounds led by Canaan, True Ventures, Tiger Global, DNX Ventures, Next Coast Ventures, and Northwestern Medicine Innovation. Diligent's revenue model is robot deployment/leasing and enterprise services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Moxi or its underlying robotics stack.

providers.name: Flyzipline
providers.description: Flyzipline (Zipline International Inc., flyzipline.com / zipline.com) designs, manufactures, and operates autonomous delivery drones for food, groceries, and medicine. Its instant logistics platform flies vital shipments — blood products, vaccines, pharmaceuticals, prepared meals, and retail goods — on direct aerial routes at up to 70 mph, with temperature-controlled pods and real-time tracking. Zipline operates distribution centers across the United States, Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire, and Japan, partnering with health systems, retailers (Walmart, Chipotle), and restaurant technology providers (Olo) that submit delivery requests through Zipline's ordering system or software integrations. As of early 2026 the fleet has completed more than two million commercial deliveries across 120+ million autonomous miles. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars-adjacent portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Zipline publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI at this time — partner integrations are bespoke.

providers.name: Wandercraft
providers.description: Wandercraft is a robotics company founded in 2012 by Nicolas Simon, Matthieu Masselin and Jean-Louis Constanza, dual-headquartered in Paris and New York with 175+ AI, robotics and industrial staff. It designs, manufactures and sells self-balancing robotic exoskeletons and humanoid robots. Atalante X is a hands-free, self-balancing overground rehabilitation exoskeleton with 12 motors, used in more than 100 rehabilitation and research centers, CE-marked in 2019 and FDA-cleared for stroke (2022), spinal cord injury (2024) and multiple sclerosis (2025). Eve is the personal self-balancing exoskeleton for wheelchair users, FDA-cleared and commercially launching in the United States in 2026. Calvin-40 is the industrial humanoid built on the same full-body control stack for part handling, flow logistics, picking and kitting in factories and warehouses, deployed at Renault's Douai plant. Renault Group took a stake and joined as industrial partner alongside the June 2025 Series D. Wandercraft publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind: the product is regulated medical-device and industrial hardware, its control software is embedded in the device, and its only public code surface is a single maintenance fork of a third-party C library on GitHub.

providers.name: Kinetic
providers.description: Kinetic (Kinetic Automation) builds robotics-based automated collision repair for modern vehicles equipped with advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). The company operates robotic repair facilities (Kinetic Hubs), automated imaging for collision damage assessment and repair estimates (Kinetic Vision), and AI-powered calibration identification software (Kinetic ID) that determines which ADAS sensors need recalibration after a repair. Backed by Menlo Ventures and Techstars, Kinetic was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and corporate site plus a login-only identity portal (id.kinetic.auto); it exposes no public developer program, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or webhooks surface.

providers.name: BRINC
providers.description: BRINC builds a connected ecosystem of drones, software, and services purpose-built for public safety in the United States. Its Drone as First Responder (DFR) systems — the Guardian and Responder outdoor drones, the Lemur 2 indoor tactical drone, and the throwable BRINC Ball — pair with LiveOps teleoperations software (livestreaming, two-way comms, evidence management) to put a camera overhead within seconds of a 911 call. BRINC reports deployments across 900+ public safety agencies in all 50 states, sub-70-second average drone arrival times, and a recent $125M funding round. The company also runs its Safeguard upgrade-and-repair program and grant/DFR playbook services. BRINC exposes no public developer API, SDK, or MCP surface as of this profile; this entry is enriched from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Dexory
providers.description: Dexory is a UK-based warehouse intelligence and robotics company whose DexoryView platform pairs fleets of autonomous mobile scanning robots with physical AI to deliver real-time "ground truth" visibility across warehouses and distribution centers. The robots autonomously scan more than 10,000 pallet locations per hour and up to 18 meters of racking height, building a live digital twin that feeds AI-driven analytics for inventory accuracy, space and slotting optimization, damage/compliance detection, and operational performance. DexoryView is organized into modules (Integrity for stock accuracy and automated cycle counts, Optimise for space and productivity analytics, and Adapt for real-time operational response) and connects into existing warehouse and ERP systems such as SAP EWM, Manhattan, Blue Yonder, and Körber through pre-built connectors. Dexory serves 3PL logistics, manufacturing, food & beverage, retail, pharma, and air cargo operators. Added to the API Evangelist network from Atomico's portfolio and enriched via the pipeline; Dexory does not currently publish a public developer portal or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Gather AI
providers.description: Gather AI is a Physical AI platform for logistics that gives warehouses dock-to-dock inventory visibility. Cameras mounted on autonomous drones and forklifts capture inventory, and computer vision extracts structured data (LPNs, UPCs, lot codes, and free text) from the imagery. Its Sage AI engine analyzes operations and surfaces prioritized actions before each shift, while automated Workflows route tasks to the right personnel across integrated systems. The plug-and-play solution deploys in hours alongside existing warehouse management systems, serving manufacturing, healthcare, food & beverage, retail, and 3PL operations. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bain-capital-ventures and bloomberg-beta.

providers.name: HavocAI
providers.description: HavocAI (Havoc) is a Providence, Rhode Island-based defense technology company building all-domain collaborative autonomy software and autonomous surface vessels for the U.S. Navy, U.S. Army and allied militaries. Its software suite pairs Havoc OS, an edge autonomy operating system for heterogeneous platforms, with Havoc C2 for one-to-many operator control, Havoc Insights for real-time sensor and telemetry analytics, and Havoc Connect, a resilient peer-to-peer overlay network for degraded or GPS-denied environments. The company builds the Rampage, Seahound, Kiakoa and Atlas autonomous surface vessels and is partnered with Hanwha on 200-foot ASVs. Enrichment probing in July 2026 found no public developer API, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no developer portal or documentation, no published SDKs or packages, no MCP server, and no A2A agent card - the platform is delivered under defense contract rather than as a self-serve developer product.

providers.name: Vatn Systems
providers.description: Vatn Systems is a Bristol, Rhode Island defense technology company founded in 2023 that designs and manufactures low-cost, modular autonomous underwater vehicles (UUVs/AUVs) and the autonomy, navigation and acoustic-processing software that runs on them. Its product line spans the Skelmir S6 (6-inch, man-portable, swarm-capable) and Skelmir S12 (12.75-inch medium-class) vehicles, Eyra 5.1 and Eyra 8.0 passive hydrophone arrays, and four software systems - INStinct (maritime inertial navigation for GPS-denied operation), PARse (embedded acoustic signal processing on ARM), FUSE (multi-sensor tracking, distributed as a Docker image) and AEsir (TAK-native sensor fusion and mission planning). Mission planning is delivered through an ATAK/CivTAK/MilTAK/WinTAK plugin and Fathom, a browser-based mission planner and vehicle configurator. Vatn raised a $60M Series A in December 2025 (total funding $76.5M) and acquired Crewless Marine. It publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract; every integration surface is reached through a demo request or supplier form.

providers.name: Xenex Disinfection Services
providers.description: Xenex Disinfection Services is a San Antonio, Texas-based medical technology company founded in 2008 by Johns Hopkins-trained epidemiologists Dr. Mark Stibich and Dr. Julie Stachowiak. Its LightStrike+ pulsed-xenon UV robot is the first FDA-authorized whole-room microbial reduction device, used by hospitals to destroy pathogens like C. difficile on surfaces; the portfolio also includes the LightStrike6 robot, the Deactivate handheld LED unit, and the TrackMate digital cleaning-event tracking system with a client portal at dms.xenex.com. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, but the company does publish an llms.txt company profile on its website.

providers.name: Aeronext
providers.description: Aeronext Inc. (株式会社エアロネクスト) is a Tokyo-based industrial drone technology startup, founded April 2017 by Keisuke Toji in Ebisu-Nishi, Shibuya-ku. Its core product is 4D GRAVITY(R), a patented airframe design that separates the flight unit from the payload unit and actively controls the center of gravity, improving stability, flight efficiency and payload performance. Aeronext monetizes through technology licensing and joint development — the Next-series airframes (AirTruck, LogiAir, PD4B-M-AN with PRODRONE) are built by licensee manufacturers — rather than through software. Its subsidiary NEXT DELIVERY Inc. operates SkyHub(R), a drone-plus-ground smart logistics platform co-developed with Seino Holdings and deployed across Japanese municipalities, with the SkyHub TMS system and a SkyHub Provider License program. Aeronext publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Farmwise
providers.description: FarmWise Labs is an agricultural technology company building AI-powered robotics for specialty crop farming. Its flagship product, Vulcan, is an intra-row weeder and precision cultivator that uses computer vision and machine learning to identify and mechanically remove weeds without herbicides, covering up to three acres per hour and saving growers an estimated $250+ per acre. The self-calibrating machine operates in all field conditions and receives over-the-air software updates. Founded in San Francisco and backed by GV (Google Ventures), FarmWise is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or specification surface.

providers.name: GrayMatter Robotics
providers.description: GrayMatter Robotics is an American industrial AI and robotics company founded in 2020 by SK Gupta, Ariyan Kabir and Brual Shah, headquartered at a 100,000-square-foot AI Robotics Innovation Center in Carson, California. The company builds smart robotic cells for surface treatment and finishing in high-mix, high-variability manufacturing — sanding, grinding, polishing, buffing, blasting, spraying, trimming and AI-based dimensional inspection and defect detection — pairing off-the-shelf industrial robot arms, 3D scanners and tools with its own physics-informed AI stack (GMR-AI, marketed as Factory SuperIntelligence / FSI). Its flagship Scan&Sand cell 3D-scans each incoming part and generates the toolpath autonomously, so a cell can change over between parts in minutes without fixturing or teach-pendant programming, and the company claims 4-12x throughput over manual finishing with 30-70% less consumable waste. GrayMatter sells robots-as-a-service on a monthly subscription that bundles hardware, software, training, remote monitoring and 24/7 support instead of an upfront capital purchase, and counts Boeing, Caterpillar and Oshkosh among its customers. It raised a $45M Series B in June 2024 led by Wellington Management with NGP Capital, Euclidean Capital, B Capital, 3M Ventures, Calibrate VC, OCA Ventures, Pathbreaker VC, Stage Venture Partners and Swift VC participating. GrayMatter Robotics is a robotics hardware and AI systems manufacturer: as of the August 2026 enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, SDK, CLI or machine-readable API contract (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, gRPC), no MCP server and no A2A agent card. Note that this company is unrelated to greymatter.io, the service-mesh vendor with a similar name.

providers.name: Humatics
providers.description: Humatics Corporation is a Waltham, Massachusetts microlocation company founded in 2015 by MIT professor David Mindell and led by CEO James Kinsey. It builds radio-frequency positioning systems — ultra-wideband beacons, RF-pulse ranging, radar and inertial sensors fused in software — that locate people, vehicles and robots at centimeter- to millimeter-scale precision. Two product lines are on sale today: MILO, a sub-millimeter positioning system for industrial automation and in-motion robotics, advertised as compatible with Yaskawa, Mitsubishi Electric, FANUC, Universal Robots and KUKA; and Mobility, a rail and transit portfolio covering the FOCUS track-geometry monitoring kit and the Humatics Rail Navigation System (HRNS), used on New York City MTA subway signalling projects. Humatics publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable description of any product API. Two rounds of probing humatics.com returned HTTP 404 for every /.well-known/ path, /llms.txt, /openapi.json, /openapi.yaml, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /graphql; *.humatics.com is a DNS wildcard onto one retired address, so api., docs., developer., portal. and status. resolve but time out on connect. The only machine-readable HTTP interface on any Humatics host is the WordPress REST API of the marketing site itself at humatics.com/wp-json/ — 375 routes across 19 stock core and commercial-plugin namespaces, exposing pages and posts rather than positioning, and so recorded as evidence rather than catalogued as a Humatics API. The GitHub organization github.com/Humatics is real and public, but 31 of its 33 repositories are forks of third-party embedded and robotics open source (Fast-RTPS, Fast-CDR, FreeRTOS, Orange Pi BSP, Yocto meta-layers, EIPScanner, donkeycar); the two non-forks are internal tools. There is no first-party SDK, client library or specification, and no package named humatics exists on npm or PyPI. Marketing material for the earlier KinetIQ OS / Spatial Intelligence Platform referenced an "extensible API", but no public interface for it was ever documented, and the news host that carried those announcements (now.humatics.com) no longer answers.

providers.name: Lumotive
providers.description: Lumotive is a Seattle-based semiconductor company building programmable optics on its patented Light Control Metasurface (LCM) technology — solid-state, software-defined beam steering implemented in a standard CMOS process with no moving parts. Its products include the LM10 and LX10 LCM beam-steering chips, the LCM Evaluation Kit (LEK), the M30 iToF and NM120 3D-sensing development kits, and the M30/TX10 reference designs, applied to industrial automation, intelligent traffic systems, automotive ADAS and autonomy, defense, and optical circuit switching for AI data centers. Lumotive publishes an "Open Lidar API" — a real-time control interface for software-defined Lidar 2.0 hardware covering region-of-interest scanning, frame rate, resolution and range, plus a common point-cloud format — and ships C/C++ LCM control libraries with Python bindings alongside its evaluation kits. That interface is an embedded hardware-control API, not a public web API: no developer portal, documentation site, machine-readable specification, or self-service sign-up is published, and access is granted to selected partners through the Technology Access Program by contacting the company.

providers.name: Theker
providers.description: Theker (THEKER Robotics) is a Barcelona-based robotics and artificial intelligence company whose stated mission is "solving 100% of physical work" — building humanoid and physical-AI systems it frames as "a power beyond human" and "the next frontier of robotics and intelligence." The company is at a stealth stage: its public site is a landing page and careers portal with product details deliberately withheld ("Details remain secured"). Its public GitHub organization (THEKER Robotics, Spain) works in the physical-AI/ROS 2 stack — forks of the ZED ROS 2 wrapper, NVIDIA cuRobo CUDA motion planning, and Meta SAM 3 perception. Backed by CRV. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK is published yet; this profile captures its identity and public surface pending a developer platform.

providers.name: blueflite
providers.description: blueflite is a Techstars-backed unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) company that designs and manufactures autonomous cargo and delivery drones built on its SLATE platform for all-weather, time-sensitive logistics. Its aircraft target last-mile shipping and medical or life-saving delivery (such as defibrillators and emergency supplies), and the company complements the hardware with blueDelivery (a consumer ordering app), blueDigital (a cloud productivity tool), and blueControl, alongside drone consulting, engineering, and project services. blueflite is on the FAA Section 44807 approved UAS list and holds FCC conditional approval, and was founded by Frank Noppel and James McClearen. No public developer or API surface is currently published.

providers.name: EndoQuest Robotics
providers.description: EndoQuest Robotics is a Houston, Texas medical device company — founded in 2017 and operating as ColubrisMX until its June 2022 rebrand — developing what it calls the world's first flexible endoluminal robotic surgical system. Its Endoluminal Surgical (ELS) System pairs an ergonomic physician console (high-definition monitor, hand controllers, foot pedals) with a mobile patient cart and positioning arm, driving two 6mm flexible robotic instruments and a 3.7mm high-definition robotic camera through the EndoDrive, with up to seven degrees of freedom and additional channels for insufflation, suction, irrigation and third-party accessories. The design targets scar-free minimally invasive procedures inside the gastrointestinal tract — including appendectomy and cholecystectomy — performed through natural orifices or a single transumbilical incision. The company was accepted into the FDA's Safer Technologies Program in December 2023, received an investigational device exemption in December 2024, and began first colorectal cases in its PARADIGM pivotal multicenter study in May 2025. The system is not FDA-cleared and is not for commercial sale. EndoQuest sells surgical robotics hardware, not software: it publishes no API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind, and its nine-page marketing site carries no developer surface.

providers.name: Mendaera
providers.description: Mendaera is a healthcare robotics company building the Focalist handheld robotic system, which combines robotics, real-time ultrasound imaging, and software to guide needle-based medical procedures with greater precision and consistency. The FDA-cleared platform is preparing for broad commercial launch in 2026. Mendaera is backed by Lux Capital, Threshold Ventures, Founders Fund, PFM Health Sciences, and Puma Venture Capital. The company is focused on medical devices rather than a developer-facing platform; as of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Agility Robotics
providers.description: Agility Robotics is a Salem, Oregon humanoid robotics company building industrial bipedal robots for warehouse and factory automation. Founded in 2015 as a spin-out of Oregon State University's Dynamic Robotics Laboratory, its flagship product is Digit — described as the first humanoid robot in commercial production deployment — and Arc, the cloud-based automation platform that operates Digit fleets, provides real-time visibility, manages task assignments, and connects Digit to existing warehouse automation including AMRs, WMS, and WES systems. Digit has commercial deployments and pilots with Amazon, GXO Logistics, Schaeffler, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, and Mercado Libre, with an expanded NVIDIA partnership for foundation-model and simulation tooling. Agility operates RoboFab, a humanoid robot factory in Salem, OR with capacity to produce 10,000 robots annually. Digit has surpassed 100,000 totes moved in commercial deployment at a single Georgia facility. Agility Robotics does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Digit or Arc; integration is performed by Agility's solutions team and partners through a gated low-level JSON-over-WebSocket API and pysdk delivered with the robot. The company's public GitHub org primarily contains forks of infrastructure tooling (JFrog, Bazel, Fluent Bit, Kubernetes Cluster API) plus an archived documentation repo for the earlier Cassie research platform.

providers.name: FANUC
providers.description: FANUC Corporation is a Japanese multinational headquartered in Oshino, Yamanashi at the base of Mount Fuji, and is one of the world's largest suppliers of factory automation, industrial robots, and CNC (computer numerical control) systems. Founded in 1972 after spinning out of Fujitsu's numerical control division (originated 1955) under Seiuemon Inaba, FANUC pioneered commercial NC and CNC technology and by the early 1980s held roughly half of the global CNC market. The company operates three primary business segments: FA (CNC systems, servo motors, lasers, and PMC controls for machine tools), Robot (industrial arms from the LR Mate and M-series through the heavy-payload M-2000iA, plus the CRX collaborative robot family), and ROBOMACHINE (ROBODRILL machining centers, ROBOCUT wire EDM, and ROBOSHOT all-electric injection molding machines). FANUC's primary developer surface is FOCAS (FANUC Open CNC API Specification), a licensed C/C++ library (fwlib32.dll) used by machine builders and MES/OEE vendors to read CNC state over Ethernet, plus KAREL and Teach Pendant (TP) programming on the robot controllers and a published ROS 2 driver for the CRX collaborative arms. FANUC does not operate a public REST developer portal or publish OpenAPI specifications; integrations are partner-driven through MTConnect adapters, OPC UA servers, FIELD system edge apps, and the FANUC America customer/training portals.

providers.name: KUKA
providers.description: KUKA AG is a German industrial automation company headquartered in Augsburg, Bavaria, founded in 1898 and majority-owned by China's Midea Group since 2016. KUKA designs and manufactures industrial robots, autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), production cells, controllers, and the software stack that drives them. Its product portfolio spans six-axis articulated robots (KR series), sensitive collaborative robots (LBR iiwa, LBR iisy), mobile platforms (KMR iiwa, KMP), and palletizing/welding/CNC cells, controlled by the KR C4 and KR C5 / KR C5 micro controller generations. The robot software stack centers on KUKA System Software (KSS/VSS) for KR C4-class hardware, the newer iiQKA.OS / iiQKA.OS2 operating system for KR C5, and the KUKA Robot Language (KRL) for motion programming, with extension surfaces including KUKA.RobotSensorInterface (RSI), KUKA.EthernetKRL, KUKA.PLC mxAutomation for external PLC control, KUKA.OPC UA, and KUKA.AppTech / iiQKA App Builder for option packages. Engineering and simulation are delivered through iiQWorks (iiQWorks.Sim, iiQWorks.App Builder, iiQWorks.Copilot) and KUKA.Sim, while operational software includes KUKA Xpert (documentation/cloud), KUKA iiQoT (condition monitoring), and KUKA Connect / my.KUKA customer portals. KUKA does not publish a first-party public REST/OpenAPI developer API or an official GitHub organization for its robot control stack; integration is performed through proprietary protocols (RSI, EthernetKRL, mxAutomation, OPC UA, PROFINET, EtherCAT) and SDKs distributed via the iiQKA Creator portal and KUKA Xpert. A meaningful body of open-source KUKA integration code lives in the community-maintained kroshu GitHub organization (ROS 2 drivers, external-control SDK, URDF robot descriptions) and the roboticsapi / openkuka projects. KUKA serves automotive, electronics, battery, metal, consumer goods, healthcare, aerospace, and e-commerce logistics customers, and through its Swisslog subsidiary extends into warehouse and intralogistics automation.

providers.name: Aigen
providers.description: Aigen ("AI Generated Agriculture") is a Kirkland, Washington robotics company founded in 2020 that builds fully autonomous, solar-powered farm robots for daily, chemical-free weed control. Its flagship product, the Element, uses AI vision to identify and mechanically strike weeds — including herbicide-resistant weeds — with no herbicides, running on solar power with onboard battery storage and coordinating as a crew over a mesh network. In 2026 Aigen introduced Alchemy, a generative world model for outdoor physical AI that produces self-labeling synthetic training data. Aigen sells a managed robotics-as-a-service engagement rather than a self-serve developer product: growers are onboarded through a local Aigen agent and an intake form, and Aigen operates and maintains the fleet through the growing season. As of this profile Aigen publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Dronamics
providers.description: Dronamics is a European deep-tech company that designs, builds, and operates autonomous long-range cargo drones for middle-mile logistics. Its flagship aircraft, The Black Swan, is a remotely piloted UAV that carries up to 350 kg (770 lb) of cargo over distances up to 2,500 km (1,550 mi), enabling same-day, cross-border, point-to-point deliveries that are faster, cheaper, and lower in CO2 emissions than traditional air freight. Founded in 2014 in Sofia, Bulgaria by brothers Svilen and Konstantin Rangelov and operating as Dronamics Group Limited, the company is building the world's first cargo drone airline, operating a proprietary drone fleet from a network of low-cost droneports. The public dronamics.com marketing site is built on Wix and exposes a Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic access; Dronamics does not publish a developer-facing logistics API, OpenAPI, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: ECOVACS Robotics
providers.description: ECOVACS Robotics is a global home service robotics company founded in 1998 and headquartered in Suzhou, China, that designs, manufactures, and sells AI-powered autonomous cleaning devices for consumer and commercial use. Its product families include DEEBOT robotic vacuum and mopping robots, WINBOT window-cleaning robots, GOAT robotic lawn mowers, ULTRAMARINE pool-cleaning robots, and the DEEBOT PRO commercial line, all managed through the ECOVACS HOME mobile app. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of IDG Capital; as of this enrichment pass ECOVACS publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documented API surface — this profile captures its public web, support, and legal properties plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Ubiq (now NECTURE)
providers.description: Ubiq is a Vienna, Austria mobility-intelligence company (NECTURE GmbH) that rebranded from UBIQ to NECTURE in 2024. Its "distributed operations" SaaS platform turns fleet data into action for shared-mobility operators, business fleets transitioning to EVs, autonomous fleets, and last-mile delivery -- offering automated rebalancing, predictive charging (Charging as a Service), and airport peak services, alongside StreetCrowd, its decentralized community workforce for fleet operations. Founded in 2015 around city parking optimization, it pivoted to shared-mobility SaaS in 2020 and is backed by Speedinvest among other investors. No public developer portal, API documentation, or client packages were found.

providers.name: Adasky
providers.description: ADASKY (Adasky Ltd.) is an Israeli automotive sensor company founded in January 2016 and headquartered in Yokneam, Israel, that develops and manufactures automotive-grade long-wave infrared (LWIR) thermal imaging cameras and the perception software that runs on them. Its flagship product, Viper, is a compact solid-state shutterless thermal camera with 50mK sensitivity, object detection to about 300 metres and living-being classification beyond 200 metres, sold into ADAS and autonomous-vehicle programs for pedestrian, cyclist and wildlife detection, free-space detection and automatic emergency braking in darkness, glare and fog. A second line, SharpVision, serves intelligent transportation, V2X and smart-city infrastructure. ADASKY publishes no developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification; its software ships embedded in the camera under commercial OEM engagement.

providers.name: Armstrong Robotics
providers.description: Armstrong Robotics is building general-purpose robots for commercial kitchens, beginning with autonomous dishwashing systems that load, run, and unload dishware without human intervention. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, the company is an early-stage robotics startup focused on kitchen labor automation. It currently exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation; it was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-sourced lead awaiting a public API surface, and this profile carries only the identity and domain-security signals that could be verified from its public website.

providers.name: Bliq
providers.description: Bliq is a Berlin-based premium driverless-car subscription service rolling out across Europe. Instead of owning a car or paying per ride, members subscribe monthly to a private autonomous vehicle that Bliq charges, cleans, insures, maintains, and parks on their behalf. Cars are booked for time windows (hours or days) rather than single trips, every journey is remotely supervised by licensed local operators, and there is no surge pricing. Backed by Speedinvest, Bliq positions itself as "ownership without ownership." The company currently operates a consumer marketing site with early-access and waitlist flows and does not publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: ChemTech AI
providers.description: ChemTech AI is an industrial software company, founded in 2018 and headquartered in New York, that builds autonomous AI control systems for chemical production plants. Its software continuously optimizes manufacturing by autonomously adjusting DCS setpoints to push plants to their maximum safe capacity, sustaining peak production while reducing emissions and losses. The platform is applied across chemical processes including ammonia, nitric acid, phosphoric acid, sulfuric acid, methanol, ethanol, and polyethylene, serving the chemicals, food, cosmetics, and oil and gas sectors. ChemTech AI is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal are currently published.

providers.name: Cortica
providers.description: Cortica is a Tel Aviv, Israel based Autonomous AI company founded in 2007 that builds and spins out category-leading AI companies. Its self-learning, unsupervised "Autonomous AI" is modelled on the mammalian cortex — signatures instead of labels, adaptive architecture, and self-learning neural networks that index high volumes of visual, audio, radar and time-series signal on low-compute platforms. Cortica states it has invested more than $250M over 15 years and holds 300+ patents, and it operates as a venture builder rather than a product vendor: its technology reaches the market through partner joint ventures and spin-outs including Autobrains (autonomous driving), Corsight AI (facial recognition), Corsound AI (voice), SeeTrue (airport security screening), CordiGuide (medical imaging) and Lean AI / Qualisense (industrial quality inspection, with Johnson Electric). Cortica itself publishes no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification on its own domain.

providers.name: Mytra
providers.description: Mytra, Inc. is a Brisbane, California robotics company founded in 2022 by former Tesla robotics lead Chris Walti, building what it calls software-defined warehousing: a three-part system of low-profile MytraBots that travel in X, Y and Z through a modular steel "cell" matrix up to 80 feet tall, and an AI-driven operating system that plans routes, resolves conflicts and dynamically reconfigures the matrix to store and retrieve anything from cases to full 3,000 lb pallets. The company raised a $120M Series C led by Avenir Growth in January 2026 (roughly $200M total) and sells the system as installed industrial infrastructure to enterprise distribution and food-and-beverage operators. Mytra publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Nomagic
providers.description: Nomagic builds Physical AI for end-to-end warehouse automation, using AI-powered robotic arms and computer vision to automate picking, packing, sorting and other fulfillment tasks across e-commerce, fashion, pharmaceutical and third-party logistics warehouses. Nomagic exposes a standard Station API for systems integrators, WCS/WMS providers and customers to control its robots, and a Grip AI API that adds an intelligence layer to third-party robot hardware; all robot actions are recorded to the Nomagic Cloud to continually improve its models. The company is backed by Khosla Ventures. Public developer documentation for these APIs is not published; integration is arranged directly with Nomagic.

providers.name: Norbert Health
providers.description: Norbert Health, Inc. builds "Norbert", an autonomous care manager for nursing homes and rehabilitation facilities — a robot-mounted or tabletop AI module that plans rounding schedules, contactlessly senses patient vitals and behavior, and writes clinical notes without additional staff. Its multimodal sensing stack captures pulse and respiratory rate, room presence and activity, mobility and gait, environmental context, and cognitive signals from vocal biomarkers, then turns them into tasks, role-specific alerts, and structured EMR notes. Founded in 2019 by Alexandre Winter with offices in Brooklyn, Paris, and Montreal, the company raised a $5M Seed II in 2021 co-led by Serena Capital and HCVC. The device is investigational and limited by US federal law to investigational use pending FDA clearance. Norbert Health publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable contract; integration is arranged through a sales conversation.

providers.name: Plus
providers.description: Plus (PlusAI) develops AI-based autonomous driving technology for commercial trucks. Its flagship SuperDrive is an AI-powered Level 4 autonomous driving system, and HyperFoundry is an integrated development platform for Physical AI. Plus works through partnerships with truck OEMs including TRATON GROUP, Hyundai, and IVECO rather than shipping a public developer API. Backed by GGV Capital, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; this enrichment pass confirmed it exposes no public API, SDK, or developer portal surface, and captured its domain-security posture.

providers.name: Scout
providers.description: Scout (Scout Space) is a Techstars- and venture-backed space technology company founded in 2019 that builds next-generation orbital sensing and autonomy for Space Domain Awareness (SDA). Its in-space products, first launched in 2021, let spacecraft see and understand objects around them through electro-optical and infrared sensors (the Owl long-range SDA sensor line), edge processing hardware, mission autonomy software developed with the U.S. Space Force, and mission-design analysis. Scout supplies cross-orbit intelligence and dynamic space operations to government and commercial operators and has been awarded multiple AFWERX SBIR and USSF TACFI contracts. Scout does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sensemesh
providers.description: Sensemesh builds an AI-powered operating system that unifies cameras, sensors, and drones into a single intelligent network for real-time perception and autonomous response. The platform fuses visual, thermal, audio, and pressure sensor data so organizations can detect threats, investigate incidents, dispatch drones autonomously, and query sensor history in natural language across law enforcement, corrections and prisons, events and venues, homeowners associations, and schools and universities. Backed by DCVC, Sensemesh was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass the company publishes a single marketing site (sensemesh.ai) with no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or well-known metadata.

providers.name: Symbotic
providers.description: Symbotic is an AI-powered warehouse automation company that designs, manufactures, and operates end-to-end robotic distribution and micro-fulfillment systems for food and beverage, retail grocery, healthcare, apparel, retail general merchandise, and consumer packaged goods customers. Its portfolio includes the Symbotic distribution solution for case handling, SymMicro for less-than-case micro-fulfillment, autonomous SymBots mobile robots, warehouse AI software, and Warehouse-as-a-Service offerings. Symbotic operates as a hardware-and-services vendor and does not publish a public developer portal or open APIs.

providers.name: The Bot Company
providers.description: The Bot Company is a San Francisco robotics startup founded in 2024 by Kyle Vogt, the co-founder and former CEO of Cruise, building a helpful general-purpose robot for every home to automate everyday household chores. Its team draws from Tesla, Cruise, OpenAI, Google, and Pixar, and the company has raised roughly $301M (reportedly valued near $2B) from investors including Spark Capital and SV Angel. As of this profile the company operates a marketing and careers site only and publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Thirdwave
providers.description: Thirdwave (Third Wave Automation) builds autonomous material-handling systems for warehouses and distribution centers, led by its shared-autonomy forklift platform where one human operator can supervise a fleet of self-driving forklifts that operate independently and hand control back to a person when needed. Its ArmadaFMS (Armada Fleet Management System) software coordinates the robotic fleet across facilities. The company is a venture-backed logistics-robotics provider (backed by Homebrew and Norwest Venture Partners). As of this enrichment pass Third Wave publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: WeRide
providers.description: WeRide (NASDAQ: WRD) is an autonomous driving technology company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Guangzhou, China. It develops Level 4 self-driving technology across a portfolio of five core products — Robotaxi, Robobus, Robovan, Robosweeper (autonomous sanitation) and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) — and operates its fleets in more than 40 cities across 12 countries. WeRide does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public web presence and domain-security posture as surfaced by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Bedrock
providers.description: Bedrock (Bedrock Ocean Exploration) builds advanced autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) and Mosaic, a cloud-native data platform that transforms how the world maps, monitors, and understands the seafloor. Its AUV fleet carries multibeam echosounder, side-scan sonar, magnetometer, and sub-bottom profiler payloads to deliver high-resolution geophysical survey data for offshore energy (wind, oil and gas, renewables), ports and harbors, submarine telecom infrastructure, defense, and scientific research. A Northzone portfolio company, Bedrock is an enterprise ocean-data provider; it publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Zipline
providers.description: Zipline is a South San Francisco–headquartered autonomous logistics company operating the world's largest commercial drone delivery network, with more than two million customer deliveries flown across the United States, Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Côte d'Ivoire, and Japan. Zipline designs, builds, and operates two end-to-end aircraft platforms: Platform 1 (P1, "Sparrow"), a long-range fixed-wing aircraft that launches from a catapult, parachutes payloads from altitude, and is used primarily for national-scale healthcare logistics — delivering blood products, vaccines, medicines, and lab samples to hospitals and clinics — and Platform 2 (P2), a short-range hybrid VTOL aircraft with an autonomous tethered "droid" delivery vehicle that lowers packages from a hovering aircraft directly to a designated point on the ground, enabling precision quick-commerce delivery from restaurants, retailers, pharmacies, and hospitals. Zipline's customer roster includes Walmart, OhioHealth, Michigan Medicine, Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic Florida, MultiCare, Sweetgreen, GNC, Jet's Pizza, the governments of Rwanda, Ghana, Nigeria, and Kenya, and Japan's Toyota Tsusho, with the P2 platform actively scaling across the Dallas–Fort Worth Metroplex, Pea Ridge (AR), and expanding into Houston and Phoenix in 2026. The company also operates one of the largest civil autonomous aviation stacks in the world — proprietary detect-and-avoid, route planning, weather, fleet operations, and flight-control software — and in 2025 received the first-ever FAA Part 135 BVLOS (beyond-visual-line-of-sight) operational approval permitting drone package delivery without visual observers. Zipline is a privately held company; its revenue model is drone-as-a-service contracts with healthcare systems, retailers, restaurant brands, and governments. There is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, GitHub organization, status page, changelog, or self-service developer portal — integrations with customer systems (order management, EHR, WMS, dispatch) are delivered as managed enterprise integrations rather than as a public programmable API.

providers.name: Avidbots
providers.description: Avidbots is a robotics company that designs and manufactures fully autonomous commercial floor-cleaning robots, including the Neo, Neo 2W, and Kas scrubbers, powered by its proprietary Avidbots Autonomy AI, lidar, and 3D sensing for real-time mapping, dynamic route planning, and intervention-free cleaning. Its robots serve airports, warehouses, retail, manufacturing, education, and healthcare facilities, and are managed through the web-based Avidbots Command Center. Avidbots was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Cyngn
providers.description: Cyngn (NASDAQ: CYN) is a Mountain View, California autonomous vehicle technology company that develops and deploys industrial autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for material handling. Its flagship DriveMod stack is a vehicle-agnostic, AI-powered autonomy system that retrofits onto standard industrial vehicles such as tuggers and forklifts, paired with the Cyngn Insight fleet-management, teleoperation, and analytics platform and the Cyngn Evolve data toolkit — together marketed as the Enterprise Autonomy Suite. Cyngn targets warehousing, manufacturing, and logistics operators facing labor shortages and safety challenges, and integrates with major warehouse management systems (Manhattan, Blue Yonder, SAP EWM). The company traces its corporate lineage to Cyanogen Inc. (the CyanogenMod company), whose dormant GitHub organization still links to cyngn.com.

providers.name: Pickle Robot Company
providers.description: Pickle Robot Company builds Physical AI robots for supply chain automation, focused on autonomously unloading non-palletized goods (floor-loaded boxes and parcels) from trucks and shipping containers at warehouse speed. Its Dill Autonomy Engine (DAE) combines classical optimal control with generative AI and machine vision so fleets improve continuously across deployments, with operational dashboards reporting picks-per-hour, unload times, and package-mix analysis. Customers include UPS and Cintas. Headquartered in the Boston, Massachusetts area, Pickle Robot is a DCVC portfolio company backed by investors including Teradyne Robotics Ventures, Toyota Ventures, Catapult Ventures, Hyperplane, and VersionOne. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation portal, or SDK; its GitHub organization hosts robotics tooling (mostly ROS/SLAM forks) rather than API client libraries.

providers.name: Sereact
