providers.description: Sereact GmbH is a Stuttgart, Germany based physical-AI company building intelligent robotic systems for warehouse and fulfillment automation. Its "Cortex" platform pairs a Vision Language Action Model (VLAM) with robot control so robots can pick, place, sort, induct, and inspect diverse items in production without task-specific retraining, running across 50+ deployments in Europe and the US. Products include Pick-and-Place, Putwall, Induction, Bin Handling, Returns Handling, and the Lens perception system. Backed by Creandum and Point Nine; announced a $110M Series B. Sereact does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, or documentation surface — an internal api.sereact.ai host exists but is a placeholder. This profile captures the company identity and public web/GitHub surface.

providers.name: Lyte
providers.description: Lyte is a Mountain View, California perception company building an end-to-end integrated vision system for robotics and Physical AI. Founded in 2021 by Alexander Shpunt, Arman Hajati and Yuval Gerson — architects of Apple's depth-sensing and Face ID perception stack, and, in Shpunt's case, co-founder and CTO of PrimeSense — the company emerged from stealth in January 2026 with $107M in aggregate funding from Fidelity Management & Research, Atreides Management, Exor Ventures, Key1 Capital, Avigdor Willenz's group and Venture Tech Alliance. Its flagship product, LyteVision, combines 4D sensing (distance plus velocity), RGB imaging and inertial motion awareness with custom silicon and software into a single plug-and-play perception platform for robots, mobility and next-generation automation; it won a CES 2026 Best of Innovation award in Robotics and was named an honoree in Vehicle Tech and Advanced Mobility. Lyte is collaborating with NVIDIA to stream perception into GPUs over Holoscan Sensor Bridge (zero-copy, Jetson Thor, CUDA, NITROS) and into Omniverse and Isaac Sim for real-time digital twins. Lyte ships hardware and an embedded perception stack rather than a developer platform, and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract as of this profile.

providers.name: BrainCo
providers.description: BrainCo is a Harvard-innovation-lab-founded neurotechnology company building non-invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) hardware and the developer SDKs that surround it. Its consumer and research line centers on wearable EEG headbands - Focus, Focus1 and FocusCalm - that measure attention and stress from brainwave signals for education, wellness and biofeedback, alongside the BrainRobotics neuroprosthetic hand and the Revo (Revo1/Revo2/Revo3) family of dexterous robotic hands for robotics and embodied-AI developers. BrainCo ships first-party SDKs rather than a public REST API: the Crimson SDK for its portable EEG devices (Node.js and native/BLE), the Focus SDK for headband brainwave measurement, and the Revo Hand SDKs (Python and C/C++, distributed on PyPI and GitHub) that speak RS-485, CAN 2.0A/CAN FD, EtherCAT and Protobuf, plus ROS 2 drivers and URDF/MJCF/USD simulation assets. The company is backed by IDG Capital and operates in the healthcare, neurotech, robotics and education-technology sectors.

providers.name: Covariant
providers.description: Covariant is an Emeryville, California warehouse-robotics AI company founded in 2017 (originally as Embodied Intelligence) by UC Berkeley professor Pieter Abbeel and his former students Peter Chen, Rocky Duan, and Tianhao Zhang. The company builds the Covariant Brain, a universal AI platform that enables industrial picking robots to handle virtually any SKU regardless of shape, size, or packaging, and in March 2024 it introduced RFM-1 (Robotics Foundation Model 1), an 8-billion-parameter multimodal transformer trained on text, images, video, robot actions, and numerical sensor readings to give robots human-like reasoning over the physical world. Covariant ships AI-powered solutions for order picking, sortation, item induction, kitting, depalletization, and goods-to-person workflows, delivered through long-running integration partnerships with KNAPP (Pick-it-Easy Robot, since 2020) and ABB (warehouse robotics, since 2020), as well as deployments with retailers and logistics providers worldwide. In August 2024, Amazon announced a non-exclusive license to Covariant's robotic foundation models and hired its three co-founders along with roughly a quarter of its workforce in a reverse-acquihire arrangement; Covariant continues to operate independently under COO-turned-CEO Ted Stinson and co-founder Tianhao Zhang. The Covariant Brain and RFM-1 are proprietary, deployed on-premise on partner robotics hardware, and the company has no public developer API, SDK, open-source release, or third-party developer program.

providers.name: Tera-ai
providers.description: Tera AI is a San Francisco-based robotics AI company (founded 2023, out of stealth March 2025 with $7.8M seed co-led by Felicis and Inovia) that builds the first unified, software-only spatial reasoning stack for camera-based mapping and navigation across air, onroad, offroad, and sea platforms. Its foundation-model approach delivers GPS-denied, manufacturer-interoperable autonomy that runs on a robot's existing camera and onboard GPU. Tera publishes research (TARDIS/STRIDE) and technical field results but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; this profile captures its public web, research, and GitHub surface.

providers.name: Zimmer Biomet
providers.description: Zimmer Biomet is a global medical technology company that designs, manufactures, and markets orthopedic reconstructive products, sports medicine, biologics, extremities, trauma products, dental implants, and related surgical products. The company is a Fortune 500 organization with operations in over 25 countries and a portfolio of digital and robotic technologies including ZBEdge Dynamic Intelligence, ROSA Robotics, the mymobility patient app, Persona Knee, and ZBEdge Analytics. Zimmer Biomet does not currently publish a public REST API developer portal; its digital platforms are surfaced through partner integrations, hospital systems, and proprietary devices.

providers.name: Aerodyne
providers.description: Aerodyne Group is a Malaysia-headquartered DT3 (drone technology, data technology, and digital transformation) enterprise solutions provider, founded in 2014. Through its Drone-as-a-Service (DaaS) model and the AI-powered, cloud-based vertikaliti asset-management platform, Aerodyne turns aerial and sensor data into deep analytics and actionable insights for infrastructure, power line, wind turbine, solar, and agricultural (Agrimor) asset inspection and management. Operating across 45 countries with a global network of AeroRangers, it was ranked the world's number-one drone service provider by Drone Industry Insights in 2021 and 2022. Aerodyne is a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer portal, API, or machine-readable specification has been identified at this time.

providers.name: Allen Control Systems
providers.description: Allen Control Systems is a defense technology company building autonomous precision weapon stations that detect, track, and neutralize unmanned aerial systems (drones) for military and partner forces. Its Bullfrog family of robotic gun mounts (M240C, M2, M230, M134) pairs passive machine-vision drone detection with autonomous fire-control targeting, synthetic training-data generation, and low-collateral engagement options such as laser dazzlers and composite rounds. The systems use an open architecture to integrate with command-and-control platforms. Backed by Craft Ventures, the company is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a defense-sector provider; it publishes no public developer API, portal, or specification at this time.

providers.name: Brumby
providers.description: Brumby (formerly GrazeMate) is a Y Combinator-backed (W2026) precision-grazing company based in Sydney, Australia, building an autonomous drone toolkit for cattle ranchers. Brumby drones plan routes and move herds with gentle, AI-guided pressure, fly scheduled monitoring missions that locate and count every animal, measure standing dry-matter pasture biomass from the air, and inspect water troughs, tanks and fences on every flight — all managed from a single phone app that works online or in a local base-station mode without connectivity. The company is running pilot programs and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, or documentation; this profile is a company lead maintained in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Connected Robotics
providers.description: Connected Robotics Inc. is a Japanese foodtech startup, founded in 2014 by Tetsuya Sawanobori and headquartered in Koganei, Tokyo, that develops specialized robotics and AI systems to automate labor-intensive work across food factories and restaurants. Its product line pairs AI image-processing and robot-control technology with purpose-built machines including the Delibot S plating robot, Delibot X filling robot, AI inspection software, a soft-serve ice-cream robot, and a french-fry cooking robot, targeting labor shortages, productivity, and food safety. The company has raised multiple rounds (including a July 2019 Series A led by Global Brain and a Series B closed in 2023 with strategic investors such as Yaskawa Electric, Hoshizaki, and Mitsubishi HC Capital) and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. As a hardware and robotics manufacturer, Connected Robotics publishes no public web API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Crewline
providers.description: Crewline is an autonomous heavy-equipment company that retrofits existing construction machinery to operate self-driving. Its hardware retrofit kit installs on-site in about an hour and adds autonomy to drum rollers today (compatible with Caterpillar, Bomag, Hamm, Volvo, and CASE), with dozers on the 2027 roadmap and rock trucks, excavators, motor graders, and wheel loaders in development. It is offered on a subscription model with zero upfront cost, a fixed monthly rate per machine, and 24/7 technical support, targeting earthworks and grading crews. Crewline is backed by Initialized Capital and headquartered in San Francisco. It publishes no public API or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Cron Systems
providers.description: Cron Systems (now operating as Cron AI) builds deep-learning perception software for 3D sensor and LiDAR data. Its flagship platform, senseEDGE, performs real-time 3D object detection, classification, and tracking from point-cloud data at the edge, with multi-sensor fusion and adverse-weather resilience. The technology serves intelligent transportation systems, smart infrastructure, autonomous mobility, smart cities, and security and surveillance — powering use cases such as traffic management, autonomous tolling, crowd and queue management, smart parking, vehicle counting, and airport and aircraft-movement monitoring. Object output is emitted as JSON and Flatbuffers binary over WebSocket, with a web-based configuration and visualizer utility, VPN and PTP time-synchronization support, and a privacy-preserving, GDPR-compliant design. Cron AI was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Cx2
providers.description: CX2 is a defense technology company building AI-enabled electromagnetic spectrum (electronic warfare) systems for the tactical edge. Founded in 2024 and headquartered in El Segundo, California, CX2 develops attritable, machine-learning-powered hardware and software that detect, disrupt, and geolocate RF threats across land, air, sea, and space. Its flagship products are Wraith, a roughly 32-pound autonomous airborne EW platform that geolocates and identifies hostile emitters such as jammers and radars in GPS-denied environments, and Vadris, an RF-seeking payload for FPV drones that hunts ground control stations and other emitters of interest. CX2 is backed by 8VC, Point72 Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, and others, and sells directly to military and government customers. It does not currently publish a public API or developer portal.

providers.name: Fernride
providers.description: FERNRIDE (FERNRIDE GmbH) is a Munich, Germany based ground-autonomy company delivering human-assisted autonomous driving for logistics. Its platform automates electric and diesel trucks and terminal tractors across container terminals, yard operations, manufacturing supply, defence logistics, and open-road trucking, pairing on-vehicle autonomy with remote human oversight (teleoperation) for reliability at scale. A centralized Management Suite lets fleet managers monitor and control the autonomous fleet and integrates with existing terminal operating systems (TOS) and yard management systems (YMS). Customers and partners have included DB Schenker, Volkswagen, HHLA, and NVIDIA. FERNRIDE was acquired by Quantum Systems in December 2025. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest; the company exposes no public developer portal, API, or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Mach Industries
providers.description: Mach Industries develops and manufactures asymmetric aerospace and defense systems and components at scale, with a product portfolio that includes the Viper vertical-takeoff attack drone, the Glide precision strike munition, the Stratos high-altitude pseudo-satellite, the Pike long-range munition, the Dart counter-drone kinetic interceptor, and energetics testing services. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Ribbit Capital and added to the API Evangelist network. The company is a defense hardware manufacturer and publishes no public developer or API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: MeetFuture Technology
providers.description: MeetFuture Technology (弥费科技) is a Shanghai-based, global-leading supplier of semiconductor Automated Material Handling Systems (AMHS) and core components, founded in 2014. It designs and manufactures overhead hoist transport (OHT), stocker/storage, purge, and AMHS control-software solutions for semiconductor wafer fabrication plants, integrating with fab MES systems over SEMI equipment communication standards (E37/HSMS, E30/GEM, E82, E84, E10). MeetFuture holds 300+ intellectual-property items, operates China's largest AMHS cleanroom test center, authored China's first semiconductor OHT standard (T/SICA 006—2024), and won the 2025 SEMI Product Innovation Award. It is a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company. MeetFuture is an industrial semiconductor-equipment maker and does not publish a public web API, developer portal, or SDKs; this profile is maintained for network identity and discovery.

providers.name: Orqa
providers.description: Orqa is an aerial robotics company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Osijek, Croatia, that designs and manufactures mission-ready FPV (first-person view) drone systems for the defense and enterprise markets. With full vertical integration, Orqa builds every component in-house — tactical drones such as the MRM1-5 and MRM2-10, FPV goggles (FPV.One Pilot), controllers, simulators, and detection equipment — to keep its supply chain secure and its systems high-performance. The company is ISO 9001 certified and backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners (Seed round, 2024, partners Antoine Moyroud and Alexander Schmitt). As of this profile Orqa is a hardware manufacturer and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a programmatic developer surface; this repository tracks it for identity and network completeness.

providers.name: Overland AI
providers.description: Overland AI is a Seattle- and Washington, DC-based defense technology company building autonomous ground vehicle systems for military and national-security applications. Its product line spans ULTRA (a fully autonomous tactical vehicle with modular payloads), OverDrive (an off-road autonomy stack for tactical maneuver in GPS- and comms-denied environments), OverWatch (a command-and-control platform for single-operator control of multiple ground vehicles, which the company describes as offering an open API for integration with existing C2 systems), and SPARK (modular hardware that adds autonomous mobility to existing platforms). Overland AI is a portfolio company of 8VC. The company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI specification; its "open API" is referenced only in marketing material and integration is handled through direct contact.

providers.name: PopCom
providers.description: PopCom is an AI-powered automated retail technology company founded by e-commerce entrepreneur Dawn Dickson. Its flagship product, the PopShop, is a robotic self-service kiosk that dispenses physical and digital products while capturing customer data through computer vision, facial recognition, and real-time analytics. The platform gives brands and entrepreneurs the kind of sales metrics, inventory monitoring, targeted advertising, and customer-sentiment insight that online retailers enjoy, but for physical, unattended retail. PopCom sells its hardware on an annual lease with a monthly software subscription. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass PopCom publishes no public developer platform, API, or specification.

providers.name: Vermeer
providers.description: Vermeer is an American-Ukrainian defense-technology startup (founded 2018 by Brian Streem; headquartered in New York with forward operations in Kyiv) building vision-based autonomy for unmanned aerial platforms. Its Visual Positioning System (VPS) uses electro-optical and infrared cameras plus onboard AI (NVIDIA) to match imagery to 2D/3D maps and deliver precise navigation in GPS-denied, jammed, or spoofed environments. Products include Air (absolute positioning without GPS), Celestial (star-based navigation), and Terminal Guidance (precision targeting). The technology has been fielded by the Armed Forces of Ukraine and is aimed at defense customers including Lockheed Martin, General Atomics, Northrop Grumman, and the U.S. Air Force and Army. Vermeer exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time; this profile is a company/marketing surface with no API artifacts.

providers.name: Acacus Group
providers.description: Acacus Group (Acacus Technologies) is a Dubai-headquartered mobility technology company founded in 2013 that builds artificial-intelligence and machine-learning software for the transportation and airline industries. Its Lynx product family — Lynx, Lynx Pro and Lynx Vision — provides intelligent fleet management, optimized dispatch built on mathematical combinatorics, disruption management, telematics and vehicle diagnostics, and deep-learning video analytics from in-vehicle cameras covering driver fatigue, lane departure, tailgating and passenger counting. Acacus also develops autonomous vehicle technology and Peregrine, an optimization solution for airline crew and airport operations. It won Best Global Startup at GITEX 2016 in Dubai and signed an MOU with Dubai Police for driverless patrol vehicles. Lynx sells as an enterprise SaaS subscription through a demo request; Acacus publishes no public developer program or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Cartwheel
providers.description: Cartwheel is a generative motion platform for games, film & TV, advertising, and robotics. It gives creators a new way to animate 3D characters — turning ordinary video into clean, usable character motion (video-to-motion), and posing and rendering characters as images in any visual style. Cartwheel is delivered as a hosted web studio (studio.getcartwheel.com) with exportable animation formats for downstream 3D, game, film, and social pipelines. The product is in private beta and is backed by Accel, Craft Ventures, and Menlo Ventures. At this time Cartwheel exposes no public developer/REST API; this profile captures its public web, documentation, and security surface.

providers.name: Gatik
providers.description: Gatik is an autonomous trucking company founded in 2017 by Gautam Narang, Arjun Narang and Apeksha Kumavat, headquartered in Silicon Valley, California. Gatik builds and operates the Gatik Driver, an SAE Level 4 autonomy system purpose-built for the middle mile: short-haul, repeatable freight routes between distribution centers, dark stores and retail endpoints. Gatik runs driverless medium-duty box trucks in commercial service for Fortune 50 retailers and grocers including Walmart, Loblaw, Kroger, Tyson Foods, Pitney Bowes and PepsiCo, across Texas, Arkansas, Arizona, Ontario and other North American markets. The company partners with Isuzu, Ryder, Goodyear and NVIDIA, runs the Gatik Arena simulation platform, and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK or developer portal — its surface is a corporate marketing site plus a legacy archive site carrying about, safety, news, careers and legal pages.

providers.name: Efference AI
providers.description: Efference AI is a robotics perception and compute company building the hardware-plus-software foundation for data-driven robotics at scale. Founded in 2025 by Gianluca Bencomo and based in San Francisco (Y Combinator Fall 2025), Efference treats machine vision as a software problem, pairing affordable stereo-camera hardware with learned 3D-perception foundation models ("cheap hardware + great algorithms"). Its M1 device targets distributed, robotics-grade data collection at scale, while the H1 stereo system is built for real-time cloud inference with foundation models. The company serves autonomous vehicles, humanoid robots, and drones, and publishes hardware-interfacing documentation and firmware through its GitHub organization. As of this profile Efference exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or authenticated service surface.

providers.name: EverestLabs
providers.description: EverestLabs builds AI, computer vision, and robotics for the recycling industry. Its RecycleOS platform identifies, tracks, and sorts recoverable materials on the conveyor lines of Materials Recovery Facilities (MRFs), giving recyclers, reclaimers, and packaging manufacturers analytics, bale tracing, plant optimization, and compliance reporting to increase recovery rates, cut labor costs, and verify recycled content. Headquartered in Fremont, California and backed by Sierra Ventures. EverestLabs does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web, GitHub, and discovery surface.

providers.name: Firestorm
providers.description: Firestorm (Firestorm Labs, Inc.) is a San Diego based defense technology company founded in 2022 that builds expeditionary manufacturing systems and modular unmanned aerial systems. Its xCELL containerized production unit uses HP Multi Jet Fusion additive manufacturing to 3D print industrial-grade PA-12 nylon composite airframes and spare parts at the tactical edge, feeding modular UAS platforms including the Tempest fixed-wing family and the Squall FPV drone. The company holds a five-year, $100M U.S. Air Force IDIQ and closed an $82M Series B in April 2026 led by Washington Harbour Partners. Firestorm ships hardware, not software: as of this profiling pass it publishes no developer portal, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Blendid
providers.description: Blendid operates fully autonomous robotic smoothie kiosks that prepare chef-created blended beverages from real whole fruits, vegetables, seeds, nuts, and juice with no artificial flavors or added sugar. Each kiosk uses AI and robotics to run without on-site staff, taking mobile-app orders with customization and payment, producing up to eight simultaneous drinks and roughly thirty per hour. Blendid deploys its Blendid M2 platform into retail, colleges and universities, health clubs, and hospitals as a low-labor, low-capex, 24/7 automated food-service offering. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Partech in the Food & Agritech sector; the company publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Dotterel
providers.description: Dotterel Technologies is an Auckland, New Zealand acoustics and audio-hardware company founded in 2015 out of the Callaghan Innovation C-Prize. It began by solving drone noise, building acoustic shrouds, low-noise propellers, and onboard active audio-recording systems for UAVs used in film, security, and noise mapping. That work led to Konos (now marketed as Konos Digital), an 80-element directional MEMS microphone array with a continuously variable 60-300 degree beam width that streams four channels of AES67 / SMPTE ST 2110 audio over a single Power-over-Ethernet cable, targeting film, broadcast, and live-sports production. The microphone exposes a firmware-updatable on-device HTTP control interface (a web page plus a POST control endpoint for beam steering) rather than a public developer web API. Dotterel is backed by Techstars (Adelaide 2017 cohort) and is tracked here as a hardware company; it publishes no public API specification, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: KEENON Robotics
providers.description: KEENON Robotics is a global commercial service-robotics company founded in 2010 and headquartered in Shanghai, China, designing and manufacturing autonomous service robots deployed across more than 70 countries and 600+ cities. Its product lines span catering and delivery robots (the T-series and W3), the KLEENBOT commercial floor-cleaning range (C20/C30/C40/C55), heavy-load delivery robots (S100/S300), humanoid service robots (XMAN-R1/XMAN-F1), hospital and hotel logistics solutions (including the WITMED medical line), and the Keenmow K1 domestic robot. KEENON is a hardware-and-solutions company; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. This record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Trucks Venture Fund I
providers.description: Trucks Venture Capital (Trucks VC) is an early-stage venture firm headquartered in San Francisco investing in companies building the future of transportation — making mobility decarbonized, safer, and more accessible. Its focus spans autonomous vehicles, electric aviation, agricultural robotics, fleet management, and mobility infrastructure. Trucks Venture Fund I is the firm's first fund; notable portfolio outcomes include Joby Aviation (NYSE: JOBY), Bear Flag Robotics (acquired by John Deere), nuTonomy (acquired by Delphi), Roadster (acquired by CDK Global), and Zendrive (acquired by Intuit). Surfaced as a portfolio relation of 500 Global and profiled in the API Evangelist network as a venture-capital firm; it publishes a marketing/portfolio website but no developer API surface.

providers.name: Zeromatter
providers.description: Zeromatter is a deep-tech simulation platform that lets teams build, test, and train autonomous systems in one environment. It provides high-performance sensor simulation, automatic environment generation, and multi-agent co-simulation frameworks used to accelerate development across autonomy, aerospace, automotive, agriculture, drones, and green energy. Backed by Spark Capital, Zeromatter currently exposes a marketing and company site only; no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs were found during enrichment. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a lead pending any future public API surface.

providers.name: Airforestry
providers.description: AirForestry is a Swedish climate-technology company developing autonomous electric drones that perform forest thinning from the air. Its system pairs AI and computer vision for tree identification and selection with a lightweight aerial harvesting tool, letting a fleet of drones fell and extract trees without ground machinery. The result is forestry with zero soil compaction, no root damage and no machine tracks, higher operational efficiency, and lower emissions than conventional harvesters, while increasing forest growth and carbon sequestration. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. It currently publishes a marketing and news presence but no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Apptronik
providers.description: Apptronik is an Austin, Texas-based humanoid robotics company founded in 2016 as a spinout from the Human Centered Robotics Lab at the University of Texas at Austin. Co-founded by Jeff Cardenas (CEO), Dr. Nick Paine (CTO), and Dr. Luis Sentis (scientific advisor), the company designs and manufactures Apollo, a general-purpose humanoid robot standing 5'8", weighing 160 lbs, capable of lifting 55 lbs, and running for roughly 4 hours on a swappable battery. Apollo targets warehouse, manufacturing, and logistics applications including trailer unloading, case picking, palletization, machine tending, and workcell delivery. Apptronik has commercial pilot programs and partnerships with Mercedes-Benz (automotive manufacturing logistics), GXO Logistics (multi-phase R&D in U.S. distribution centers), Jabil (supply-chain partner helping scale production and an internal Apollo deployment), and Google DeepMind (Apollo integrates Gemini Robotics vision-language-action models). The company previously built NASA's Valkyrie humanoid and ten-plus other research robots. As of February 2026 Apptronik had raised more than $935M (including a $520M Series A-X extension) at a reported $5B valuation, with investors including B Capital, Google, and Mercedes-Benz. The company sells/leases Apollo to enterprise customers via a direct contact-sales motion and ships a proprietary "point-and-click" control suite for deploying solutions; there is no public developer portal, no published REST/AsyncAPI/gRPC API, no public SDK, no open-source release, and no public GitHub repositories under the `apptronik` org.

providers.name: Apex.AI
providers.description: Apex.AI is an embedded and autonomous software company whose tagline is "software that moves," focused on safe, real-time, software-defined systems (SDx) for automotive, robotics, and other safety-critical embedded platforms. Its product line includes Apex.Grace (deterministic embedded execution framework, an automotive-grade evolution of ROS 2), Apex.Ida (high-speed fault-tolerant middleware for sensor, compute, and cloud connectivity), Apex.OS for V&V (data recording and replay for validating autonomous systems), and Apex.Alan (automated tooling and CI/CD workflows for safe software development at scale). Apex.AI also provides technical assessment, architecture, embedded and cloud software development, CI/CD pipeline, and ROS 1 to ROS 2 migration services. The company is a maintainer of substantial ROS 2 and embedded middleware open source. It is backed by Canaan Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Apex.AI publishes no public developer REST API at this time.

providers.name: Aseon Labs
providers.description: Aseon Labs builds robotic pitstops for self-driving cars — distributed robotic micro-depots (the "Aseon Pod") that automate charging, interior and exterior cleaning, and inspection for autonomous vehicle fleets directly within their operating zones, so vehicles reset locally instead of returning to centralized facilities. The company says the approach can cut reset costs by up to 50%, reduce downtime by ~65%, and add $50,000+ in annual revenue per vehicle. Founded in 2026 and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026 batch), the Redwood City, CA startup is a physical-infrastructure and robotics company; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Asylon
providers.description: Asylon Robotics is an American-made robotic security company founded in 2015 and headquartered in Norristown, Pennsylvania, that automates physical perimeter security with autonomous drones, ground robots, software, and AI. Its flagship products include the Guardian automated security drone (the most widely used automated security drone system, with tens of thousands of patrol and alarm-response missions completed), the DroneDog quadruped ground robot built on Boston Dynamics Spot with the Asylon DogHouse charging enclosure and PupPack cellular PTZ payload, and DroneIQ, the Robotic Security Operations Center (RSOC) and software platform that coordinates robotic assets, fixed surveillance, and human operators. DroneIQ exposes an open-architecture integration layer for third-party alarms and sensors (radar, smart fences, Bosch alarm panels, gun-detection computer vision, Genetec), but the company publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs; API and integration access is arranged directly with Asylon. Asylon raised a $26M Series B in July 2025 led by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Drone Racing League
providers.description: The Drone Racing League (DRL) is a New York-based professional drone racing property founded in 2015 by Nicholas Horbaczewski, staging first-person-view (FPV) races in which pilots fly identical, league-built quadcopters - the Racer series - through three-dimensional courses in stadiums, arenas and landmark venues at speeds above 80 mph. DRL designs its own racing drones, timing and telemetry hardware, produces and distributes its race broadcasts across NBC, Sky Sports, ProSiebenSat.1 and streaming platforms, and operates the DRL Simulator, an FPV racing game on Steam, PlayStation and Xbox that feeds the Swatch DRL Tryouts esports pipeline used to recruit professional pilots. The company was acquired by Infinite Reality (now Napster) in April 2024. DRL publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specification, and as of the 2026-08-04 enrichment pass its primary web properties (thedroneracingleague.com, drl.io) were not completing a TLS handshake.

providers.name: Teradar
providers.description: Teradar is a Boston, Massachusetts semiconductor and sensing company founded in 2020 by Matthew Carey, Gregory Charvat and Nicholas Saiz that is commercializing terahertz-band vision sensors for vehicles, defense and security screening. Its Modular Terahertz Engine (MTE) is an all-solid-state chip architecture built from proprietary transmit (TX), receive (RX) and Teracore processing silicon, delivering 0.13-degree native angular resolution at 300+ meters in day, night, rain, fog and snow, positioned to sit alongside cameras and to displace radar and lidar in SAE L1-L5 driver assistance and autonomy programs. The company emerged from stealth in late 2025 with a $150M Series B led by VXI Capital with Ibex Investors, Capricorn Investment Group, The Engine Ventures and Lockheed Martin Ventures, and is working with global OEMs and Tier-One suppliers toward a 2028 model-year launch. Teradar is a hardware and silicon company: it publishes a marketing site and product specification sheets, but no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: Mips
providers.description: MIPS is a processor IP and compute company building embedded and edge AI silicon for automotive, robotics, and mission-critical systems. Its portfolio spans the MIPS RISC-V CPU families (M8500, I8500, P8700, S8200), the ARC processor and NPX/VPX accelerator lines, and development tooling such as MIPS Atlas Explorer virtual platforms and the ASIP Designer / ASIP Programmer toolchains. MIPS frames its offering around a "Sense, Think, Act, Communicate" signal chain for real-time autonomy — what it calls Physical AI at the edge. MIPS is a semiconductor IP licensor rather than a public web-API provider; this profile was surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company and enriched with identity and probed security posture.

providers.name: Path Robotics
providers.description: Path Robotics is a Columbus, Ohio autonomous welding robotics company founded in 2018 by brothers Andy and Alex Lonsberry (CEO and CTO) out of Case Western Reserve University. The company builds AI-powered intelligent welding cells that automate metal fabrication for defense shipyards, utility and energy infrastructure, data centers, and heavy industry. Its core technology is Obsidian, a physical-AI reinforcement-learning agent trained inside Path's proprietary Weld World Model on tens of millions of welded inches; Obsidian runs at the edge of each cell and makes real-time, seam-by-seam welding decisions using a sensor stack of two cameras plus four lasers that deliver sub-millimeter 360-degree awareness around the torch. Path markets the cells with a CapEx-free consumption model and reports 97%+ first-pass yield, 4x productivity, and 30% lower welding costs across customers including HII (America's largest military shipbuilder), Saronic, LAD Services, Tycrop, Mine Rite Technologies, and Millerbernd. In April 2026 Path announced Rove, a mobile welding system mounted on a quadruped platform, extending its addressable geometry beyond fixed-cell applications. The company has raised approximately $271M across Seed through Series D from Drive Capital, Matter Venture Partners, Tiger Global, Addition, and Yamaha Motor Ventures, with the most recent $100M Series D closing in October 2024. Path Robotics has no public developer API, SDK, or webhook surface; its GitHub organization contains roughly 50 repositories that are almost entirely upstream open-source forks (ROS, protobuf, abseil, ceres-solver, pytorch3d, etc.) used as internal build dependencies rather than published developer artifacts. Revenue is earned through welding-cell deployments, services, and the consumable weld-output model — not API monetization.

providers.name: Agrist
providers.description: AGRIST Inc. (AGRIST株式会社) is a Japanese deep-tech agricultural robotics company founded in October 2019 and headquartered in Shintomi-cho, Koyu-gun, Miyazaki Prefecture, with an AI robot farm in Higashikushira (Kagoshima), an AI robot test facility in Shintomi-cho and the AGRIST Joso Farm in Joso City, Ibaraki. Its flagship product is "L", an automatic bell-pepper harvesting robot that travels along overhead wires strung between greenhouse rows rather than on ground rails, using multiple cameras and a proprietary computer-vision model to find and cut harvest-ready fruit through layered foliage; a cucumber harvesting robot followed. Around the hardware the company sells AGRIST Ai, a greenhouse cultivation-support and yield-forecasting system fed by robot patrol data and environmental sensors, and it operates its own farms plus Smart Agri University (SAU), a nine-month smart-agriculture training program. AGRIST is venture-backed through a Series B that includes Mizuho Capital, Global Infrastructure Management, Nippon Steel Kowa Real Estate, Nippon Express Holdings, Takamiya and Sparx, and has taken more than 27 domestic and international awards including a CES 2023 Innovation Award and a Japanese Minister of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries Award. It is a robotics and farm-operations business, not a software vendor: as of 2026-09-13 it publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Aurelius Systems
providers.description: Aurelius Systems is a defense technology company building autonomous directed-energy laser defense platforms for counter-unmanned-aerial-system (C-UAS) missions. Its flagship product, Archimedes, fuses high-power lasers, advanced optical sensing, and AI-guided autonomous tracking into a compact, field-deployable platform that detects, tracks, and neutralizes Group 1 and Group 2 drone threats at the speed of light and a fraction of the cost of traditional interceptors. The system runs on grid, generator, or commercial off-the-shelf batteries, is designed to operate without human operators, and can be networked into modular defensive grids to protect troops, bases, and critical infrastructure. Founded in 2025 by Michael LaFramboise and John Marmaduke, the company raised a $10M seed round co-led by General Catalyst and Draper Associates and is partnered with American Rheinmetall. Aurelius currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or software developer surface — it is a directed-energy hardware company.

providers.name: Birdstop
providers.description: Birdstop is an American autonomous-drone and remote-sensing company that lets organizations monitor and inspect field assets at scale without personnel onsite. Its Fealty system is an all-weather, always-on drone that launches in under three seconds, flies for up to 45 minutes, cruises at 45 mph, and patrols 24/7 across public safety, utilities, transportation, construction, and data-center sites. Birdstop pairs networked UAVs and ground stations with computer vision and a patented optical/acoustic detect-and-avoid system to enable safe beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight under some of the FAA's most advanced approvals, delivering Observation-on-Demand intel over the internet. The company is FAA-authorized, SOC 2 certified, and NDAA compliant, and builds its drones in Detroit. Backed by Techstars, Birdstop currently exposes no public developer API; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Blue River Technology
providers.description: Blue River Technology is an agricultural robotics and machine-learning company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and a wholly owned subsidiary of John Deere (Deere & Company), which acquired it in 2017. Founded in 2011 by Jorge Heraud and Lee Redden out of Stanford University, the company builds intelligent machinery that combines computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and full-stack software to make farming more precise and sustainable. Its flagship product, See & Spray, uses onboard cameras and deep-learning models to distinguish crops from weeds in real time and target herbicide only where it is needed, dramatically reducing chemical use. Blue River operates as John Deere's autonomy and computer-vision engineering hub, applying the same perception and edge-AI stack across agriculture, construction, and mining equipment. The company does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; its technology ships embedded in John Deere machinery and is surfaced to growers through John Deere Operations Center rather than a standalone developer program.

providers.name: Elementary
providers.description: Elementary is an AI-powered machine-vision inspection company for manufacturing, founded in 2017 in South Pasadena, California (originally Elementary Robotics). Its VisionStream self-training edge AI detects production defects in seconds without rules, labeling, or tuning, while the QualityOS cloud platform delivers traceability, analytics, and MES/ERP integration across production lines. Elementary inspects over one billion parts annually for Fortune 500 manufacturers across food & beverage, automotive, consumer packaged goods, electronics, and life sciences, and is backed by Rockwell Automation, Tiger Global, Toyota Ventures, Threshold Ventures, Fika Ventures, and Idealab. The company exposes no public developer API; this profile captures its identity, security posture, and public web properties.

providers.name: Flexion
providers.description: Flexion Robotics builds the autonomy stack for humanoid robots — from command to control, from manipulation to locomotion, across any hardware and task. Founded by former NVIDIA and ETH Zurich reinforcement-learning researchers (Nikita Rudin, David Höller, Julian Nubert), the Zurich- and San Francisco-based company uses large-scale simulation and reinforcement learning to train generalizable robot policies that transfer to real-world hardware. Its Flexion Reflect model line targets long-horizon autonomous humanoid work. The company raised $50M and is backed by Prosus Ventures. Flexion does not currently expose a public developer API.

providers.name: Kiva Systems (Amazon Robotics since 2012)
providers.description: Kiva Systems was a warehouse robotics company founded in 2003 that pioneered the goods-to-person mobile fulfillment model, in which fleets of low-profile drive units lift and carry mobile storage pods to human pick stations instead of moving workers to static shelving. Amazon acquired Kiva Systems in March 2012 for approximately US$775 million and renamed it Amazon Robotics in 2015. Since the acquisition the technology has been developed exclusively for Amazon's own fulfillment and sortation network and is no longer sold to third parties. Amazon Robotics publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs; amazonrobotics.com now redirects to Amazon's internal identity provider and kivasystems.com no longer resolves. This profile is retained as a historical and acquisition record in the physical-AI and warehouse-robotics space rather than as an integratable API provider. Not to be confused with AWS RoboMaker or AWS IoT RoboRunner, which are AWS product APIs.

providers.name: newmo
providers.description: newmo (newmo株式会社, "ニューモ") is a Japanese mobility company with the mission "移動で地域をカラフルに" — coloring regions through movement. It modernizes regional transportation through a consumer ride-hailing app and taxi service (newmo-taxi.jp), driver recruitment and dispatch, and its newmo Autonomy initiative (newmo.ai), which since 2025 has run Level 4 autonomous-driving taxi trials spanning safety, remote monitoring, operations design, and vehicle integration. newmo is a consumer transportation service rather than a developer/API platform; probing found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or well-known discovery surface. Backed by DCM Ventures.

providers.name: Nimble Robotics
providers.description: Nimble Robotics (Nimble) is an autonomous robotic third-party logistics (3PL) company building AI-powered robots that pick, pack, and fulfill ecommerce orders with minimal human intervention. Founded by Simon Kalouche, the company operates fully autonomous robotic fulfillment centers and is training general-purpose robot AI to power fast, economical commerce. Backed by Accel and partnered with FedEx, Nimble raised a $106M Series C at a $1B valuation, with board member Marc Raibert (Boston Dynamics founder). Nimble is a physical robotics and logistics operator and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: RIVR
providers.description: RIVR (RIVR Technologies AG, formerly Swiss-Mile) is a Swiss robotics and AI company spun out of ETH Zurich that develops autonomous legged-wheeled robots for doorstep delivery across parcel, grocery, and instant food/convenience segments. RIVR pursues "General Physical AI" by combining large-scale reinforcement learning in simulation with real-world self-supervised learning from live delivery operations, owning the full stack from software to hardware for reliability, safety, and cost efficiency. The company operates commercial deployments with partners including Just Eat Takeaway.com, Swiss Post, Migros Online, Evri, and Veho, and is backed by investors including Hongshan and Bezos Expeditions. This profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network company record; RIVR publishes no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Savion Aerospace
providers.description: Savion Aerospace (FlySavion) is an aerospace company developing sustainable, zero-emissions aviation technology. Its flagship SavionJet is an autonomous blended-wing-body (ABWB) aircraft with a standup cabin and satellite-based piloting via proprietary autonomous flight software, and the company offers Zero-Emissions Flight Credits (ZFCs) as a subscription for organizations seeking carbon-free air travel beyond offsetting. Savion demonstrated a cryogenic LNG-fueled flight in 2019 and is a 500 Global (500 Startups) and Alchemist Accelerator portfolio company. The company operates as an aviation hardware and services business and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Third Dimension AI
providers.description: Third Dimension AI is a spatial-generation company building high-fidelity 3D worlds and simulation for embodied AI, autonomy, robotics, gaming, and entertainment. Its core product, SuperSim, models the world across the full fidelity spectrum - from real-world reconstruction of scenes captured from sensor data to open-ended generative simulation - so autonomy teams can validate, train, and deploy AI systems and close the simulation-to-reality domain gap without hand-built 3D art. Founded by Tolga Kart (CEO) and Piotr Sokolski (CTO), with Oxford professor Christian Rupprecht as Chief Researcher, the team draws on experience from Wayve, Tesla, Google, Luma AI, Nvidia, Niantic, Amazon, and Unity. The company raised $7 million and is backed by Felicis. As of this profile it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; enrichment captured its identity and probed its domain security posture.

providers.name: Waabi
providers.description: Waabi is a Toronto-based artificial intelligence company founded in 2021 by Raquel Urtasun, pioneering Physical AI for autonomous driving and starting with self-driving trucks. Its flagship product, the Waabi Driver, pairs a generative-AI, end-to-end interpretable and verifiable autonomy stack with sensors and compute, trained and validated in Waabi World, a high-fidelity neural closed-loop simulator, and designed for factory-level OEM integration and large-scale commercialization. Waabi is a product/technology company: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal, so this profile carries identity and domain-security signal rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Urban Machine
providers.description: Urban Machine is a GV-backed robotics company building AI and computer-vision powered machines that remove metal fasteners (nails, staples, and screws) from construction and demolition lumber waste, reclaiming it for premium wood products and circular-economy reuse. The company publishes no public API, but maintains an open-source ROS/Python robotics tooling footprint on GitHub, including the colcon-poetry-ros package on PyPI.

providers.name: Addionics
providers.description: Addionics is a Smart Metals manufacturer headquartered in London, United Kingdom, with operations in Israel, Korea and the USA, building Smart 3D Porous Current Collectors that replace the flat copper and aluminium foils inside a battery cell with a porous, ion-permeable metal architecture. The technology is chemistry-agnostic and drop-in, produced roll-to-roll on existing coating lines, and is sold into robotics, defence, space and EV programmes. Addionics is a hardware and materials company: it operates no developer program and publishes no API, SDK, webhook or machine-readable API contract. It does run a deliberate agent-readable content surface on its own domain — a served /llms.txt digest, a published /agents.md agent guide, a markdown twin of every page under Accept: text/markdown, a complete /sitemap.xml and an RSS blog feed — all captured in this profile.

providers.name: Aeon Industrial
providers.description: Aeon Industrial is an American defense technology company, founded in 2023 and headquartered in the Austin, Texas area, that designs and manufactures affordable precision tactical weapon systems. Its two named products are ODIN, an autonomous precision targeting software package that observes, detects, interrogates and neutralizes threats and is advertised as an open architecture installable on third-party hardware, and Zeus, a modular software-defined tactical missile system powered by ODIN. The company is vertically integrated, building in-house from commercially available American-made components, and sells to U.S. and allied defense customers. Aeon publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification; its only public machine-readable documents are the OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 discovery files served by its own WorkOS AuthKit identity host for its login-gated partner portal.

providers.name: Avea Robotics
providers.description: Avea Robotics is a San Francisco-based robotics software company (Y Combinator Spring 2026) building teleoperation software that lets operators control robots from anywhere in the world with ultra-low latency. Its product, Sentinel, provides real-time remote control, immersive viewing, haptic feedback, and multi-stream video so operators can remotely intervene and keep robots running continuously. The platform supports industrial robotic arms, humanoid robots, and custom systems, and targets use cases such as data collection for Physical AI training, remote real-world robot deployment, and supervised autonomy with human oversight. Integration is handled during onboarding by sharing a robot's URDF and joint control API rather than through a public developer API. As an early-stage startup, Avea Robotics publishes a website, Notion-hosted documentation, and a Substack blog, but does not yet expose a public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a self-serve developer platform.

providers.name: Flytrex
providers.description: Flytrex is an autonomous drone delivery operator headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel, with US operations centered on the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex and North Carolina. The company runs an end-to-end backyard delivery service that flies food and small goods from partner restaurants and retailers to consumer homes in roughly five minutes, operating its own Sky-series multirotor aircraft, ground docks, and a remote-operations control center. Flytrex sells to consumers through its own iOS and Android ordering apps and to merchants through a partner portal, and routes demand from third-party marketplaces including DoorDash and Uber Eats. It does not currently publish a public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Mighty Buildings
providers.description: Mighty Buildings is a construction-technology and advanced-manufacturing company that industrializes homebuilding using large-format 3D printing, proprietary polymer-composite materials and robotic automation. Founded in 2019 and originally based in Oakland, California, it raised more than $150 million from investors including Khosla Ventures, Bold Capital and Aramco's Wa'ed Ventures, and was the first company certified under the UL 3401 standard for evaluating building structures and assemblies, as well as being certified under California's Factory Built Housing program. Its current product is the Mighty Kit System / Mighty Wall System - factory-made complete wall panels that arrive on site with integrated structure, insulation, waterproofing and exterior finish, so builders assemble a building envelope with conventional methods and fewer on-site steps. After a January 2025 restructuring and sale process, the full suite of Mighty Buildings technologies was acquired by LUMUS Inc., and Mighty Buildings now operates as a LUMUS brand headquartered in Beaverton, Oregon. The company sells physical building systems to developers and builders; it operates no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Vayu Robotics
providers.description: Vayu Robotics is a Palo Alto, California robotics company building AI foundation models and sensing for autonomous mobile robots. Its stack spans Vayu Drive, an end-to-end learned, sim-first foundation model for mobility; Vayu Sense, a plenoptic sensor with embodied AI for high-resolution depth perception; a Vayu Sense Development Kit bundled with NVIDIA Orin; and Vayu One, a low-cost autonomous delivery robot for last- and middle-mile delivery. Backed by Khosla Ventures, the company was acquired by Serve Robotics in September 2025. Enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface.

providers.name: Chef Robotics
providers.description: Chef Robotics is a San Francisco, California physical-AI company building AI-enabled robots for high-mix food production. Its core product is an NSF-certified food-assembly robot that picks, scoops, and deposits a wide range of ingredients — fresh, cooked, IQF, sauces, leafy greens, mixed vegetables, and discrete piece items — into trays, burritos, wraps, pizza bases, and other containers on conveyor lines. The robots are powered by ChefOS, a proprietary Generalized Food Manipulation Model trained on tens of millions of real-world servings and tens of thousands of hours of production data, combining vision, decision-making, and robot control across a See / Think / Act stack with continuous Fleet Learning. Chef Robotics sells via a Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) model that bundles hardware, software updates, 24/7 monitoring, and customer success. Deployed customers include Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket, Cafe Spice, and Chef Bombay, with the fleet having produced 98+ million servings across the US, Canada, and Europe. The company is venture-backed (Kleiner Perkins, Avataar Ventures-led $43M Series A, Bloomberg Beta, Construct Capital) and serves frozen meals, fresh meals, co-manufacturing, D2C meal delivery, medically tailored meals, meatpacking, airline catering, and foodservice verticals. There is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for ChefOS — the platform is operated as a closed, fleet-managed service on Chef-owned hardware deployed inside customer facilities.

providers.name: iRobot
providers.description: iRobot Corporation is a Bedford, Massachusetts consumer robotics company best known for the Roomba robot vacuum and the Braava and Braava jet robot mop product lines. Founded in 1990 by MIT roboticists, iRobot pioneered the home cleaning robot category and has sold tens of millions of units worldwide. Its current portfolio includes the Roomba Max, Roomba Plus, and Roomba 100/200 series vacuums and combo (vacuum + mop) models, along with AutoWash and AutoEmpty docks, the iRobot Home App for scheduling and mapping, and a cleaning accessories and trade-in program. The proposed acquisition by Amazon was abandoned in January 2024 after regulatory pushback from the European Commission, after which iRobot underwent a major restructuring and layoffs. iRobot's revenue model is direct robot and accessory sales plus recurring consumables; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification, and its homesupport documentation explicitly notes that Wi-Fi connected Roombas do not have an open API. A community of unofficial reverse-engineered libraries (dorita980, rest980, pyirobot) exists but is not endorsed by iRobot.

providers.name: Mecka AI
providers.description: Mecka AI is the data and deployment layer for physical AI — it captures, structures, and evaluates real-world human and robot activity into datasets that robotics and embodied-AI teams can train on. Rather than building robots, Mecka positions itself as the integrator of the robotics ecosystem, plugging into hardware makers, frontier model labs, and commercial partners and owning the last-mile data, annotation, QA, and evaluation layer between them. Its Egoverse dataset captures large-scale first-person (egocentric) human activity across tasks and environments, and a companion iOS app lets teams collect task-specific data at scale. Mecka is backed by Forerunner Ventures and raised a $60M Series A in 2026. As of this pass Mecka publishes a marketing site, an iOS data-collection app, and the Egoverse data platform, but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Pyka
providers.description: Pyka is an Alameda, California company that designs and manufactures large, dual-use heavy-lift autonomous electric aircraft for commercial and defense operations. Its flagship products are the Pelican 2 autonomous crop-protection aircraft for aerial application and the DropShip long-range heavy-lift cargo UAS. Pyka builds a fully integrated, vertically owned autonomy stack — an Autonomy Engine (real-time OS, sensor fusion, flight control, and path planning), a Mission Control operator suite (simulation, communications, and operator interface), and custom aerospace-grade hardware. The company is backed by DCVC and Obvious Ventures. Pyka does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public web and domain-security footprint. Surfaced via VC portfolio enrichment.

providers.name: Rollup AI
providers.description: Rollup is a browser-based, real-time collaboration platform for engineering teams building complex hardware. It supports the full hardware development lifecycle across modular tools for systems engineering, systems modeling, requirements management, technical documentation, CAD viewing, and design reviews, with modules that interlink so changes propagate across a project. Rollup markets first-class APIs and developer-friendly features so teams can integrate it into new and existing systems; the platform exposes a REST API (authenticated with API keys or OAuth tokens) with pagination and websockets. Rollup serves early-stage hardware companies from small satellite builders to robotics firms, and offers Self-hosted and GovCloud options for ITAR/EAR export-controlled data. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Thiel Capital ($5.6M seed) and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company.

providers.name: Sensmore
providers.description: Sensmore (sensmore GmbH) is a German industrial-automation and embodied-AI company that turns robotics research into field-proven systems for heavy machinery in raw material operations. Its platform connects machines, sites, and data across mining, aggregates/construction, and defense, spanning products including Site Intelligence (live site operations), Machine Assist (driver assistance and collision warning), Eye (visual monitoring), Live Mapping (real-time site mapping), and Loader Automation (autonomous vehicle systems), with claims of reducing downtime by up to 30% while improving safety and resource efficiency. Sensmore was surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or developer documentation; its web presence is a marketing and corporate site.

providers.name: Sunrise
providers.description: Sunrise Robotics builds intelligent, two-armed autonomous robotic cells for manufacturing. The AI-driven system combines built-in perception and environmental awareness with autonomous execution to transform existing production processes, increase capacity, and free human workers for higher-value tasks. Cells deploy quickly (needing only a three-phase outlet), are flexible across manufacturing applications, and are built to ISO 10218 / TS 15066 safety standards. The company is backed by Seedcamp and Slow Ventures.

providers.name: teaBOT
providers.description: teaBOT is a Toronto-based hardware startup (Y Combinator, Summer 2015) that builds an automated loose-leaf tea-making robot offered to offices, showrooms, and lounges as an amenity-as-a-service. For a flat monthly fee, teams use the companion teaBOT app to explore premium teas and dispense a custom-blended cup in under 30 seconds, which companies such as Google, HubSpot, and McKinsey use as a workplace recruiting and retention perk. Founded by robotics PhD Rehman Merali, teaBOT runs a physical-product and mobile-app business and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: TRIC Robotics
providers.description: TRIC Robotics builds autonomous agricultural robots that replace chemical pesticides with ultraviolet light. Its flagship platform, Luna, is a tractor-scale robot that roams California strawberry fields after dark, using UV-C light to kill fungal pathogens such as powdery mildew and botrytis while a mechanical "Bug Vac" removes pests like Lygus bugs, spotted wing drosophila, and spider mites — without a single drop of pesticide. Founded in 2017 by Dr. Adam Stager and Vishnu Somasundaram out of the University of Delaware and now based in California, TRIC operates a robotics-as-a-service model that requires no upfront investment from growers, and reports pesticide reductions of up to 70% across the farms it serves. The company raised a $5.5M seed round led by Version One Ventures to expand its fleet across Santa Maria, Oxnard, and Watsonville. TRIC Robotics is an agricultural robotics operator and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its company identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Aerialoop
providers.description: Aerialoop is a drone technology and urban logistics company that designs, builds, and operates intelligent aerial networks for cargo delivery, surveillance, and infrastructure inspection. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Miami with operations rooted in Quito, Ecuador, it is one of the fastest-growing drone delivery operations in Latin America. Its ALT 6-8 delivery drone carries a 5kg payload for urban logistics, while the ALT 6-ISR line adds HD, infrared, and night-vision cameras with AI-powered intrusion detection; extended-range variants operate up to 120km using LEO satellite connectivity for beyond-visual-line-of-sight flights. The company has completed over 50,000 flights across six countries. Aerialoop is a Techstars Miami (powered by J.P. Morgan) portfolio company. It currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: AIMACH Automation
providers.description: AIMACH Automation is the international brand of Jiangsu Desu Intelligent Machinery Co., Ltd. (江苏德速智能机械股份有限公司), a Changzhou, Jiangsu-based manufacturer of machine-tool core functional components founded in 2009. Its product lines are physical assemblies — CNC tool magazines (刀库), motorized spindles (主轴), rotary / index tables (转台) and mineral-cast machine beds (矿物铸件) — which the company states account for more than 60% of a machine tool's total cost. It also builds five-axis machining-centre platforms, ultra-precision grinders and turnkey automated production lines for automotive and general manufacturing customers, and operates provincial R&D centres for CNC machine-tool functional components. The company is pre-IPO and runs a Chinese-language corporate site with an investor-relations section; it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Generalist AI
providers.description: Generalist AI, Inc. is a frontier AI research and product-driven company building general intelligence for the physical world — training robots that work autonomously across factories, warehouses, laboratories, restaurants, farms, homes, and beyond. Its flagship model, GEN-1, is a general-purpose embodied foundation model trained from scratch that reaches mastery of simple physical tasks, going beyond world models and vision-language-action (VLA) approaches. Backed by Spark Capital, the company publishes its research through a blog and open-sources vision and robotics tooling on GitHub. Generalist AI exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Peer Robotics
providers.description: Peer Robotics builds collaborative autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for manufacturing and warehouse material movement, designed to learn directly from humans to lower the cost and complexity of traditional automation. Its lineup includes the Peer 3000 collaborative mobile robot and the RM250 and RM500 AMRs (250kg and 500kg payloads) that handle pallets, trolleys, bin delivery, and machine tending through an intuitive human-robot dashboard interface. Backed by Techstars, the company operates a hardware and robotics product line rather than a public developer API surface; no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or GitHub repositories were found during enrichment probing.

providers.name: Boxbot
providers.description: Boxbot builds next-generation supply chain automation, making logistics operations more productive, intelligent, and resilient through automated, high-density dynamic storage that unlocks new AI-driven capabilities. Its platform is designed for mission-control fulfillment facilities: real-time space allocation packs variable-sized items densely, hands-free load/unload moves items onto and off proprietary storage trays linked to standard conveyors with no pick or load stations, and a modular, gantry-based architecture delivers a robust, fault-tolerant design with no single point of failure. Boxbot is a hardware/robotics company backed by Playground Global; it publishes a marketing presence but no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Monumental
providers.description: Monumental builds autonomous construction robots and the software that runs them. Its robots lay bricks and blockwork on real building sites, coordinated by Monumental's software platform (Atrium) and fleet operations (Fleet). The venture-backed company operates across the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and the United States, and has raised multiple funding rounds (including a reported $32M raise and Series B rounds in the US and UK). Monumental was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation - this record captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Vitesse
providers.description: Vitesse is a universal physical-AI platform for industrial machines, founded by the team behind Tesla's "Model 3 automation hell" fix alongside leaders from SpaceX, Siemens, and Safran. It connects any machine - Siemens, Allen-Bradley, Fanuc, KUKA, ABB, and legacy PLCs - through 135 native OT connectors, generates control logic from a natural-language description of a process (up to 15x faster than traditional PLC programming), and runs the full stack at the edge on purpose-built industrial controllers with no cloud required. The platform layers hardware, live data dashboards and SCADA views, interoperability, physical AI, and zero-trust OT/IT cybersecurity (NIS2 and NIST aligned) into one stack, with real-time browser-based monitoring across 800,000+ machine hours. The company traded as Full Speed Automation and renamed to Vitesse Automation after acquiring Niagara Tech; the legacy fullspeedautomation.com domain no longer resolves over TLS. Vitesse exposes a marketing website and a login-gated product application at app.vitesse.dev; as of August 2026 it publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL specification, SDK, webhooks, developer portal, or pricing page, and serves no /.well-known discovery documents.

providers.name: Vsim
providers.description: Vsim (Vsim Technology Ltd) is a Manchester, UK physics-simulation startup founded in 2022 by ex-NVIDIA simulation engineers Michelle Lu (CEO) and Kier Storey (CTO). The company builds a next-generation physics simulation platform and an end-to-end reinforcement-learning training framework for robotics, reporting up to 100x training performance speed-ups over existing solutions, with applications across robotics, AI, visual effects, aerodynamics, gaming, and e-commerce. Vsim raised a $21.5M seed round led by EQT Ventures (total ~$24M). It does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Andustry
providers.description: Andustry is an AI-native industrial equipment broker that streamlines sourcing and procurement for manufacturers. The platform combines AI-powered supplier discovery with manual qualification and commercial negotiation to source industrial machines (CNC mills, lathes, press brakes, laser cutters, robotic cells), machined/forged/cast parts, and robotics and electronics across Europe, China, India, and the United States. Clients hand off a sourcing need and Andustry returns a verified supplier shortlist within 24-48 hours, delivering an average of roughly 30% cost savings and 2x faster sourcing timelines on a commission-only basis with no subscription. Founded in 2026 (Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch) by Het Dave and Johann Stuerken and operated as Andustry GmbH.

providers.name: Lincoln Electric Holdings
providers.description: Lincoln Electric Holdings is a global manufacturer of arc welding products, robotic welding systems, plasma and oxyfuel cutting equipment, and brazing and soldering alloys. The company also offers connected welding solutions and equipment monitoring software for industrial environments.

providers.name: dopl technologies
providers.description: Dopl Technologies is a Seattle-based data and AI company (founded 2022, Techstars-backed) democratizing access to diagnostic exams and interventional procedures through telerobotic ultrasound. Its Dopl Traverse platform and SonoFlex app let a remote sonographer operate an ultrasound probe over a network from significant distances, extending specialist-level imaging into rural and workforce-constrained regions. Field testing in rural Washington hospitals has reduced patient wait times by over 90 percent. The company cites 50M+ missed ultrasound exams annually and $19.5B in lost revenue from unequal imaging access, and expects FDA clearance in 2027 before expanding into minimally invasive procedures. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or API documentation; this record is a network stub maintained for discovery and future enrichment.

providers.name: Aerospace Times Feipeng
providers.description: Aerospace Times Feipeng Co., Ltd. (航天时代飞鹏有限公司) is a Chinese unmanned transport aircraft manufacturer founded in 2020 in the Huaqiao Economic Development Zone of Kunshan, Jiangsu, as a mixed-ownership enterprise launched by the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC) together with SF Express. It designs, manufactures and operates cargo UAV systems across three payload/range classes — the Double 1000 (1000 kg / 1000 km trunk-line), Double 100 (branch-line) and Double 10 (last-mile) series — alongside special aircraft, ground control stations, an unmanned aircraft operation control system, and an AOPA-certified UAV pilot training centre. Its FP-98 "Leo" large fixed-wing UAV received a CAAC type certificate in April 2024. The company publishes a corporate marketing website in Chinese and English; it operates no public developer program and publishes no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: AliciaBots
providers.description: AliciaBots is a maritime robotics company, backed by Techstars, that builds autonomous robot teams for cleaning and inspecting ship hulls. Its flagship Roverclean robot operates independently to remove marine growth and monitor hull condition in real time without interrupting a vessel's voyage, using self-learning adaptive systems, precision cleaning, and remote monitoring and control to improve fuel efficiency and help operators meet IMO regulatory standards. AliciaBots does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile tracks the company as a network lead.

providers.name: AutoStore
providers.description: AutoStore is a global warehouse robotics and technology company headquartered in Nedre Vats, Norway, that pioneered the cube storage automated storage and retrieval system (AS/RS). Its goods-to-person solution combines autonomous robots, an aluminum storage grid of stacked bins, workstation ports, and controlling software (marketed as CubeVerse, spanning design, simulation, operations, and predictive diagnostics) to fulfill orders in a fraction of the floor space of conventional warehouses. With more than 1,950 systems deployed across nearly 65 countries, AutoStore serves retail, grocery, 3PL, healthcare, and industrial customers. Systems are distributed, designed, installed, and serviced through a global network of qualified system integrators rather than a public developer/API program. AutoStore was surfaced as a portfolio company of SoftBank Vision Fund and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: COSY
providers.description: COSY (CosyRobo) is a retail-technology robotics company that builds autonomous inventory robots for physical stores. Its flagship robot, SCOUT, roams store aisles using AI and machine vision to scan shelves, map products, audit stock levels, and check planogram compliance, feeding the results into a cloud-based management system so retailers can reduce out-of-stocks and improve on-shelf availability. Backed by 500 Global, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; it publishes a marketing website but does not currently expose a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: emergen
providers.description: emergen (智昌科技集团股份有限公司, Zhichang Technology Group) is a Chinese industrial intelligence company founded by Dr. Gan Zhongxue, an expert in intelligent manufacturing. Built around its proprietary "ternary control" technology and cluster (swarm) robotics, the company positions itself as "AI + Control," delivering integrated "industrial agent" solutions that install a control "brain" into individual machines, production lines, and whole factories. Its portfolio spans robot controllers, ubiquitous controllers, industrial and collaborative robots, life-science robots, GVision 2D/3D machine vision, the GSC-AI100 sense-compute-control AI controller, a swarm-intelligence network controller, a micro-control cloud platform, and the "Jiangxin" family of industrial large models (design, production, service, and management). emergen serves automotive, electronics, equipment manufacturing, steel, metallurgy, textile, furniture, and shipbuilding sectors, plus Robotics-as-a-Service. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this pass no public developer/API surface was found.

providers.name: Isengard Industries Inc
providers.description: Isengard Industries builds sovereign production capability for defense: the means for allied nations to manufacture precision-strike and counter-drone (counter-UAS) systems by the thousand, on their own soil, at a fraction of what traditional prime contractors charge. The company describes its approach as "Weapons of Mass Production." Founded in 2026 and part of Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch, it is led by Francisco Serra-Martins (previously co-founder/CEO of Terminal Autonomy) and James Tennant (former Australian Army officer), and is headquartered in San Francisco. As a hardware and defense-manufacturing company it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public identity and security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Rhoda Ai
providers.description: Rhoda AI develops robotic intelligence for real-world industrial and commercial environments, building general-purpose foundation models that adapt to the variability of physical work through its Direct Video Action model.
