Its robots handle tasks across automotive, manufacturing, logistics, and ecommerce, including returns processing, component handling, and material breakdown. The company is a venture-backed portfolio company of Mayfield and currently publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Slip Robotics
providers.description: Slip Robotics is an Atlanta, Georgia-based robotics company that builds SlipBots, autonomous omnidirectional Automated Loading Robots (ALRs) that load and unload any truck trailer in about five minutes without a forklift ever entering the trailer. Each SlipBot carries up to eight pallets and roughly six tons, cutting driver dwell time from around ninety minutes to five while reducing material-handling damage and loading-dock accidents. The company also offers SlipLift, a platform that extends autonomous trailer loading and unloading to heavier freight and regional and last-mile routes. Slip Robotics markets its robots-as-a-service offering as requiring no IT integration, is backed by DCVC, and won Best New Innovation in supply chain technology at MODEX 2024. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Lily Camera
providers.description: The domain lily.camera currently serves "Lily Camera", a consumer-facing marketplace that connects clients with certified drone pilots for aerial photography and videography across real estate, events, agriculture, construction, and media production. It is a client-rendered single-page application: every requested path returns the same HTML shell, and the routes defined in its JavaScript bundle cover browsing pilots and drones, comparisons, bookings, messaging, a pilot dashboard, and a drone raffle. There is no public API, no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, no SDKs, and no /.well-known discovery surface. The site is built on Lovable (GPT Engineer), monetized with Google AdSense, and backed by a hosted Supabase project. No API artifacts could be harvested because the provider publishes none.

providers.name: Mirana Toys
providers.description: Mirana Toys (Mirana Innovations Pvt Ltd) is an India-based smart-toy company and OEM/ODM manufacturer of electronic toys — RC cars, monster trucks, drones, educational toys, and AI/AR toys. It pairs its consumer products with the Mirana smart app (iOS and Android), a mobile gaming platform that lets kids and adults control and play with Mirana toys over Bluetooth. As an OEM partner it offers in-house PCB/PCBA design and SMT assembly, tooling and mold design, mobile app development, compliance support (ASTM, EN-71, RoHS, ISO, SMETA), and global logistics for toy brands and retailers. Backed by Accel. The company publishes a consumer e-commerce storefront and support center but no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Shotwellai
providers.description: Shotwell AI is a Y Combinator-backed startup building an observability and annotation layer for robotics training data. Its pipeline ingests raw teleoperation video, robot logs, and multimodal sensor streams, then uses models to watch every frame, segment continuous motion into discrete actions, and label each action against a customer's task definition and SOP rubric. Every label is quality-scored and returned in hours rather than weeks, producing dense, frame-accurate, training-ready datasets for robot manipulation, deformable/folding tasks, teleoperation episode QA, and vision-language-action (VLA) foundation-model post-training. As of enrichment the company exposes only a marketing website and a sales contact (hello@shotwell.ai); no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs were found.

providers.name: Skycatch
providers.description: Skycatch built spatial data capture, processing, and analytics for mining and construction sites, turning drone and aerial imagery into high-precision 3D data, volumetrics, and AI-driven site insights. Its products included Spatial Sight, Spatial DataHub (datahub.skycatch.com), and EdgeServer for on-site edge processing. Skycatch was acquired by Caterpillar Inc. on July 7, 2026 (following Caterpillar's RPMGlobal acquisition) to expand its mining technology capabilities. A developer platform exists at docs.skycatch.com but is password-gated, and no public API specification is available. Originally surfaced as a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company.

providers.name: Synphony
providers.description: Synphony builds and deploys robots that work in the real world, combining AI, robotics, and human-in-the-loop systems so machines can perform practical physical tasks across agriculture, assembly, and inspection. Its platform trains AI models on real-world data, tests robot performance in realistic scenarios, and deploys systems into production. The company's first application is autonomous strawberry-harvesting robots plus farm software services (bed-level analytics, data-pipeline integration, and agentic solutions), targeting California's roughly $3B strawberry industry where labor is about 60% of costs. Founded in 2025 and backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026), Synphony runs a customer-facing platform at app.synphony.co but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: AMI Labs
providers.description: AMI Labs is a frontier AI research lab building intelligent systems that understand the real world. The lab develops world models trained with self-supervised learning on continuous, high-dimensional sensor data (cameras and other sensors), aiming for AI with persistent memory, reasoning and planning, and controllable, safety-oriented behavior. Targeted applications span industrial process control, automation, wearable devices, robotics, and healthcare. Founded by Yann LeCun as Executive Chairman with Alexandre LeBrun as CEO, AMI Labs launched officially on 2026-03-10 with a $1.03B USD round co-led by Cathay Innovation, Greycroft, Hiro Capital, HV Capital, and Bezos Expeditions, and operates from Paris, New York, Montreal, and Singapore. The lab operates as a research organization and publishes no public developer platform, API, SDKs, documentation, or machine-readable contract: amilabs.xyz is a two-page site whose own sitemap declares only / and /updates, and every OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP, A2A and /.well-known/ discovery path probed on it returns HTTP 404.

providers.name: Basis Set Ventures
providers.description: Basis Set Ventures is an AI-native, early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2017 by Dr. Lan Xuezhao and headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area. The firm invests at the seed and early stages in founders building artificial intelligence across AI infrastructure, autonomous systems, molecular and materials discovery, agentic development tooling, intelligent collaboration, and automated workflows. Basis Set announced a $250M Fund IV and describes itself as "the first capital when it's just you and your vision," pairing capital with an operator-led founder concierge team. Portfolio companies include Path Robotics, Quince, Sakana AI, Tigris Data, Mem0, OpenArt, Cusp, Simular, Vizcom, and Entire. This is an API Evangelist network profile of the firm; Basis Set Ventures does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so this record captures firm identity, web properties, and derived security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Fantasmo
providers.description: Fantasmo builds CPS (Camera Positioning System), a computer-vision positioning technology it positions as a "camera-powered GPS replacement" delivering hyper-accurate localization that works indoors and in dense urban environments where satellite GPS degrades, using only a device camera and a data connection rather than additional infrastructure. Its target applications span micromobility (scooter/bike tracking and theft prevention), robotics navigation, mobile augmented-reality experiences, and automotive lane-level positioning. Fantasmo was a Techstars-backed startup and was acquired by Niantic in 2022; the public fantasmo.io site remains online but exposes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or OpenAPI surface at this time. This profile was enriched from the provider's public web presence and live DNS/TLS/HTTP probes.

providers.name: Neocis
providers.description: Neocis is a medical robotics company and the maker of Yomi, described as the first and only FDA-cleared robot-assisted dental surgery system. Yomi combines preoperative implant planning software with intraoperative haptic robotic guidance to assist dentists during dental implant placement procedures. The company sells hardware, planning software, and practitioner training to dental practices rather than operating a public developer platform. Neocis is a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners. As of this profile it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or webhook surface.

providers.name: Orchard Robotics
providers.description: Orchard Robotics (Orchard AI, "The AI Farming Company") is an agricultural technology startup founded in 2022 that builds AI-powered camera systems and farm-management software for precision fruit and vine growing. Its FruitScope platform mounts AI-enabled cameras on any farm vehicle to collect precise per-tree and per-vine data — fruit count, size, color, and growth rate — which is stored in FruitScope Vault and surfaced through FruitScope OS for crop decision-making, with a Vineyard Robotics division serving grape growers. Backed by General Catalyst, the company has raised roughly $22M. As of this profile Orchard Robotics publishes a marketing and careers website but no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Xwing
providers.description: Xwing, Inc. is a San Francisco and Concord, California aviation company founded in 2016 that built Superpilot, a modular retrofit autonomy system enabling ground-supervised, uncrewed gate-to-gate flight on conventional fixed-wing aircraft. Flying a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan testbed, Xwing completed more than 250 fully autonomous flights and over 500 auto-landings, and in April 2023 became the first company to receive an FAA project designation toward certification of a large unmanned aircraft system. Joby Aviation acquired Xwing's autonomy division in June 2024; Xwing retained its Part 135 air cargo operation, and www.xwing.com is now an archived marketing site pointing visitors to Joby. Xwing never published a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable contract; the domain's only agent-readable surfaces are the llms.txt and Site MCP endpoint that Wix generates for every site it hosts.

providers.name: Advex AI
providers.description: Advex AI (Advex AI, Inc., San Francisco / Pleasanton, California; founded 2022 by Pedro Pachuca and Qasim Wani) builds generative-AI synthetic data and self-healing computer vision for industrial quality inspection. Its flagship product, Composer, is a no-code AI vision system that lets manufacturing and logistics teams train, deploy and manage visual inspection tasks — defect and anomaly detection, pick-and-place, kitting and assembly verification, counting — from a handful of real images, using diffusion models to synthesize the missing training data and VLMs to run the inspection. Composer is sold as an on-premises appliance (the "Advex box") paired with plant cameras and is explicitly designed to run entirely on-device without network connectivity. The company raised a $3.5M seed round in November 2024 led by Construct Capital with Pear VC and Emerson Collective. As of this profile Advex publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind, and its own website is currently unpublished.

providers.name: Aerospace Kate
providers.description: Aerospace Kate (航天凯特) is the trading name of Chengdu Aerospace Kate Mechanical & Electrical Technology Co., Ltd. (成都航天凯特机电科技有限公司), a Chinese high-precision servo drive manufacturer founded in 2017 in Pidu District, Chengdu, Sichuan. A national high-tech and state-designated "little giant" specialized-and-innovative enterprise with roughly 200 staff (over half in R&D) and 210+ registered IP rights, it builds fully domestically-sourced servo drivers spanning 15V to 800V (KTSD, 蜀芯, 蓉驭 and 锦驱 series), KTMT hollow-cup motors, underwater thrusters and electric actuators, phased-array antenna steering gear, and the 灵捷 (Lingjie) line of robot joint modules, collaborative arms, quadruped robots and humanoid platforms. A second line covers optoelectronic detection — panoramic detectors, maritime search lights and airport runway FOD detection. The product is physical hardware; Aerospace Kate publishes no API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: TakeOff
providers.description: Takeoff Technologies, Inc. is an eGrocery micro-fulfillment company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts. It paired KNAPP-built robotic storage-and-retrieval hardware with its own cloud software stack — order management, inventory, pick routing, labor management, and delivery orchestration — into micro-fulfillment centers (MFCs) installed inside or beside existing supermarkets, so grocers could assemble online orders in minutes instead of sending shoppers down the aisles. Customers and partners included Albertsons, Wakefern Food Corp., Woolworths Group and Chilean grocer SMU. The company filed for Chapter 11 in May 2024 and Woolworths Group acquired its micro-fulfillment assets in August 2024. Takeoff never published a public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification anywhere on its public surface, and the marketing site at www.takeoff.com no longer serves TLS. A closed API gateway at api.takeoff.com remains live and actively certificate-maintained, serving customer integrations behind authentication.

providers.name: ThayerMahan
providers.description: ThayerMahan, Inc. is a U.S. maritime autonomy and ocean-intelligence company headquartered in Groton, Connecticut, founded in 2016 and led by former U.S. Navy Vice Admiral Michael Connor. It builds and operates uncrewed surface and subsurface sensing systems — Outpost, SeaPicket, SeaGuard (a non-kinetic counter-UUV defeat system) and the TransparenSea data platform — combining passive acoustic arrays, electronic sensors, edge processing, AI classification and human analysts to deliver persistent undersea surveillance, port and critical-infrastructure security, subsea infrastructure monitoring, passive acoustic marine-mammal monitoring and illegal-fishing (IUU) detection for defense, government and commercial offshore customers. ThayerMahan sells outcomes as a service rather than developer tooling: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable contract. The only public reference to programmatic access is on the TransparenSea page, which states that contact reports are delivered by application programming interface (API), voice report, or other means in near real-time — a customer-delivery integration negotiated per engagement, not a self-serve public API. Its GitHub organization holds two forks of third-party tools and no first-party libraries.

providers.name: Alba Robot
providers.description: ALBA Robot is a Turin, Italy based autonomous micro-mobility company building a fleet of self-driving robots for indoor and pedestrian spaces such as airports, hospitals, and large facilities. Its product line includes ALBA One, ALBA Ride, ALBA Ride +, and the ALBA Caddie autonomous baggage transport robot, and it layers digital services such as Digital Twins and Digital Out-of-Home (DOOH) advertising on top of the mobility platform. ALBA Robot runs pilots and deployments with airports including Cagliari, London Gatwick, Dallas, Milan, Turin, and Dubai (with dnata), and operates from Turin with a US presence in Detroit, Michigan. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDKs, or GitHub organization; it is a hardware/robotics fleet operator rather than an API provider.

providers.name: Andrenam
providers.description: Andrenam is a defense technology company building an AI-powered maritime sensing network for undersea surveillance. It develops mass-manufacturable, low-cost buoy-based autonomous sonar systems that deploy from manned and unmanned vessels to detect, track, and identify real-time maritime traffic using cloud and edge AI, then dispatch resources to priority areas. Its product line spans deployment, AI-enhanced detection, and integration with naval command-and-control systems, targeting government and military maritime-domain-awareness customers. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Aqrose Technology
providers.description: Aqrose Technology (阿丘科技) is an industrial AI machine-vision platform provider founded in Beijing in 2017 out of the Tsinghua University AI Lab, now dual-headquartered in Beijing and Singapore with offices in Suzhou, Shenzhen, Hsinchu, Berlin, Tokyo, and Seoul. The company builds AI tools, models, and turnkey systems for manufacturing quality control, safety inspection, and process optimization, with 20,000+ AI deployments across 1,200+ clients in 50+ industrial sectors. Its product line spans the AIDI defect-inspection platform, the AQVision low-code AI vision development toolkit, the AIDG toolkit, the SV2000 smart vision hardware, an AI Review System (ARS), a robot inspection system, and the AQ-VLM industrial vision-language model, serving EV batteries, automotive, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, electronics, photovoltaics, food and beverage, and packaging. Surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Atlas Motion Systems
providers.description: Atlas Motion Systems (atlasmotion.com) designs and builds brushless DC (BLDC) motors and actuators for defense and robotics applications, engineered around a customer's specific program and manufactured at scale. The public web presence is a single-page marketing site (hero plus a contact page); it is a hardware company that does not publish a developer portal, public API, SDKs, documentation, or well-known discovery surface. This profile was seeded as a Homebrew-portfolio lead and enriched with verifiable identity and live domain-security probe data only. Enrichment found no API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Cerrion
providers.description: Cerrion builds enterprise-grade video AI agents for manufacturing. Its platform connects to existing or provided factory cameras to monitor production lines in real time, using pre-trained visual triggers to automatically detect and respond to quality defects, safety hazards, process deviations, and equipment issues. The closed-loop system can slow or stop machines, raise alarms, and escalate alerts while giving operators root-cause insight, helping manufacturers resolve problems up to 50% faster and cut downtime and scrap. Cerrion is deployed in live production across glass, food & beverage, tableware, sawmilling/timber, and CPG environments (customers include Unilever, Riedel, Schott Zwiesel, Stölzle Lausitz, Sisecam, and Verallia). Zurich-based and backed by Creandum, Y Combinator, Goat Capital, 10x Founders, and Session VC. No public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: FIMI Technology
providers.description: FIMI Technology Ltd. (Beijing FIMI Technology Co., Ltd. / Shenzhen FIMI Robot Technology Co., Ltd.) is a consumer aerial-imaging hardware manufacturer founded in May 2014 as a member of the Xiaomi ecosystem. FIMI designs and sells affordable camera drones, handheld gimbal cameras, and smartphone gimbals, with a product lineup that includes the X8 series (X8 SE, X8 Pro, X8 Tele, X8T enterprise), the compact Mini 3, the Manta VTOL fixed-wing drone, and the PALM series gimbal cameras. The company holds hundreds of patents across flight control, wireless transmission links, mechatronic design, gimbal image-stabilization, and computer vision. FIMI is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. This is a consumer-electronics company with no public developer program, API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Heaviside Industries
providers.description: Heaviside Industries is a defense-technology company founded in 2024 in Los Angeles, California, building autonomous precision munitions for U.S. and allied special operations and conventional forces. Its products — MOTH (land electromagnetic signal intelligence and spectrum awareness), TYR (autonomous aerial munition), and HYDRA (autonomous underwater munition) — are designed to deliver hyper-precise strike capabilities across air, land, and sea in GPS-denied and contested environments. Named after physicist Oliver Heaviside, whose electromagnetic theory enabled miniaturized electronics, the company emerged from stealth in May 2026 with a $28M Series A. It does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API artifacts.

providers.name: MOLG
providers.description: MOLG (molg.ai) is a circular manufacturing company tackling electronic waste. It operates autonomous robotic microfactories that disassemble complex devices like laptops and servers to recover components and materials for reuse, remanufacturing, and recycling. MOLG also partners with manufacturers on design-for-circularity (modular snap/press-fit/latch assembly instead of screws and adhesives) and offers OriginMark, a traceability platform for tracking devices, components, and materials across their lifecycle to calculate embodied carbon and supply-chain transparency. As of this enrichment pass MOLG publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: One Robot
providers.description: One Robot is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup building world-model-based simulation environments for robotics teams. Its core product learns physics and visual appearance directly from real robot data, producing simulation environments that are both visually and physically realistic so teams can train and evaluate robot manipulation policies without excessive reliance on physical robot time and real-world data collection. One Robot specializes in contact-rich manipulation, deformable objects (such as textile and box folding), and precise assembly tasks. As an early-stage two-person company it currently offers task-specific simulation collaboration rather than a public developer platform or API; this profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network for future enrichment as any developer surface emerges.

providers.name: Seeing Systems
providers.description: Seeing Systems is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) defense technology company building autonomous, modular strike drones and AI-powered swarm coordination software at the intersection of artificial intelligence and robotics. Its product line includes Bandit, a cost-effective FPV drone for training and expendable missions with 30+ km of range; Banshee, an autonomous modular platform built for contested, jamming-resistant environments with 40+ km of range; and Aerie AI, swarm coordination software for multi-platform operations that lowers operator cognitive load. The company works directly with military and defense partners — including UK Royal Marine Commandos and NATO forces — rather than publishing a public developer platform. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of the latest enrichment pass Seeing Systems exposes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: VICTUS Technologies
providers.description: VICTUS Technologies builds contested-autonomy software for autonomous systems operating in GPS-denied and jamming-heavy environments. Its PhantomNAV platform delivers precise state estimation from the gravity and inertial sensors already embedded in drones, aircraft, submarines, satellites, and ships - no new hardware required - and integrates with Palantir Foundry's AIP infrastructure. VICTUS is backed by Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes a marketing and platform site but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Wing
providers.description: Wing is Alphabet's drone delivery subsidiary, spun out of Google X in 2018, with operating headquarters in Palo Alto, California and significant operations in Australia, Finland, Ireland, and the United States. Wing designs, builds, and operates a fleet of small fixed-wing electric VTOL aircraft that autonomously pick up and deliver packages to customers' homes, and it operates an unmanned traffic management (UTM) stack used by drone pilots and aviation authorities. Wing was the first company to receive an FAA Part 135 Air Carrier Certificate for drone delivery (2019) and is an approved LAANC USS in the United States and an approved drone airspace authorization provider for CASA in Australia. Wing's commercial surface is split across two main platforms — the Wing Delivery Platform, a partner-only API and UI suite that lets retailers, restaurants, and logistics providers embed drone delivery into their own order flows (Walmart, DoorDash, Papa Johns, and others), and OpenSky, a consumer drone airspace authorization app and partner API. Wing also co-founded the InterUSS Platform open-source UTM project, now hosted by the Linux Foundation. Wing's revenue comes from per-delivery fees charged to merchant partners and from drone-as-a-service operations rather than from public developer APIs; the Delivery Platform API and OpenSky API are not openly published and there is no public OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at the time of profiling.

providers.name: 3S robotics
providers.description: 3S robotics (Shanghai Shengshi Weisheng Technology Co., Ltd. / 上海昇视唯盛科技有限公司) is a Chinese intelligent-robotics manufacturer founded in 2020 and headquartered in the Songjiang district of Shanghai, with a smart factory in the Haining Economic Development Zone, Zhejiang. It is a member company of the listed Harbin Institute of Technology intelligent-robotics group (哈工智能), and its majority-held subsidiary Hagong Hyundai (哈工现代, HGXD) builds general-purpose industrial robots. The company develops an in-house "AI + 3D + ROBOT" stack — machine-vision cameras, motion control, and offline path-planning software — packaged as task-specific intelligent robots for welding, grinding and assembly, marketed as needing no teach-pendant programming. Its flagship line is a 3D-vision intelligent welding robot aimed at steel-structure, tunnel arch, rail-transit and heavy-equipment fabrication. The software it ships is embedded machine-side control and vision tooling sold with the hardware; the company publishes no public developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: Civil Maps
providers.description: Civil Maps was a San Francisco autonomous-vehicle mapping company founded in 2015 by Sravan Puttagunta and Scott Harvey, with Fabien Chraim and Anuj Gupta on the founding team. It built AI software that turned vehicle LiDAR and camera data into machine-readable HD 3D maps and delivered real-time six-degrees-of-freedom localization at 15-20 cm absolute accuracy, crowdsourcing map updates from production fleets rather than from dedicated survey vehicles, and packaged that as the Atlas DevKit and Atlas Lite DevKit car-mounted units. It raised roughly USD 17 million across four rounds, including a USD 6.6 million seed led by Motus Ventures with Ford Motor Company, Wicklow Capital, StartX and AME Cloud Ventures, and was acquired by Luminar Technologies in mid-2022 - an acquisition Luminar announced at CES in January 2023 and folded into its Sentinel platform. Civil Maps no longer operates as an independent business: civilmaps.com is a frozen four-page marketing archive stamped "Copyright 2019" with no developer section, it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and its 2015-era GitHub organization holds five C++ repositories last pushed between 2017 and 2020.

providers.name: Nuro
providers.description: Nuro is a Mountain View-based autonomy company that has pivoted from its original autonomous-goods-delivery vehicle program (R1, R2, R3) to a licensable, vehicle-agnostic autonomous driving stack. The Nuro Driver is an AI-first Level 4 self-driving system, validated through 5+ years of driverless deployments and more than 1.7 million autonomous miles with zero at-fault incidents, paired with the Nuro Toolkit suite of supporting technology. Partners and customers include Uber and Lucid (premium robotaxi program with production-intent vehicles announced for CES 2026), Mercedes- Benz, Toyota, Kroger, Domino's, and Walmart, with NVIDIA participation in recent funding rounds. Nuro has offices in Mountain View, San Francisco, Santa Clara, Las Vegas, Houston, Toronto, Washington DC, Shenzhen, Tokyo, and an upcoming Munich expansion. Nuro does not publish a public developer API; the Driver and Toolkit are commercialized through B2B licensing rather than a self-serve developer portal.

providers.name: Aktoria Robotics
providers.description: Aktoria Robotics is a San Francisco-based robotics company (Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch) building a teleoperation and remote-operation layer for robots under the banner "Human as API for Robots." Its platform lets operators run any robot anywhere in the world, remotely collecting operational data from robot fleets 24 hours a day, monitoring and intervening in deployed fleets, and moving hardware through a train-to-deploy-to-monitor lifecycle. Founded in 2026 by Shreenabh Agrawal (robotics, Carnegie Mellon University) and Jaskaran Singh Walia (previously a researcher at Microsoft, MIT, CMU, Cambridge, and NUS), the company is at the pre-product-launch stage and does not yet publish a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation.

providers.name: Dyna Robotics
providers.description: Dyna Robotics is a Redwood City, California robotics AI company founded in 2024 by Lindon Gao, York Yang and Jason Ma to build robot foundation models for real-world commercial automation. Its DYNA-1 vision-language-action (VLA) model drives pairs of stationary robotic arms through high-dexterity tasks such as napkin folding and garment handling, and the company reports a 99%+ autonomous success rate over 24-hour continuous runs. Dyna targets commercial laundry, food service and factory environments, and closed a $120M Series A in September 2025 led by Robostrategy, CRV and First Round Capital with participation from NVentures, the Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, Salesforce Ventures, Samsung Next and LG Technology Ventures, following a $23.5M seed. Dyna sells robotics-as-a-service rather than software: enrichment probing of dyna.co found no public developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, SDK, developer portal, MCP server, agent card, or event surface.

providers.name: Iron Ox
providers.description: Iron Ox (legally Inevitable Tech, Inc.) was a San Carlos, California robotics company that built autonomous indoor farms — hydroponic greenhouses worked by mobile transport robots and a robotic arm that seeded, moved, imaged and harvested leafy greens and herbs, with machine learning used to spot pests and disease plant by plant. Founded in 2015 by Brandon Alexander and Jon Binney, it went through Y Combinator (W16), raised roughly $98 million in total including a $53 million Series C led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures in September 2021, and ran greenhouses in Gilroy, California and Lockhart, Texas. It cut about half its staff — roughly 50 people — in November 2022 and ceased operations in mid-2023. Iron Ox never ran a developer program: it sold produce, not software, and the only public code it ever shipped was internal ROS robotics tooling on GitHub. Its site, ironox.com, is now a GoDaddy parking lander and every developer subdomain has been removed from DNS, so there is no API, specification, SDK or documentation surface left to profile.

providers.name: Lemnos Labs
providers.description: Lemnos Labs, Inc. is an early-stage deeptech venture capital firm that invests at the earliest phases of hardware company formation, helping founders better understand their customer, anticipate problems, and leverage their assets. Lemnos contributes engineering, manufacturing, marketing, and financial capital alongside the check, and deliberately keeps a minimal public presence — its site is a single page that lists only the active portfolio. That portfolio spans robotics and autonomy (Built Robotics, Fort Robotics, Path Robotics, Scythe Robotics, Simbe Robotics, Petra), agricultural technology (FarmWise, Ceres Imaging), autonomous cargo aviation (Elroy Air), space data and precise positioning (Spire, Swift Navigation), simulation (Duality), video analytics (Lumeo), and physical security (Rhombus). Lemnos itself publishes no API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; it is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a venture-capital entity whose value to the network is its portfolio graph — several of its companies are meaningful API providers in their own right.

providers.name: Twolabs
providers.description: Twolabs is a San Francisco robotics startup (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building Tobi, a modular humanoid robot platform for builders to collect data, train skills, and deploy autonomous robots. The two-founder company vertically integrates hardware and AI in-house, streamlining robot training into a Record, Upload, Train, Deploy workflow, and is initially focused on caregiving applications in senior-care facilities such as feeding, dressing, medication reminders, mobility support, and companionship. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company; it does not yet publish a public developer API, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Unmannd
providers.description: Unmannd (Unmannd Autonomy Pvt Ltd) is an India-based defense technology company backed by Accel and Speciale Invest, engineering autonomous drones under the banner of aerial dominance. Its TITAN 30 is an autonomous defense-logistics drone with a 30 kg max payload, 60 km/h cruise speed, 20,000 ft operational ceiling, and 30 km max range; its FURY counter-UAS interceptor was announced as launching in Q1 2026. Unmannd is a hardware/defense company and publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs as of July 2026.

providers.name: Veo Robotics
providers.description: Veo Robotics built FreeMove, a 3D depth-sensing computer vision safety system that lets standard industrial robots work safely alongside people by monitoring workcells and dynamically restricting or resuming robot motion. Backed by GV and Lux Capital, the company's assets - including FreeMove and related intellectual property - were acquired by Symbotic in July 2024, and veobot.com now redirects to symbotic.com. Veo Robotics published no public API surface; this profile records the company in the API Evangelist network graph.

providers.name: Fourier Intelligence
providers.description: Fourier (Fourier Intelligence, founded 2015 and headquartered in Shanghai, China) is a full-stack robotics company that develops core robot technology and finished robot products. It began in rehabilitation robotics — exoskeletons and upper/lower-limb rehab devices such as the ArmMotus and ExoMotus lines and the RehabHub intelligent rehabilitation ecosystem — and has expanded into general-purpose humanoid robots (the GRx series, including GR-1 and GR-2), smart actuators (FSA), and dexterous hands. Fourier publishes first-party developer SDKs for robot control through its FFTAI GitHub organization: the RoCS (Robot Control System / General Robotics OS) client libraries for Python and JavaScript/TypeScript, and the fourier-grx control stack for the GRx humanoid series. Fourier is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. These are device/robot-control developer libraries rather than a hosted web API; the company publishes no public REST/OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Arlo Industries
providers.description: Arlo Industries is a San Francisco defense hardware company (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building a passive sensing network for detecting and tracking drones and aerial threats without traditional radar. Its product, Mentat, uses a distributed mesh architecture of low-cost sensors that cooperatively detect and track targets in 3D while remaining invisible to the threats they monitor. The company frames its approach around "asymmetric economics" — sensor deployment cost grows linearly while tracking accuracy grows exponentially — making the system more scalable than conventional radar installations. Arlo has demonstrated its technology with Ukrainian military operators on active frontlines and maintains partnerships across the US, Ukraine, and Northern Europe. As an early-stage hardware startup it publishes no public API, developer program, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Aurora Innovation
providers.description: Aurora Innovation is a Pittsburgh-headquartered autonomous-vehicle company publicly traded on NASDAQ as AUR. Its core product is the Aurora Driver, a self-driving system designed as a single platform deployable across vehicle classes - first commercialized in long-haul Class 8 trucking through Aurora Horizon, with Aurora Connect intended for ride-hailing applications. The Aurora Driver is integrated into the Volvo VNL Autonomous and PACCAR Peterbilt 579/Kenworth T680 trucks, uses Aurora's proprietary FirstLight FMCW lidar with 450+ metre range, and benefits from a NVIDIA-powered compute platform and Continental hardware partnership. Aurora launched commercial driverless freight operations in Texas in 2025 between Fort Worth, El Paso, Dallas, and Houston, with freight customers including Werner, Hirschbach, Uber Freight, FedEx, Schneider, Ryder, and Toyota Motor North America. Aurora does not publish a public developer API; the public surface is product, safety, and investor material.

providers.name: Coolant
providers.description: Coolant (Coolant Climate, Inc.) is a climate-technology startup building AI-powered forest monitoring and carbon measurement from consumer-grade drone imagery. Its "3D spatial intelligence" platform reconstructs high-resolution 3D forest models from ordinary drone footage (DJI Mini, Mavic) and applies computer vision to measure biomass, tree height, diameter at breast height (DBH), tree counts, species, and growth rates — delivering LiDAR-grade accuracy at a fraction of the cost. The company positions this as the measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) layer for scalable, verifiable carbon removal, reforestation success tracking, and conservation planning. Coolant raised a $4.3M seed round from General Catalyst and Floodgate in October 2025. As of this profile the company operates a marketing site, a demo web application, and a technical blog, but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Firnas Aero
providers.description: Firnas Aero is a Saudi Arabian deep-tech startup building autonomous Drone-in-a-Box (DiaB) systems for aerial surveillance, industrial inspection, and environmental assessment. Its turnkey platform pairs self-charging, robotic battery-swapping drone stations with cloud-based remote management over 5G, Ethernet, or Wi-Fi, and applies machine-learning and deep-learning models for anomaly detection, Foreign Object Debris (FOD) detection, hazard identification, and geo-location. Based at KRTP HQ in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia, the company serves infrastructure, energy, and security clients including Red Sea Global, NEOM, and the Saudi Electricity Company, and is backed by 500 Global. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Fortastra
providers.description: Fortastra is a spacecraft manufacturer building low-cost, maneuverable orbital defense systems designed for scalability and autonomous operation. Its spacecraft protect space-based infrastructure with autonomous navigation that detects, analyzes, and responds to orbital anomalies without relying on distant ground-based sensors. The company's open software architecture spans sensing, maneuvering, coordination, and response functions, and its hardware is validated through component testing, simulation, and orbital deployment. Surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta.

providers.name: Fyto
providers.description: Fyto is a Bay Area agricultural cleantech and robotics company, founded in 2019 by Jason Prapas with MIT origins, that builds automated cultivation systems for lemna — fast-growing aquatic "superplants" in the duckweed family. Its ReCover process, GrowGrid raised growbeds, and autonomous Harvester machine capture excess nutrients from dairy and livestock operations and convert them into high-protein animal feed, cutting nitrate pollution and greenhouse-gas emissions without arable land, synthetic fertilizer, or manual labor. Backed by GV, Fyto is scaling regenerative farming from California's San Joaquin Valley. No public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation is currently published.

providers.name: GITAI
providers.description: GITAI is a space robotics company building safe and affordable robotic labor for space. It develops robotic arms, spacecraft platforms, autonomous "Inchworm" robots, and lunar rovers for on-orbit servicing, satellite assembly and maintenance, and lunar and orbital infrastructure construction, working with customers and agencies such as NASA and JAXA. GITAI operates as a B2B and government contractor and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, SDK, or developer documentation; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched with the publicly observable web, blog, and domain-security surface only.

providers.name: IONA
providers.description: IONA (IONA Drones) is a UK-based autonomous drone delivery company building the full technology stack for logistics operators. Its tilt-rotor Sonnet aircraft performs VTOL from compact sites and carries up to 20 parcels up to 200 km per autonomous flight. IONA pairs the aircraft with an onboard autonomy operating system, GPS/LiDAR sensor-fusion precision landing, a SORA-aligned BVLOS compliance engine, an operations centre for real-time fleet monitoring and analytics, and a digital twin for simulation and predictive maintenance. The platform integrates with existing TMS/WMS logistics systems and targets healthcare, rural/remote, express e-commerce, industrial, and maritime delivery. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: MightyFly
providers.description: MightyFly is an autonomous air-logistics company building hybrid-electric eVTOL cargo aircraft for expedited, long-range, same-day deliveries. Its autonomous aircraft carry up to 500 pounds, travel up to 1,000 miles at roughly 150 MPH, and cut delivery emissions by around 64% versus traditional ground and air freight. MightyFly targets B2B logistics and defense delivery partnerships rather than offering a public developer platform. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer API, SDK, developer portal, or public specifications; this profile captures its public web presence and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Mobileye
providers.description: Mobileye is an Israel-headquartered ADAS and autonomous-driving technology company, majority-owned by Intel and publicly traded on NASDAQ as MBLY. Its flagship platform is the EyeQ family of purpose-built automotive systems-on-chip (EyeQ4, EyeQ5, EyeQ6L, EyeQ6H, EyeQ Ultra), shipped in over 175 million vehicles worldwide through partnerships with most major OEMs. Mobileye's solution portfolio spans entry-level ADAS, Mobileye SuperVision (eyes-on, hands-off highway and urban driving), Mobileye Chauffeur (eyes-off conditional autonomy), and Mobileye Drive (Level 4 full autonomy in robotaxi and goods-delivery applications). The company pioneered Responsibility- Sensitive Safety (RSS), a mathematical framework for AV decision safety contributed to IEEE standards work, and operates Road Experience Management (REM), a crowdsourced HD-mapping system that harvests anonymized road data from millions of consumer vehicles to build and update the Mobileye Roadbook. Mobileye does not publish a traditional public developer API; OEM and integration relationships are private B2B engagements.

providers.name: Movel AI
providers.description: Movel AI is a Singapore-based robotics deployment software company, founded in 2016, that makes it faster and cheaper to get autonomous mobile robots up and running in real-world environments. Its platform pairs deep learning, sensor fusion, and probabilistic planning so robots can perceive their surroundings and plan tasks on their own. Core products are the Movel Fleet Management System (FMS) for real-time monitoring and control of multi-robot fleets and Movel RNS (Robotic Navigation System) for precise single-robot navigation of complex spaces, applied across logistics, manufacturing, construction, and healthcare. The company is backed by Silicon Solution Ventures, 500 Global, AviTech, SGInnovate, Seeds Capital, and Enterprise Singapore. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Movel AI publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Quantum Systems
providers.description: Quantum-Systems GmbH is a Gilching/Munich, Germany-based dual-use drone manufacturer founded in 2015 by former Bundeswehr helicopter pilot Florian Seibel. The company designs, builds, and operates small electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) fixed-wing unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) for reconnaissance, intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition (RSTA), surveying, and mapping. Its flagship platforms include the Trinity Pro (mapping/surveying VTOL with up to 90-minute endurance), the Vector tactical reconnaissance drone (the de facto main small UAS supplier to the German Bundeswehr and, with 619+ systems delivered as of April 2025, one of the most-used Western reconnaissance drones in Ukraine), the Reliant long-range Group 2 ISR/RSTA platform built for the U.S. market with 10+ hours endurance and hot-swappable MOD-compliant payload bays (EO/IR, SIGINT, EW, CRPA), and the Ukraine-manufactured Sparta drone carrier that delivers two FPV drones to a 200 km combat radius. All platforms are operated through QBase 3D, Quantum-Systems' proprietary Windows-based mission planning, control, and post-processing software with integrated ESRI terrain data and direct export to Pix4D, Agisoft, Propeller, and Trimble Business Center. The Vector tactical line is built on Auterion's flight stack. Backed by HV Capital, DTCP, Thiel Capital, Project A, Airbus Ventures, and Omnes Capital, the company reached unicorn status in May 2025 as "Europe's first dual-use unicorn." Quantum-Systems supplies the militaries of Germany, the United States, Ukraine, Australia, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Romania, and Spain. There is no public developer API, REST endpoint, SDK, or open-source release for QBase 3D or any Quantum-Systems platform; integration with Pix4D/Agisoft/Propeller/Trimble is via standard photogrammetry file exchange (GeoTIFF, RAW imagery, flight logs), not a programmable API.

providers.name: SiLC
providers.description: SiLC Technologies is a silicon photonics company headquartered in Monrovia, California that builds integrated single-chip FMCW (frequency-modulated continuous-wave) LiDAR — coherent 4D vision systems that capture depth, instantaneous velocity via micro-Doppler, and dual-polarization intensity from one photonic chip. Its Eyeonic product family spans Eyeonic Trace Ultra (a Class 1 laser line scanner for industrial automation and inspection), Eyeonic Vista (an ultra-long-range perimeter security and counter-UAS vision system with detection beyond 2 km), and Eyeonic Edge (high-precision 4D inspection of large objects). The company sells sensors, modules and vision chips to industrial and AI robotics, perimeter security, and mobility customers. It was founded by Dr. Mehdi Asghari and is backed in part by Honda. SiLC ships hardware, not software services: as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Skild AI
providers.description: Skild AI is a Pittsburgh-founded robotics AI company developing the Skild Brain, a general-purpose, omni-bodied physical AI system intended to control many different robot embodiments across many tasks without being tied to a specific hardware design. The company is initially targeting three application platforms: security and inspection robots that can navigate dangerous environments, mobile manipulation systems combining grasping and navigation, and autonomous packing with dexterous skills. Skild publishes a research blog discussing topics such as learning from humans and video data. The company is backed by Sequoia, General Catalyst, Felicis, SoftBank, Bezos Expeditions, and other investors. Skild AI does not currently publish a public API, SDK, model weights, or developer documentation; commercial engagement appears to run through direct partnerships and pilots.

providers.name: Tekever
providers.description: Tekever is a multinational defence technology company headquartered in Lisbon, Portugal, with operations in the United Kingdom (Bath and a planned large-scale drone production facility in Swindon), France (Toulouse and Cahors), and the United States (Fayetteville, North Carolina). Founded in 2001, the company specialises in AI-driven autonomy for civil and defence missions, with its core business centred on long-endurance Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) used for Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), maritime surveillance, and electronic warfare. Its flagship platforms include the AR3, a configurable medium-range tactical UAS (designated StormShroud in service with the UK Royal Air Force), the AR5, a SATCOM-enabled long-endurance maritime and land ISR aircraft, and the ARX, a next-generation system positioned as the company's game changer. These platforms are paired with ATLAS, Tekever's real-time intelligence-as-a-service platform that fuses sensor and satellite data into actionable mission intelligence. Tekever drones are operated by the UK Ministry of Defence, the British Army, the Armed Forces of Ukraine (with the UK having committed approximately £270 million in Tekever UAVs for Ukraine since the start of the Russian invasion), the European Maritime Safety Agency under a €30 million contract, the French Ministry of Armed Forces (CNES/DGA), Portugal, and NATO. The company also develops satellite technology and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) capabilities to extend its intelligence services beyond the airborne domain. Tekever's revenue model is built on government and defence contracts, platform sales, and managed ISR-as-a-service offerings; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release, and engagement with the company is conducted through direct sales, government procurement, and partnership channels.

providers.name: 6river
providers.description: 6 River Systems (6RS) is a warehouse fulfillment automation company founded in 2015 in Waltham, Massachusetts. Its flagship product is "Chuck," a collaborative autonomous mobile robot (AMR) that works alongside human associates to guide and optimize picking, sorting, and replenishment in distribution centers. The platform is WMS-agnostic and integrates with existing warehouse-management systems as an intelligent execution layer via a private/partner REST API for host data exchange; it does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or consumer SDKs. Norwest Venture Partners was an early investor; the company was acquired by Shopify in 2019 and by Ocado Group in 2023. The public marketing site at 6river.com currently serves a parked lander stub.

providers.name: AICE
providers.description: AICE is a defense-technology company building the next generation of underwater defense systems: autonomous swarms of modular marine drones that secure naval assets and coastal infrastructure against evolving underwater threats. Founded in 2026 by former NASA engineer Gregoire Chomette and European Robotics Champion Remi Bouteiller, the company is part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, is based in the San Francisco Bay Area with hardware manufactured in France, and applies swarm robotics and AI to surveillance, detection, and protection of critical subsea infrastructure. AICE currently ships hardware and does not publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bestmile
providers.description: Bestmile was a Swiss fleet-orchestration SaaS company, spun out of EPFL in Lausanne in 2014, whose cloud platform planned, dispatched and optimized mixed fleets of autonomous and human-driven vehicles for on-demand mobility and transit operators. The platform was described by the company as API-first, with documented Fleet, Booking and Transportation APIs for integrating operator booking apps, fleet-management systems and traveler-information systems. The company no longer operates: ZF Friedrichshafen acquired Bestmile's technology in November 2021 and folded it into its own SCALAR fleet-orchestration platform, so any successor API belongs to ZF rather than to Bestmile. As of 2026-08-17 bestmile.com is a parked Gandi.net registrar domain that refuses HTTPS, and no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, package or /.well-known surface survives. Surfaced originally as a Partech portfolio company.

providers.name: Boson Motors
providers.description: Boson Motors is an electric vehicle and robotics company founded in 2017, building a modular electric off-road utility vehicle (UTV) platform for agriculture, farm automation, and work applications. Its flagship LX40 is a user-serviceable, low-maintenance electric 4WD UTV that charges from a standard 110v outlet and accepts interchangeable work modules for spraying, hauling, and crew transport. The company operates engineering and production out of Tada, Andhra Pradesh, India, with a strategic base in Fremont, California, and maintains a robotics arm (Boson Robotics) focused on autonomous and agricultural automation. Boson Motors is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. As of this profile it publishes a consumer marketing and reservation site with no public developer program, API, SDK, or developer documentation; its public engineering footprint is a GitHub organization of ROS/robotics libraries. This profile is maintained as an API Evangelist network lead and enrichment target.

providers.name: Elorian AI
providers.description: Elorian AI Inc is a Palo Alto, California frontier AI research company founded in 2025 and emerged from stealth in April 2026, building foundation models for visual reasoning — models that process visual input directly rather than first converting imagery into text, with the stated goal of advancing toward "visual AGI" for applications in architecture, automotive, manufacturing and robotics. It was co-founded by Andrew Dai (CEO, formerly Google Brain and DeepMind, first author of the 2015 work introducing LM pretraining followed by supervised fine-tuning, co-lead of GLaM and PaLM 2 pretraining), Yinfei Yang (Chief Multimodal Architect, formerly Apple Foundation Model Multimodal and co-creator of ALIGN at Google Research) and Seth Neel (formerly a Harvard professor researching data-centric generative AI), with Dustin Tran (formerly xAI post-training lead) as Chief Reasoning Architect. The company raised a $55M seed round at a reported $300M valuation with Nvidia and Menlo Ventures as strategic partners, and was named to the Forbes Next Billion-Dollar Startups 2026 list. As of this profiling pass Elorian is pre-product: its site states the first foundation visual thinking model will be released "later this year" and offers only an early-access waitlist. It publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no machine-readable specification, and no public API host.

providers.name: Embark Trucks
providers.description: Embark Trucks was an autonomous-trucking company founded in 2016 and backed by Y Combinator, building a self-driving software stack (the Embark Driver) for Class 8 semi-trucks operating on interstate highway freight lanes. The company went public via a SPAC merger with Northern Star Investment Corp II in late 2021, but wound down operations in November 2023 after failing to secure additional funding; its autonomous-driving technology and engineering assets were subsequently acquired by Applied Intuition. Embark never operated a public developer platform, REST API, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile is an identity record rather than a live API. Its only surviving public technical surface is the embarktrucks GitHub organization, which hosts open-source robotics and autonomous-vehicle tooling (ROS drivers, LIDAR/camera integrations, and the webviz visualization libraries) rather than first-party API client SDKs.

providers.name: Foundation Robotics Labs
providers.description: Foundation Robotics Labs — trading publicly as Foundation and incorporated as Foundation Future Industries, Inc. — is a San Francisco humanoid robotics company founded in April 2024 by Sankaet Pathak, Arjun Sethi and Mike LeBlanc. It builds Phantom, a general-purpose humanoid robot aimed at industrial automation, logistics, inspection, disaster response and defense, and Cortex, the company's self-described physics foundation model built on Deep Variational Bayes Filters that pairs physics-informed prediction with vision-language reasoning to drive the robot. The company's published master plan runs from building humanoids through fleet coherence and on to building cities, and it states explicitly that it designs for military environments, unlike U.S. competitors committed to non-weaponization. Foundation has raised a reported $111M and is traded on the secondary market via Forge Global. As of this profile Foundation publishes NO public developer surface — no developer portal, documentation, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI definition, SDK, package, MCP server or agent card. Its entire public web presence is a five-page Framer marketing site (home, Phantom, Cortex, master plan, culture, careers) with no /docs, /developers, /api, /pricing, /terms or /privacy paths and no llms.txt. Its GitHub organization (github.com/foundationbot, verified first-party by @foundation.bot commit-author domains) holds internal test benches and forks of open-source robotics tooling — Drake, jetson-containers, Kalibr, PlotJuggler, Fast-DDS, an EtherCAT master, actuator dyno benches and NXP S32K MCU demos — and contains no API specification of any kind.

providers.name: INDEX Robotics
providers.description: INDEX Robotics is a South Korean humanoid robotics startup based in Seongnam (Bundang) building high-precision actuators and upper-body humanoid robots for high-mix, low-volume industrial work. Its core products are the IA Series, a family of high-precision actuators purpose-built for humanoid joints, and INDEX01, a compact upper-body humanoid prototype that deliberately foregoes a mobile base so it can slot into constrained factory workspaces for logistics handling, machining support, and precision assembly. The company treats joint precision, responsiveness under sustained repetitive motion, and long-run performance consistency as the core unsolved problems in humanoid commercialization. In February 2026 INDEX Robotics closed a $1M (KRW 1.5B) seed round led by Futureplay with Bass Ventures and 500 Global co-investing. This is a hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Local Motors
providers.description: Local Motors was an American vehicle manufacturer founded in 2007 by John "Jay" Rogers Jr. that built vehicles through open co-creation and distributed "microfactories" rather than conventional mass production. Its community designed and the company produced the Rally Fighter off-road car from its first Chandler, Arizona microfactory, the Strati — the first car to be 3D-printed live, in 44 hours at IMTS 2014 — and, from 2016, Olli, a 3D-printed electric autonomous shuttle whose conversational passenger interface ran on IBM Watson and which was piloted at National Harbor, Maryland and other campus and transit sites. The company operated microfactories in Chandler, Knoxville and National Harbor and spun its crowdsourcing community out as Launch Forth. Local Motors ceased operations in January 2022 after fifteen years, having failed to raise further capital, and its intellectual-property portfolio was acquired by drone manufacturer RapidFlight of Manassas, Virginia in July 2023. Local Motors never operated a public developer program: the archive of localmotors.com holds an internal django-tastypie JSON API under /api/v1/ that served the co-creation community website, but no developer portal, API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification was ever published, and its GitHub organization has zero public repositories. The domain is no longer the company's — it now answers HTTP 301 on every path to a third-party affiliate article — so there is no live API surface to catalog. This profile is retained as a historical record.

providers.name: NODA AI
providers.description: NODA AI is a defense-technology company building autonomous force orchestration for the frontlines. Founded in 2024 in Austin, Texas by Global War on Terrorism veterans, it develops URZA, an AI-native strategic orchestration platform that acts as a tactics repository and reasoning engine for real-time task brokering across vendor-agnostic, mixed-fleet autonomous assets, integrated with 30+ OEM vehicles and control systems from subsurface to space; and LARIA, a synthetic weapons-and-tactics training environment that uses digital-twin modeling to develop and test autonomous plays. In February 2026 the company raised a $25M Series A led by Bessemer Venture Partners to serve the U.S. Department of War, the Intelligence Community, and the UK Ministry of Defense. NODA AI is a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and Bloomberg Beta. It publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDKs; its GitHub organization holds no public repositories.

providers.name: Philon
providers.description: Philon is a Y Combinator-backed robotics research company building open-source, general-purpose humanoid robots capable of performing unsafe, repetitive, or boring tasks. Philon develops foundational AI models for embodied agents, including Holo 1.0, a generalist vision-language-action model that navigates virtual 3D worlds and completes hour-long objectives, alongside research on generative memory, focused attention for massive context windows, and latent steering of action experts. The company publishes its models and research code openly on GitHub.

providers.name: Pony.ai
providers.description: Pony.ai is a global autonomous-mobility company founded in Silicon Valley in 2016 and dual-headquartered in Guangzhou and Fremont. Its core technology is the Pony "virtual driver", a Level 4 autonomous driving stack deployed across three business lines: Robotaxi (PonyPilot+ ride-hailing service operating in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen, plus pilots in California and Arizona), Robotruck (autonomous heavy-duty trucking in China), and Personally Owned Vehicle (POV) intelligent driving software for production passenger cars. The company is publicly listed on NASDAQ under PONY and reports more than 32 million kilometres of autonomous road testing. Pony.ai does not publish a traditional public developer API; its public GitHub presence includes infrastructure tooling such as pony_aim (experiment tracker) and bazel-buildfarm rather than the AV stack itself. This profile captures the company surface and any developer-relevant artifacts.

providers.name: Valinor
providers.description: Valinor Enterprises is a defense and government technology operational holding company — a "company of companies" that builds and buys mission-critical technologies to fill the gaps others ignore. It centralizes go-to-market, compliance, security, and operations while decentralizing engineering across lean Product Companies including Condor (attritable aerial systems), Dispatch (drone charging infrastructure, selected by DIU for the CADDS program), Harbor (expeditionary medical systems for the Marine Corps), Reflex (smart optics with onboard vision models), and Streamline (AI-enabled data collection with structured ontology write-back). Backed by General Catalyst; raised a $54M Series A led by Friends & Family Capital. Valinor publishes no public API or developer portal; its developer footprint is a GitHub organization and the @valinor-enterprises npm scope.

providers.name: 6thSense
providers.description: 6thSense is a physical-AI hardware company building the touch layer for dexterous robots. It designs and manufactures wearable tactile-sensing data gloves that capture how human hands interact with the world — pressure, contact, grip, and 3D hand pose — alongside custom tactile skin molded to robot hands. Its capture stack synchronizes eight aligned modalities (tactile and pressure proxies, egocentric video, depth/RGB-D, hand pose, motion and IMU dynamics, wrist and scene cameras, dense labels and commentary, and success/failure outcomes) into model-ready demonstration datasets used to train the next generation of dexterous, manipulation-capable robots. Founded in 2026 in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (S26).

providers.name: 9 Mothers Corporation
providers.description: 9 Mothers Corporation is a defense technology company founded in 2024 and based in Austin, Texas, building AI-powered counter-drone (C-sUAS) point defense systems for the FPV drone era. Its flagship product, EDDA, is a small, low-power, autonomous-capable point-defense turret that engages Group 1 suicide drones at 10-100+ meter range to protect soldiers, vehicles, and critical assets. A Y Combinator Spring 2026 company with reported sales to the U.S. Department of War, its roadmap includes Vor (passive acoustic sensor), Atla (belt-fed shotgun system), and Gleipnir (counter-drone for larger platforms). This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. The company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Advanced Metal Research
providers.description: Advanced Metal Research is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) company based in Los Angeles building machine intelligence for American welding. The company develops American-made robotic welding cells that pair computer vision with real-time seam tracking and post-weld inspection, turning welding from a scarce manual craft into a closed-loop manufacturing system that learns from every weld as it happens. Founded in 2025 by Julian Fried, Stephen Lin, and Angus Muffatti, it targets the projected shortage of skilled welding professionals across US industrial manufacturing. The company is early-stage and hardware-focused; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Aerodome
providers.description: Aerodome was a Drone-as-First-Responder (DFR) company founded in 2023 by former California police officer Rahul Sidhu (CEO) and Kenaniah Cerny (Chief Architect). It built a fully integrated, automated, and remotely operated software platform that let public-safety agencies dispatch autonomous drones directly from 911 calls, pairing DJI drone hardware, robotic battery-swap docking nests, and radar with Aerodome DFR software featuring augmented-reality street overlays, automated flight operations, computer-aided-dispatch integration, and live airspace awareness. The company reported average 86-second response times to 911 calls. Backed by a16z, CRV, and 2048 Ventures across a seed (Oct 2023) and $21.5M Series A (May 2024), Aerodome was acquired by Flock Safety in October 2024 for over $300 million; its technology and software now ship as the Flock Safety "Flock DFR" product line, and the aerodome.com domain redirects to that product page.

providers.name: AirMap
providers.description: AirMap was a drone airspace-management and unmanned traffic management (UTM) platform that provided airspace intelligence, flight planning, digital notice, and geofencing services for drones and their operators, exposed through a developer platform of airspace and flight APIs. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of bullpen-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead. As of this enrichment pass (2026-07) the company appears defunct: airmap.com no longer serves a developer portal or API and now resolves to a parked Squarespace-hosted page with a mismatched TLS certificate, and the legacy developer.airmap.com / api.airmap.com / docs.airmap.com hosts no longer resolve. No live API surface remains to harvest.

providers.name: Airware
providers.description: Airware was an enterprise commercial-drone (UAV) software and aerial-data-analytics company founded in 2011 by Jonathan Downey and headquartered in San Francisco. It began by building an operating system and autopilot for commercial drones, then pivoted to a cloud-based "Aerial Information Platform" that captured, processed, and analyzed drone imagery for enterprise verticals such as mining, quarrying, insurance, and construction. Airware acquired French drone-analytics firm Redbird in 2016 and raised roughly $118M from investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Kleiner Perkins, GV (Google Ventures), Intel Capital, and Next World Capital. The company ceased operations in September 2018. It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; no live developer surface, API, or public specification is currently discoverable (the airware.com domain no longer resolves), so this profile is retained as a historical/defunct record.

providers.name: Aitme
providers.description: Aitme was a Berlin-based deep-tech robotics company that built a platform for automated food preparation, deploying robotic kitchen and canteen systems that cooked and assembled meals autonomously for foodservice and workplace-catering settings. Surfaced as a portfolio company of HV Capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment, the company has since been acquired and exposes no public developer surface: no documented API, developer portal, SDKs, or hosted domain could be located during enrichment. This profile is retained as an honest catalog record with no fabricated API artifacts.

providers.name: American Aerospace Advisors
providers.description: American Aerospace Technologies, Inc., doing business as American Aerospace Advisors, is a defense and critical-infrastructure monitoring company based in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania. It provides end-to-end airborne intelligence systems that combine unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), airborne sensors, analytics, and communications to deliver near-real-time data through a cloud-based intelligence gateway. Its flagship AiRanger medium-altitude long-endurance unmanned aircraft and InstiMaps sensor technology support pipeline and linear-asset patrol, beyond-visual-line-of-sight (BVLOS) flight services, sensor integration, and aviation policy consulting. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Axon
providers.description: Axon is an early-stage artificial intelligence company building real-time predictive intelligence on a brain-inspired architecture. Its approach centers on small, efficient "world models" that learn continuously on-device rather than depending on large models or the cloud, giving an edge-first design lower latency and lower cost. The initial focus is high-frequency trading and capital markets, where real-time prediction is decisive, with future applications targeted at wearables, edge devices, and robotics. Axon is backed by Northzone, Concept Ventures, a16z Speedrun, and EWOR. As of this profile the company is pre-product with no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal; this repository tracks it in the API Evangelist network for enrichment as its developer surface emerges.

providers.name: Bear Flag Robotics
providers.description: Bear Flag Robotics is an autonomous-tractor company that retrofits existing farm tractors with sensors, onboard compute, and path-planning software to enable driverless field operations such as tillage and row-crop work. Founded in 2017 and backed by Y Combinator and True Ventures, the company was acquired by John Deere in August 2021 and now advances Deere's autonomy roadmap. It is a hardware and agricultural-robotics business with no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or GitHub surface; its website redirects to John Deere.

providers.name: Bumblebee Spaces
providers.description: Bumblebee Spaces is a San Francisco smart-home robotics company that builds app-controlled motorized storage systems for compact urban living. Its ceiling-mounted robotic units lift beds, closets, and storage bins up and out of the way, reclaiming floor space in small apartments, while a built-in camera and mobile app track and retrieve stored belongings on demand. The company sells and installs hardware plus a companion consumer mobile application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Canaan Partners, the profile is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Calibrate Ventures
providers.description: Calibrate Ventures is a Pasadena, California venture capital firm backing visionary technical founders scaling deep tech to transform industries such as transportation and logistics, food and agriculture, healthcare, manufacturing, security, and warehousing. The firm invests in AI, computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and automation startups, partnering with founders to turn a technical breakthrough into scalable commercial advantage and drawing on decades of combined investment and company-building experience. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-adjacent company in the API Evangelist network and enriched from the firm's public web presence.

providers.name: Carmera *
providers.description: CARMERA was a New York City based road-intelligence and HD mapping company that provided "change-as-a-service" map maintenance for autonomous driving, mobility-as-a-service and consumer navigation. It used consumer-grade cameras mounted on commercial fleet vehicles as crowdsourced visual probes to detect permanent road inventory change (signs, signals, lane markings) and temporary closure events (construction), then regenerated both HD and SD maps in near real time. Its commercial offering was described as detection APIs that identify map-impacting events plus vector APIs that deliver map updates, layered over a customer-supplied or CARMERA-supplied base map. The company was backed by GV and was acquired in July 2021 by Woven Planet (now Woven by Toyota), the advanced mobility subsidiary of Toyota Motor Corporation. Its APIs were sold under enterprise agreements and were never published as a public developer program; as of this enrichment pass the carmera.com domain no longer resolves and no developer portal, documentation, SDK, or API artifact survives.

providers.name: chowbotics
providers.description: Chowbotics was a food-robotics company known for "Sally," a fresh-food and salad vending robot that assembled customized bowls on demand for cafeterias, hospitals, campuses, and grocery locations. The company was acquired by DoorDash in early 2021 and no longer operates as a standalone business; its domain (chowbotics.com) now redirects to DoorDash (get.doordash.com). As of this enrichment pass Chowbotics publishes no independent developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or other machine-readable developer surface, so this remains an identity-only record in the API Evangelist network rather than an active API provider profile.

providers.name: Citadel
providers.description: Citadel (also branded Citadel Defense / Drone Citadel) is a counter-unmanned-aircraft-system (C-UAS) company founded in 2016 that built an automated, modular drone-defense solution using proprietary machine-learning algorithms to detect, classify, and defeat unauthorized drones. It raised a Lightspeed Venture Partners Series A in 2017 and was subsequently acquired by BlueHalo. The company operates no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface, and its standalone domains (citadeldefense.com, dronecitadel.com) are now parked or no longer resolve.

providers.name: Congruent
providers.description: Congruent builds AI-native radar hardware and simulation tooling for self-driving cars and end-to-end autonomy. The company pairs a radar architecture that exposes raw sensor data with a world-model-based generative simulator, producing both real and synthetic raw radar returns to train autonomy stacks. Radar is the only depth sensor cheap enough to scale to every vehicle while still working in rain, fog, snow, and dust, where camera and lidar systems degrade. Congruent is an early-stage Y Combinator (W26) company founded in 2025 by Clement Barthes and Evan Scope Crafts, based in the San Francisco Bay Area. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this profile the company operates a single marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or specification.

providers.name: Cruise
providers.description: Cruise was an autonomous-vehicle (robotaxi) company founded in 2013 and majority-owned by General Motors, building self-driving technology and operating driverless ride-hail services in San Francisco and other U.S. cities. Backed by GM, Honda, SoftBank Vision Fund, Spark Capital, Y Combinator and others, Cruise suspended operations after a 2023 incident and, in December 2024, GM announced it would end robotaxi development and fold the Cruise team into GM's own autonomous and driver-assistance programs. As of 2026 the getcruise.com domain 301-redirects to GM's autonomous-driving pages. Cruise never published a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Curious Ai
providers.description: The Curious AI Company was a Helsinki, Finland-based artificial intelligence research company founded in 2015 by Harri Valpola (previously founder of ZenRobotics) along with Antti Rasmus, Mathias Berglund, Tapani Raiko, and Timo Haanpaa.
