The company pursued artificial general intelligence, real-world computer vision for robots, and interactive, autonomous, and semi-supervised machine learning, and is best known for foundational research on Ladder Networks for semi-supervised deep learning. It raised roughly 4.7M USD from investors including DCVC, Lifeline Ventures, and Invus, and was acquired by Apple in January 2021. The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public developer platform, API, documentation, or SDKs. This record is retained as a DCVC portfolio identity profile; there is no active API surface to enrich.

providers.name: CYGIA
providers.description: CYGIA (Zhuhai CYGIA Automation Equipment Co.) is an intelligent-factory equipment and solution provider founded in 2006 and headquartered in Zhuhai, China. It develops, manufactures, and services intelligent automation and automated-test equipment for consumer electronics, semiconductor and integrated-circuit, automotive, medical, and new-energy industries. Once backed by Qiming Venture Partners, CYGIA became a subsidiary of publicly traded CYG (Changyuan Group, Shanghai Stock Exchange 600525.SH) in 2015. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a VC-portfolio lead; enrichment found no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDK surface for CYGIA, which is a hardware/automation-equipment manufacturer rather than an API provider.

providers.name: DeepMap
providers.description: DeepMap was a high-definition mapping and localization software company for autonomous vehicles, building HD maps, real-time localization, and map-update infrastructure that let self-driving cars know precisely where they were. Backed by a16z and Accel, DeepMap was acquired by NVIDIA in 2021 and folded into NVIDIA's autonomous-vehicle platform; the deepmap.ai domain now resolves to NVIDIA's self-driving solutions page. No independent DeepMap developer portal, documentation, or public API surface exists post-acquisition. This profile is retained as a network/portfolio record.

providers.name: Degla Inc
providers.description: Degla is a Y Combinator (Fall 2026) startup building an autonomous aerial intelligence layer that turns natural language into multi-drone mission execution. Operators describe an objective in plain language and Degla plans the mission, assigns aircraft, defines coverage patterns, and deploys a fleet that adapts in real time — with no waypoints, flight plans, or specialized training required. The platform targets search and rescue, emergency response, infrastructure inspection, and other critical field operations. Founded in 2026 by Aziz Hanafi and based in Boston, the company is in early access and has not yet published a public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: DiDi Autonomous
providers.description: DiDi Autonomous Driving (滴滴自动驾驶) is the autonomous-driving subsidiary of Chinese mobility giant DiDi. Founded as an internal research unit in 2016 and spun out as an independent company in 2019, it develops Level 4 self-driving technology and operates robotaxi services integrated into the DiDi ride-hailing platform in Chinese cities including Shanghai and Guangzhou. In 2020 SoftBank Vision Fund led a roughly $500M funding round into the unit. As a hardware- and fleet-oriented autonomous mobility operator it does not currently publish a public developer or API surface; this profile tracks it as a SoftBank Vision Fund portfolio company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Drishti Technologies
providers.description: Drishti Technologies was a Mountain View, California company (founded 2016 by Prasad Akella, Krishnendu Chaudhury, and Ashish Gupta) that applied AI-powered computer vision and video analytics to manual assembly lines in manufacturing. Its platform digitized human actions on the production floor to enable time-and-motion studies at scale, quality traceability, and continuous improvement, with products including Drishti Trace (video capture and traceability) and Drishti Flow (line analytics). The company was acquired by Apple in September 2023 and no longer operates an independent public website, developer portal, or API surface — its domains (drishti.com, drishti.ai) no longer resolve to a live product.

providers.name: Earendil Robotics
providers.description: Earendil Robotics is a Y Combinator-backed defense technology company registered in England and Wales that builds AI-powered situational-awareness and counter-drone systems for tactical units. Its product line includes IVAS, an edge-AI vision-augmentation system fusing night vision, thermal imaging, and laser ranging for total-darkness operation; Aeglos, an autonomous high-speed (300+ km/h) interceptor drone for counter-UAS defense with autonomous target locking and all-weather thermal tracking; and Holo, an ultra-lightweight dual-mode tactical sight combining high-resolution thermal imaging with a fiber-optic reticle. As of this profile the company exposes only a public marketing website and a contact form, with no published developer surface, API, SDKs, documentation, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: Eden Robotics
providers.description: Eden Robotics is a Y Combinator-backed robotics company building autonomous robots for industrial operations, delivered on a robots-as-a-service model that starts at roughly $10 per hour with no setup fees. The offering is positioned as plug-and-play, requiring no on-site engineers or specialized robotics hires, and is powered by the company's Theta OS platform. As of this profile the company publishes a single marketing and sales-contact website and does not expose a public API, developer portal, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition; this record captures the verified company identity and domain-security posture and will be upgraded if and when a developer surface is published.

providers.name: Eka Robotics
providers.description: Eka Robotics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts robotics-AI company founded in 2025 that is building intelligence for the physical world in its native language: force. Its Vision-Force-Action (VFA) model combines vision, force sensing, and action to give robots generality, performance, and safety for close human-robot interaction. The team pioneers self-supervised robot learning, large-scale robot learning, world models, reinforcement learning, and sim-to-real transfer, drawing talent from MIT, Berkeley, Harvard, DeepMind, and Boston Dynamics. Co-founded by MIT professor Pulkit Agrawal (Improbable AI Lab), the company is an early-stage research-and-hardware venture and does not yet publish a public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched with the company's public identity for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: EraDrive
providers.description: EraDrive is a space technology company building compact, AI-powered self-driving modules that give spacecraft onboard autonomy — vision-based navigation, control, collision avoidance, and situational awareness computed at the edge. A Stanford Space Rendezvous Laboratory (SLAB) spinoff founded by Sumant Sharma (CEO), Justin Kruger (CTO), and Prof. Simone D'Amico (CSO), EraDrive integrates flight-proven autonomy software with existing satellite infrastructure for space traffic management, on-orbit servicing and logistics, and advanced remote sensing across commercial and defense missions. The company closed an oversubscribed $5.3M seed round in December 2025, co-led by Haystack Ventures with participation from Point Nine, Harpoon Ventures, Brave Capital, 2100 VC, and Entropy Industrial Capital. As an early-stage hardware/software company, EraDrive currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Fern Bot
providers.description: Fern (operating as Ishiki Labs) is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) physical-AI startup building high-fidelity, custom robot world models that let robotics companies evaluate and train their robot policies at scale in software. Fern provides plug-and-play reinforcement-learning environments generated from a foundational world model: robotics teams seed varied starting scenes from their production environments, test and improve policies entirely in simulation, and Fern generates RL heads on top of existing policies to raise speed and success rates — a continual-learning flywheel where production robots improve every week. Founded in 2025 by CEO Amit Yadav (ex-Meta LLaMA / Reality Labs research scientist) and CTO Robert Xu (ex-Meta Reality Labs and Citadel Securities). As of this profile Fern publishes a marketing site, a whitepaper, and case studies but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Figure
providers.description: Figure is a Sunnyvale, California humanoid robotics company building general-purpose bipedal robots for the home and the workplace. Its current flagship product is Figure 03, marketed as an everyday general-purpose humanoid robot, succeeding Figure 01 and Figure 02. Figure develops Helix, an in-house Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that unifies perception, language understanding, and learned control to drive a full upper humanoid body at 35 degrees of freedom and 200 Hz, with capabilities including novel-object manipulation from natural-language commands and multi-robot task coordination. Figure has run commercial pilots with partners such as BMW and previously collaborated with OpenAI on language models. The company's revenue model is robot sales/leasing and enterprise deployments; Helix is a proprietary on-board model and there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Figure or Helix.

providers.name: FireVisor
providers.description: FireVisor is an AI-based manufacturing analytics platform that helps manufacturers leverage their production data beyond traditional defect detection and process control methods. Founded in 2018 and headquartered in Singapore (with a secondary office in Toronto, Canada), FireVisor works toward "self-aware factories powered by artificial intelligence," applying machine learning to manufacturing and industrial-automation data. It is a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this profile the public firevisor.com site returns a 404 from its load balancer and exposes no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Flirtey
providers.description: Flirtey was a drone-delivery technology company founded in 2013 by Matthew Sweeny and Tom Bass, backed by Y Combinator. It pioneered autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle delivery, conducting the first FAA-approved drone delivery in the United States in 2016 (Nevada) and running early delivery trials with partners including Domino's (the first pizza delivered by drone, in New Zealand) and 7-Eleven. Flirtey developed the Flirtey Eagle delivery drone and portable landing/loading systems aimed at medical, food, and retail last-mile logistics. The company is now defunct: it did not maintain a public developer program or API, and the flirtey.com domain has since been sold and now redirects to an unrelated business (us-stemcell.com). This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical company record with no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Forge Robotics
providers.description: Forge Robotics is a Galway, Ireland and San Francisco based robotics company building modular autonomous factories for metal fabrication. Its shipping container sized, software configurable units combine a vision system, sub millimeter 3D scanning, and robotic intelligence to autonomously handle, position, weld, laser engrave, and finish metal assemblies, turning conventional human programmed industrial welding robot arms into autonomous members of the workforce. The company targets the skilled welder shortage in US manufacturing with continuously operating, snap together production modules. Forge Robotics was co founded by Eoin Cobbe (CEO) and Robert Cormican (CTO) and is a Y Combinator backed pre seed startup. As of this profile the company exposes a marketing and product website only, with no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Fulfil
providers.description: Fulfil (Fulfil Solutions) is an automation company that builds robotic online-grocery fulfillment systems. Its ShopBot robots perform zero-labor pick-and-pack across all grocery temperatures and categories (ambient, refrigerated, frozen, and produce), providing item-level data and control with claimed 99% order accuracy and roughly 50% lower operating costs. The company operates automated micro-fulfillment facilities and partners with grocery and delivery operators. Backed by DCVC, Fulfil was surfaced as a portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; it publishes a marketing website but no public developer, API, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: galbot
providers.description: Galbot (银河通用机器人, "Galaxy Universal Robotics") is the official site of a general-purpose, embodied-AI robotics company. It was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm Qiming and profiled here for API and developer-surface enrichment. As of this enrichment pass Galbot publishes only a marketing website rendered as a client-side single-page app; no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or MCP surface could be discovered. The only machine-readable signals captured are the DNS, TLS, and email-authentication (SPF/DMARC) posture of the galbot.com domain.

providers.name: General Instinct
providers.description: General Instinct is a San Francisco company (Y Combinator Spring 2026) building the deployment layer for physical AI. Founded in 2026 by Bill Jiao and Guanming Wang, it distills, quantizes, and deploys large frontier AI models onto constrained edge hardware so robotics, drone, and physical-AI teams can run low-latency models fully offline on devices like NVIDIA Jetson, mobile NPUs, ARM CPUs, the Apple Neural Engine, and Snapdragon. Its first product, Instinct Edge, takes a model, a target device, and a latency budget and returns an offline runtime that hits the budget on-device with no cloud calls, handling model compression, custom kernel optimization (CUDA, Metal, ARM NEON), and the data-to-serving pipeline. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment searched the public web and found a marketing landing page but no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or public API surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested. This profile captures the company identity plus the security posture of its public web surface, and remains an identity-only lead pending a discoverable API.

providers.name: General Radar
providers.description: General Radar Corp. (GenRad) is a Belmont, California hardtech company founded in 2016 that designs and manufactures fully solid-state, high-resolution active electronically scanned array (AESA) phased-array radar systems built largely on commercial off-the-shelf hardware. Its products include the C-band GenRad GFC multi-mission AESA radar with a GaN front-end and digital beam-forming, and the Mark-IV 76-81GHz millimeter-wave 3D imaging radar producing LIDAR-like point clouds. The company serves aerospace and defense (U.S. Air Force, Navy, NORAD), counter-drone, airfield foreign-object-debris (FOD) detection, autonomy, wind energy, and weather markets, and has raised over $35M from investors including Kleiner Perkins and Octave Ventures. General Radar publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network completeness.

providers.name: Generalastro
providers.description: General Astronautics (Generalastro) is a Y Combinator (W26) space-robotics company founded in 2025 by Bram Schork, based in San Francisco, building autonomous dexterous robotic arms that perform laboratory research and manufacturing tasks in microgravity without astronaut intervention. Its systems handle work like pipetting, sample prep, plate handling, and reagent mixing, targeting microgravity production of pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, and fiber optics where crew time on orbital stations is the bottleneck (NASA estimates ISS crew time at ~$130K/hour). The company is pre-product hardware, backed by Y Combinator and Planet Ventures (~$7.1M raised), and currently exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or other machine-readable surface; this profile captures company identity only.

providers.name: Ghost Robotics
providers.description: Ghost Robotics designs and manufactures quadrupedal unmanned ground vehicles (Q-UGV), with its flagship Vision 60 platform deployed across defense, public safety, law enforcement, industrial, construction, and education customers. The platform supports modular payloads for sensing, comms, and manipulation. Ghost Robotics provides a developer SDK only to vetted partners and integrators and does not operate a public developer portal, open API, or public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Greypoint Industries
providers.description: Greypoint Industries is a Canadian defense-technology company (Y Combinator S26) building passive RF mapping software that charts the electromagnetic spectrum so operators can see every signal, track every threat, and act first — "built in Canada for those who protect." Founded in 2026 by Nic Chu, Jordan Khoo, Steven Xu, and Darcy Zhang, the company also develops mass-produced autonomous counter-drone interceptors designed to defeat drone-swarm saturation at a fraction of the cost of the targets. As an early-stage hardware and software startup, Greypoint currently publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification; this profile captures the company's identity for the API Evangelist network and awaits a developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Hlabs
providers.description: Hlabs (Harrison Laboratories, Inc., operating as hlaboratories.com) is a US-based, Y Combinator-backed (Winter 2026) manufacturer of plug-and-play robotics components. The company produces a domestically-manufactured, integrated hardware ecosystem for robot builders — including the RB1 main board (powered by Nvidia Jetson), wireless communication modules, field-oriented control (FOC) boards, pancake motors, and actuators. Its stated goal is to eliminate the complexity of sourcing mismatched components from overseas and integrating them, so roboticists can focus on design rather than electronics debugging. Hlabs targets teams building medium-to-large robots such as quadrupeds, humanoids, and robot arms, and serves customers across household robotics, defense, and other robotic platforms. This is a hardware manufacturer with no public developer/API surface at the time of profiling.

providers.name: Impossible Aerospace
providers.description: Impossible Aerospace is a deep-tech aerospace hardware company founded in 2016 by Spencer Gore in Santa Clara, California. It builds the US-1, a long-range all-electric quadcopter whose lithium-ion cells form part of the airframe structure, giving it up to roughly two hours of flight time for aerial imaging, surveillance, and public-safety missions with law enforcement and first responders. The US-1 runs the third-party Auterion OS flight stack (built on the PX4 open autopilot). The company was later acquired and operates as a small team. Enrichment note (2026-07-19): the company publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface, and its primary domain impossible.aero no longer resolves in DNS.

providers.name: Inloop Robotics
providers.description: Inloop Robotics (InLoop) is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup in San Francisco offering robotics-as-a-service for warehouses, fulfillment centers, and light manufacturing. Its bimanual "Loop V1" robot performs box assembly, kitting, visual inspection, content preparation, unpackaging, and order pick-and-pack. The system runs a hybrid-autonomy, human-in-the-loop model: onboard AI handles routine work while remote teleoperators take over on edge cases, and production failures feed continuous learning. InLoop sells this as a flat monthly subscription that bundles the hardware, ongoing AI updates, and 24/7 teleassistance fallback, rather than selling robots outright. As of this profile the company publishes a marketing site only, with no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this record tracks it as an API Evangelist network lead pending any future developer/API program.

providers.name: Intelligence Factory
providers.description: Intelligence Factory is a San Francisco robotics and embodied-AI startup (Y Combinator Spring 2026) building general-purpose foundation models for robotic manipulation. Its stated mission is "Human Intelligence for Robots" — deploying bots with human-level dexterity and reasoning in the real world. The team trains models on human demonstration data captured through custom gloves that record what a person sees, does, and feels, retargets that human motion onto robot motion, and deploys the resulting models across robot platforms from dexterous hands to grippers, with early focus on warehouses, grocery stores, and data centers. The company was founded by Yash Sinha (CEO) and Jalaj Shukla (CTO), with a team drawn from ETH Zurich, University of Pennsylvania, Harvard, NVIDIA, Formula 1, and Ansys. As of this profile it publishes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or GitHub organization — it is an early-stage lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: IQI Inc (Beijing AIQI Technology)
providers.description: IQI Inc, operating as Beijing AIQI Technology Co., Ltd. (北京爱其科技有限公司), is a mobile-internet company founded in April 2013 that develops smart hardware and robotics products under a "Create more & More fun" philosophy. It is best known for its ONEBOT building-block robots and construction sets — including the Mi Tu (米兔) block robots in the Xiaomi ecosystem and heritage-architecture sets such as the Millennium Mortise-and-Tenon (千年榫), Qinian Hall (祈年殿) and Forbidden City Corner Tower kits. The company sells through its own store, Tmall (ONEBOT flagship) and JD.com. It is a consumer smart-hardware/toy brand; as of this profile it publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK or documentation surface.

providers.name: Iridium
providers.description: Iridium Communications Inc. (NASDAQ: IRDM) is a McLean, Virginia satellite communications company operating a constellation of 66 cross-linked Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites that deliver truly global L-band voice, data, IoT, and positioning/navigation/timing (PNT) services across every region of the Earth, including the polar oceans. Iridium sells satellite phones (Iridium Extreme), satellite messengers, satellite IoT modules and modems (Iridium 9602/9603, Iridium Certus 9770/9810/9704, Iridium Edge, Iridium Edge Pro, Iridium Edge Solar), Short Burst Data (SBD) messaging, broadband Certus terminals, and next-generation Iridium NTN Direct 5G Non-Terrestrial Network services built on 3GPP NB-IoT for direct-to-device smartphone and IoT connectivity. Iridium CloudConnect — co-developed with Amazon Web Services — pipes satellite IoT data as JSON into customer-owned Amazon SQS queues inside their own AWS VPC over a dedicated private Iridium-AWS interconnect, making Iridium the first global cloud-native satellite IoT backhaul. The company serves aviation, maritime, government/defense, land-mobile, autonomous systems, and IoT markets through a partner ecosystem of more than 500 service providers, value-added resellers, and hardware OEMs, and in May 2026 announced a planned acquisition of Aireon, operator of the world's only space-based air traffic surveillance network. Iridium's business model is airtime/subscription revenue plus hardware module licensing and engineering services; there is no public, self-service developer API or OpenAPI — network access is mediated through Iridium-authorized service providers, the Iridium CloudConnect AWS integration, and hardware-level AT-command and SBD interfaces on Iridium modems.

providers.name: Iris Automation
providers.description: Iris Automation was a Reno, Nevada deep-tech company that built Casia, a computer-vision detect-and-avoid (DAA) system enabling beyond-visual-line-of-sight (BVLOS) drone operations. Its onboard products (Casia, Casia X) and the ground-based Casia G used industrial cameras and machine-learning to detect non-cooperative intruder aircraft and prevent near mid-air collisions, integrating with MavLink-based autopilots and UAS ground control systems. Iris Automation was acquired by uAvionix in late 2023; the irisonboard.com domain now 301-redirects to uAvionix and the company exposes no public developer API, documentation, or well-known surface of its own.

providers.name: JAKA
providers.description: JAKA (Shanghai JAKA Robotics Co., Ltd.) is a collaborative robot (cobot) manufacturer founded in 2014 and headquartered in Shanghai, China, with origins in robotics research at Shanghai University. The company designs and builds lightweight, human-collaborative industrial robot arms — including its JAKA Zu series and MiniCobo — used across manufacturing, 3C electronics, automotive, healthcare, education, and commercial service applications. JAKA robots are programmed through the company's on-device control software and a robot SDK (C++/Python) that communicates with the robot controller over TCP/IP on the local network, rather than a public cloud web API. As of this profile JAKA does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or hosted REST/MCP API surface; this repository is a company profile in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kindred Ai
providers.description: Kindred AI (Kindred Systems) was an artificial-intelligence and robotics company that applied reinforcement learning and teleoperation to autonomous piece-picking robots for warehouse and retail-fulfillment automation. Founded by D-Wave alumni and backed by DCVC among other investors, Kindred was acquired by Ocado Group in 2020 and folded into Ocado's advanced-robotics operations. It no longer operates an independent public developer surface: the kindred.ai brand domain remains under corporate (CSC) DNS with active Google Workspace mail, but serves no live homepage, developer portal, documentation, or public API. This profile is retained as an enrichment lead surfaced from the DCVC portfolio; no OpenAPI, SDK, or hosted API artifacts could be verified.

providers.name: Libra Robotics
providers.description: Libra Robotics is a Silicon Valley robotics startup building autonomous robots that install solar panels in the field, targeting projects from 1 MW upward across utility-scale, commercial and industrial, community solar, and agrivoltaic applications. The company's field system — marketed as Libra 001 — combines purpose-built end-effectors, suction-based panel handling and transport, vision and positioning systems that align each module with the tracker structure, and fastener workflows compatible with multiple commercial racking systems, operating across day and night shifts. Libra Robotics was founded by Yaojing Huang and Jermaine Zhao, is part of the Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, and operates out of Newark, California. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its web presence is a six-page marketing site covering solutions, technology, safety, company, and contact.

providers.name: Lumina
providers.description: Lumina (Lumina Innovations) is a San Francisco-based startup building all-electric, autonomous heavy construction equipment. Founded by Ahmed Shubber and Federico Di Palma, the company develops both the hardware and the self-driving software in-house, taking a Tesla/Waymo-style approach to the excavation and earth-moving industry. Its flagship Moonlander ML6 is a 32-ton fully autonomous electric bulldozer with roughly 750 horsepower of peak output and a 414 kWh battery pack. The broader product lineup spans Roadrunner, Moonlander, Bladerunner, and a Powerpack energy system. Lumina does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Maquoketa Research
providers.description: Maquoketa Research is a defense-technology startup (Y Combinator, Spring 2026) building autonomous terminal-guidance systems for one-way attack drones. Its platform-agnostic guidance modules add custom computer-vision object tracking to low-cost FPV drone hardware, raising strike success rates from under 25% to roughly 80% while maintaining target lock through GPS jamming and signal loss. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, the five-person team ships hardware modules (product lines include GCS, Magpie, Odin, and TGS) that integrate with existing drone flight controllers rather than a public developer API. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and enriched from the company's public website; it currently exposes no public API, SDK, or developer platform surface.

providers.name: Microagi
providers.description: Microagi (stylized microagi) is a data research lab building end-to-end physical, embodied AGI, with a stated focus on reliable real-world deployments; its public positioning is "Accelerating embodied AGI." Backed by Northzone, the company is early-stage: as of this profile its public presence is a single marketing site at microagi.ai with no published developer API, documentation, SDKs, CLI, or agent surface. This API Evangelist profile tracks Microagi as a portfolio lead; artifacts here are limited to a live domain-security probe of the marketing host until a developer surface is published. (Note: the unrelated github.com/microagi org, "µAGI / microagi.dev" by Vitakka Consulting, is a separate entity and is deliberately not attributed here.)

providers.name: Mind Robotics
providers.description: Mind Robotics is an industrial robotics company building intelligent robotic systems for real-world industrial deployment. The company focuses on clearly defined, high-impact environments — narrowing scope to the settings with the greatest operational need as a path toward broadly capable robots. Mind Robotics is a Kleiner Perkins portfolio company in the hardtech sector. As of this profile the company operates a single-page marketing website and an Ashby-hosted careers page and publishes no public API, developer documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: nasn-auto
providers.description: NASN Automotive Electronics Co., Ltd. is a Shanghai-based automotive chassis electronic-control manufacturer founded in 2016, developing brake-by-wire and steer-by-wire systems for smart and assisted driving. Its products include the NBooster intelligent braking system, brushless electric power steering (EPS) controllers, and motion-control solutions for autonomous vehicles. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners, Matrix Partners China, Hillhouse and CATL, NASN has raised roughly $231M and is a Tier-1 supplier pursuing a Hong Kong listing. Surfaced as a Qiming portfolio company; NASN is an automotive hardware manufacturer with no public developer API surface at nasn-auto.com.

providers.name: Octapulse
providers.description: Octapulse (OctaPulse) is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) startup applying computer vision and robotics to automate quality inspection in finfish farms. Its AI vision platform integrates into existing aquaculture workflows starting at the hatchery stage, using off-the-shelf cameras to perform broodstock phenotyping and juvenile deformity detection. The system reduces per-fish inspection time from roughly five minutes to under thirty seconds while achieving over 90% accuracy, standardizing QA processes and building proprietary multi-species datasets for the aquaculture industry. At this stage Octapulse is an early hardware-and-vision product company with no public API, developer portal, or programmatic surface; this profile tracks it as a lead in the API Evangelist network for future enrichment should a developer platform emerge.

providers.name: Origami Robotics
providers.description: Origami Robotics is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) hardware startup based in Millbrae, California building advanced robotic hands designed specifically for machine learning and general-purpose robotic manipulation. The company designs a high-degrees-of-freedom hand with in-joint motors, co-designed with a matching data-collection glove that eliminates the embodiment gap between human and robot manipulation so that real-world training data transfers directly to deployed robots. Its focus areas include force transparency, avoiding the sim-to-real problems of high-ratio gearboxes, and scaling real-world manipulation data by deploying devices "in the wild." Origami Robotics targets industrial automation in manufacturing and logistics and has sold hands to Physical AI research labs including Amazon. Origami Robotics is a hardware and robotics company; as of this profile it publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable interface.

providers.name: Ornadyne
providers.description: Ornadyne is a Los Angeles hard-tech startup building autonomous flapping-wing UAVs (ornithopters) that look and fly like real birds for covert reconnaissance and surveillance. Its near-silent, AI-powered, man-portable drones are engineered for low acoustic and visual signatures, hour-class flight times, and natural bird-like flight, contrasting with easily detected quadcopters and fixed-wing aircraft. Founded by Geourg Kivijian (CEO, ex-NASA JPL and Astrolab) and Armen Arakelyan (CTO, ex-SpaceX Starship), the company is a Y Combinator Spring 2026 company operating in the hardware, robotics, drones, aerospace, and defense space. It is a hardware/defense company with a marketing website and no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Outrider
providers.description: Outrider is an autonomous yard technology company that automates distribution yard operations with self-driving, all-electric yard trucks (hostlers). The Outrider System combines autonomous driving software, robotics for connecting and disconnecting trailers, and site operations software to move trailers between docks, parking spots, and staging lanes in large logistics yards. Headquartered in Golden, Colorado, Outrider targets shippers and logistics operators seeking to improve safety, sustainability, and throughput in the supply chain. The company is backed by investors including 8VC. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal has been identified for Outrider.

providers.name: Performance Drone Works
providers.description: Performance Drone Works is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of lux-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: defense. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Phantom Auto
providers.description: Phantom Auto was a Mountain View, California and Ra'anana, Israel teleoperation company founded in 2017 by Shai Magzimof (CEO) and Elliot Katz (CBO) that built a remote-driving and remote-operation platform letting a human operator monitor and drive a vehicle from thousands of miles away over bonded commercial cellular links. It launched aimed at robotaxis and self-driving trucks as a safety fallback for autonomous vehicles, then pivoted in 2019 to logistics — remotely operated forklifts and yard trucks that have no autonomy of their own, plus autonomous sidewalk delivery robots — and signed customers including Maersk, CJ Logistics, ArcBest and Serve Robotics. It raised roughly $95M in total from Bessemer Venture Partners, Maniv Mobility, InfraBridge and strategic investors ArcBest and ConGlobal, closing a $25M round in 2023, and acquired Swedish low-latency video streaming company Voysys AB in October 2022. Phantom Auto ceased operations on 12 March 2024 after a funding round fell through, laying off its roughly 100-120 remaining employees. The company published no developer portal, public API reference, SDK, or machine-readable specification (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, MCP manifest or agent card) while it operated, and its primary host phantom.auto no longer resolves in DNS at all. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Piestro
providers.description: Piestro was a Los Angeles-area food-robotics company that built a fully enclosed, automated pizza-making vending machine — an unattended kiosk that pressed, sauced, topped, baked, cut and boxed an artisanal pizza in roughly three minutes, sold both as direct-to-consumer placements and as a white-label unit for existing pizza brands. Founded by Massimo Noja De Marco and incubated by Wavemaker Labs (since rebranded Vebu Labs), it raised roughly $11.7M from equity-crowdfunding investors, largely via StartEngine, and piloted units with partners including Capriotti's and 800 Degrees Go. Piestro shut down in January 2025 without shipping a production unit. It is a hardware and food-service company, not a software vendor: it never ran a developer program, and no public API, SDK, webhook, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind was ever published. This profile records that absence rather than inventing a surface.

providers.name: QikPod
providers.description: QikPod was an Accel-backed Indian startup that built an automated parcel locker network for last-mile e-commerce delivery, letting shoppers collect and return packages from unattended smart lockers placed in apartments, offices, and retail locations. The company has since rebranded and pivoted to Leapmile Robotics, a nano-warehouse automation and intelligent fulfillment platform that uses robotics to handle storage, retrieval, picking, auditing, and dispatch inside compact autonomous warehouse facilities. The legacy qikpod.com domain now redirects to leapmile.com/qikpod. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company lead; no public developer API surface has been found for either the QikPod or Leapmile properties.

providers.name: Raphe Mphibr
providers.description: Raphe mPhibr is an Indian deep-tech aerospace company revolutionizing unmanned aviation through in-house carbon fiber composites, UAV airframes, propulsion, and end-to-end manufacturing. The company designs and builds heavy-lift and tactical unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs/drones) for defense and industrial applications, emphasizing research-driven innovation and vertically integrated production. Raphe mPhibr is a B2B / defense-oriented manufacturer surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer portal, API, SDK, or documentation surface — its digital presence is a corporate marketing site only.

providers.name: Ready Robotics
providers.description: READY Robotics was a Columbus, Ohio industrial-automation software company, founded in 2016 out of Johns Hopkins University, that built Forge/OS — a universal operating system for industrial robots. Forge/OS presented one low-code programming and control surface across hundreds of robot models from ABB, Epson, FANUC, Kawasaki, Stäubli, Universal Robots and Yaskawa, and its Forge Edge product advertised a REST API with an OpenAPI/Swagger description plus client tooling for Python, JavaScript and C++, alongside the RAL2 (Robot Abstraction Layer 2) C++/Qt plugin interface used to write new robot drivers. The company ceased operations in August 2024 after a funding round collapsed, and its assets were liquidated through an assignment for the benefit of creditors. Every developer-facing host it operated — developer., docs., portal., market. and support.ready-robotics.com — no longer resolves in DNS, so no live machine-readable contract remains. What survives publicly is the marketing site behind a Cloudflare challenge and the GitHub organization, which still carries the RAL2 sample driver and the vendored C++ dependencies Forge/OS was built on.

providers.name: Rise Robotics
providers.description: RISE Robotics develops industrial linear-actuation technology designed to replace traditional hydraulic systems. Its flagship Beltdraulic Cylinder is a fluid-free hydraulic alternative delivering faster actuation, higher reliability, no fire hazard, and fuel-source flexibility for large-scale industrial applications. The company builds actuation products (Beltdraulic Cylinder, Railgate, SuperJammer, CLD) for Tier 1 suppliers, OEMs, and the US Department of Defense. RISE Robotics is a hardware and heavy-equipment company backed by Techstars; it publishes no developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this API Evangelist profile captures identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Sabanto
providers.description: Sabanto is an agricultural autonomy company known for retrofitting existing farm tractors and equipment with an autonomy kit and an autonomy-as-a-service model, enabling unmanned tillage, planting, and field operations. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of the enrichment pass on 2026-07-21 the company's primary domain (sabanto.com) no longer resolves to a live site — it redirects to a GoDaddy parked/for-sale page — so no developer portal, API, documentation, SDK, GitHub organization, or other public API surface could be found. This profile is retained as a lead with no live API surface at this time.

providers.name: Savioke
providers.description: Savioke is a robotics company, backed by GV, that built the Relay autonomous delivery robot used by hotels and hospitals to move items such as amenities, medications, lab samples, and supplies through facilities without human assistance. The company now operates as Relay Robotics (savioke.com redirects to relayrobotics.com). It publishes no public API, SDK, or developer surface; enrichment found only a marketing/contact site.

providers.name: SE3 Labs
providers.description: SE3 Labs is a European artificial intelligence company building spatial AI for autonomous systems, with a mission to enable machines to perceive, reason, and act autonomously in the physical world. Its technology performs real-time 3D reconstruction of operational environments, spatial understanding to orchestrate fleets of autonomous machines, and natural-language interfaces for commanding multiple machines at once. Early applications target the defence sector, including vision-based autonomy and multi-drone reconnaissance. SE3 Labs is backed by Seedcamp and works directly with government and military partners; it does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Seasats
providers.description: Seasats designs and manufactures autonomous uncrewed surface vehicles (USVs) for ocean intelligence, maritime domain awareness, and defense missions. Its platform lines include the hand-deployable Lightfish (6-month endurance), the fast-response Quickfish (35+ knots with an integrated drone bay), and the heavy-payload Heavyfish. Vessels carry modular payloads, run persistent autonomous surveys, and integrate with existing command-and-control (C2) architectures. Seasats is a Techstars-backed company. As of this enrichment pass Seasats publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable discovery surface; its integration story is C2 interoperability, not a web API.

providers.name: Servo7
providers.description: Servo7 is a Y Combinator-backed warehouse robotics company that builds AI-powered robots for automating physical material-handling tasks such as loose-loaded container unloading, mixed-pallet palletizing, depalletizing, sortation, and case handling (up to a 20kg payload). Its differentiator is a no-code, demonstration-based deployment model in which an operator shows the robot the task to automate, with no engineers or integration project and no facility redesign required. Servo7 works with logistics providers including CEVA, Stord, DHL, and PostNL. It is a physical-robotics/hardware company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Stratim
providers.description: Stratim (originally incorporated as Zirx in 2014, rebranded to Stratim in 2017) was a San Francisco-based SaaS company that built an enterprise fleet-operations and logistics platform for transportation companies, autonomous-vehicle operators, and urban fleets. Its three product lines were the Stratim Platform (fleet operations software), the Stratim Exchange (on-the-ground vendor fulfillment), and the Stratim Marketplace (fleet-owner/vendor transactions), and it advertised API access, a workforce app, processing-engine integration, and SMS updates. Founded by Shmulik Fishman and Sean Behr and backed by Norwest Venture Partners and Trinity Ventures ($36.4M raised), Stratim was acquired by ACV Auctions in 2021. As of this enrichment pass the stratim.com domain is held in custodial parking (CSC Corporate Domains) with no live website, developer portal, documentation, or reachable API surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested.

providers.name: supermag
providers.description: Suzhou Supermag Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. is a Chinese deep-tech manufacturer specializing in magnetic levitation (maglev) motion and fluid-handling systems. Its product lines include SCM maglev wafer turntables for ultra-clean semiconductor rotation, SCP maglev pumps for contamination-free fluid transport, MSS maglev stirring systems for low-shear mixing, and SCT maglev turbomolecular pumps for high-vacuum applications, serving the semiconductor, biopharmaceutical, chemical, and energy industries. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners, the company markets physical industrial hardware and publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Symbio Robotics
providers.description: Symbio Robotics is an AI industrial-automation company founded in 2014 and based in Emeryville, California. Its flagship product, SymbioDCS, is a robot-agnostic middleware and Python programming framework that lets automation teams build, deploy, and continuously improve AI-driven assembly applications on existing factory robots. Symbio has publicly worked with automakers including Ford, Nissan, and Toyota to speed transmission and vehicle assembly. SymbioDCS is deployed on-premises inside manufacturing lines rather than offered as a public web API; as of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer portal, documentation, SDK/package registry presence, MCP server, or API surface, and its former web domains (symb.io, symbiorobotics.com) now resolve to parked/for-sale landing pages.

providers.name: Target Arm
providers.description: Target Arm is a robotics company building systems to autonomously launch and recover drones from moving vehicles without stopping. Its Ralar robotic arm captures drones mid-air, recharges them, and relaunches them, while TRACKR sensor-fusion, TurboFly autopilot, and Maestro mission-control software coordinate drone fleets across commercial delivery, first-responder, agriculture, energy-inspection, and defense/ISR use cases. A Techstars-backed hardware startup with no public API or developer program at this time; this network profile captures identity and infrastructure signals only.

providers.name: Tenet Industries
providers.description: Tenet Industries is a Swedish defense-technology startup founded in 2026 by Hugo Frisk, Fabian Andersson, and Emil Falk (students from KTH Royal Institute of Technology and the Stockholm School of Economics) building low-cost, mass-producible defense systems. Applying design-for-manufacturing and first-principles engineering, the company starts with strike/attack drones — a kamikaze quadcopter that assembles in two minutes with roughly half the parts of comparable systems — and extends the same hardware/software platform to loitering munitions, jammers, radars, and missile systems. Backed by Y Combinator ($500K). As a defense hardware manufacturer, Tenet Industries currently publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface; this profile is maintained as a company record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Terra Industries
providers.description: Terra Industries is a Nigeria-based defense-technology company, positioning itself as Africa's first defense prime, that designs, manufactures, and deploys autonomous multi-domain security systems across air, land, and eventually sea. Founded in 2024 by Nathan Nwachuku and Maxwell Maduka, the company builds ArtemisOS (an AI-powered operating system for infrastructure security), the Archer long-range VTOL surveillance drone, the Iroko modular UAV, the Duma autonomous unmanned ground vehicle, and the Kallon solar-powered AI sentry tower to monitor, detect, and respond to threats such as terrorism, sabotage, and armed attacks on critical infrastructure including hydropower plants, mines, and power assets. Terra raised $11.75M led by 8VC in January 2026. As a hardware and defense-systems manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface; this profile is maintained as a company/provider record in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: TopXGun
providers.description: TopXGun (Nanjing TopXGun Robotics / 拓攻机器人) is a Chinese unmanned aerial vehicle manufacturer specializing in the research, development, and production of agricultural spray drones, heavy-lift delivery drones, industrial and cleaning drones, firefighting and emergency UAVs, tethered drones, eVTOL and large unmanned aircraft, and the professional flight-control and avionics hardware, payload equipment, and software systems that power them. Its whole-aircraft capability spans all airspace below 5,000 meters and payloads up to 1.5 tons across core industries, and it offers ODM/OEM customization and education support. Its overseas agricultural line is marketed as TopXGun Agriculture (topxgunag.com) with CE, FCC, RoHS, and KC certifications. Surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures. No public web API, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment; this is a hardware manufacturer.

providers.name: Vicarious
providers.description: Vicarious (Vicarious FPC) was an artificial intelligence and industrial robotics company founded in 2010 by D. Scott Phoenix and Dileep George. It pursued brain-inspired machine learning, notably the Recursive Cortical Network that solved text CAPTCHAs with far less training data, then applied that research to general-purpose robotic automation for warehouse and manufacturing tasks. The company was backed by DCVC, Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, ABB, Samsung, and Wipro, and was acquired by Intrinsic, Alphabet's robotics moonshot, in 2022. Its vicarious.com domain no longer resolves and it exposes no public API surface.

providers.name: Vimaan
providers.description: Vimaan is an autonomous inventory intelligence company that combines computer vision, machine learning, and autonomous drones and robotics to verify, count, and audit inventory across warehouses, distribution centers, and supply-chain operations. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of wing-venture-capital and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Vimaan publishes no public developer, API, SDK, or documentation surface: the corporate website (vimaan.ai) sits entirely behind an sgcaptcha challenge wall and no developer, docs, or api subdomains resolve. This profile therefore captures verified company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Vision Space Inc.
providers.description: Vision Space Inc. (VisionSpace) is a South Korean company building Physical AI robot simulation software for automation in the logistics and manufacturing sectors. Its TESSERACT product implements logistics and manufacturing sites as digital twins, visualizing process data and predicting operational efficiency through AI-based simulation, while its TARS product delivers real-time 3D monitoring that integrates and manages data from equipment and robots in a unified 3D control dashboard. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass VisionSpace publishes a marketing website only and exposes no public developer API, documentation, developer portal, or GitHub organization.

providers.name: Wayve
providers.description: Wayve is a London-based embodied AI company pioneering AV2.0, an end-to-end, mapless, vehicle-agnostic approach to autonomous driving built on large-scale self-supervised learning rather than hand-engineered HD maps and rule stacks. Wayve's core technology stack includes the Wayve AI Driver (the production driving stack licensed to automakers), GAIA generative world models that synthesize realistic driving video from text and serve as simulators for policy training, and LINGO, a vision-language-action research line that uses natural language to train and explain driving decisions. Backed by SoftBank, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and Uber with a 1.5 billion USD funding round, Wayve is partnering with Nissan, Mercedes-Benz, and Stellantis on production programmes, and with Uber and Nissan on a Tokyo robotaxi launch. Wayve does not publish a public developer API; its public surface is research, press, and product positioning material.

providers.name: Akara
providers.description: Akara is a healthcare automation company building AI-powered systems for the operating room and clinical environments. Its platform combines the Akara AI Sensor, a thermal-only computer-vision system that passively tracks surgical and procedure events without capturing identifiable patient data (named to TIME's Best Inventions list); the Akara AI Platform, which delivers real-time OR monitoring, automated alerts, interactive dashboards, analytics, and Clara, an AI chat assistant for exploring surgical data and optimizing scheduling; and the Akara UV Robot (Violet), a fully autonomous UV-C disinfection robot that generates 3D UV dose maps and disinfects occupied clinical spaces up to six times faster than manual cleaning. Akara is trusted by hospitals across Europe and the US. The company does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile tracks its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: finern
providers.description: Finern (Finern Automation) is a China-based industrial automation company that designs and builds fully automated production lines and intelligent measurement systems for manufacturing. It serves five sectors — automotive, electronics, new energy (battery/EV), healthcare/pharmaceutical equipment, and consumer goods — with automated assembly, testing, and inspection systems. The company reports 600+ personnel, 30,000+ square meters of facilities, 100+ global clients, 8 international sites, and 4 R&D centers. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Finern publishes a corporate marketing website but does not currently expose any public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable discovery surface (no /.well-known/*, llms.txt, or OpenAPI found on probe).

providers.name: Advanced Farm Technologies
providers.description: Advanced Farm Technologies (brand: advanced.farm) was an agricultural robotics company founded in 2017 in Davis, California, building autonomous robotic harvesters for specialty crops. Its T-6 robotic strawberry harvester and six-armed robotic apple harvester used custom rugged stereo cameras and machine-learning ripeness models to identify and pick fruit alongside human crews, and the company sold harvesting as a service rather than selling the machines. It raised roughly $34M from investors including CNH Industrial, Yamaha Motor Ventures and Catapult Ventures. On 2025-04-02 CNH Industrial acquired the company's intellectual property and assets and the majority of its technical team joined CNH; the company no longer operates independently. Its domain, advanced.farm, now returns a blanket HTTP 301 to CNH's New Holland Agriculture site. Advanced Farm never published a public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: AIForce Technology
providers.description: AIForce Technology (Beijing Zhongke Yuandongli Technology Co., Ltd. / 北京中科原动力科技有限公司) is a Beijing agricultural-robotics manufacturer incubated out of the Chinese Academy of Sciences Institute of Microelectronics, registered in 2018 and operating since July 2019, with Chinese Academy of Engineering academician Li Deyi as chief scientist. It builds autonomous and battery-electric farm machinery across four product lines: the Wantu (万途) electric intelligent tractors, the Zhiniu (智牛) unmanned agricultural machines, the Zhinong (智农) multi-function field robots, and the Zhiyun (智耘) unmanned-operation system that adds full-day autonomous tillage, planting, crop management and harvest to existing machinery in dry fields, paddies and greenhouses, paired with a mobile app and telemetry cloud for route setting and operation monitoring. It is a hardware company that sells machines and retrofit systems to farms, cooperatives and agricultural enterprises, backed by Vertex Ventures China, Chery and CCV among others, and named champion of PepsiCo's Greenhouse Accelerator APAC edition for an AI-powered low-carbon automatic tractor. aiforcetech.com is a five-section Chinese marketing site with no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Doxel
providers.description: Doxel is a Menlo Park, California construction technology company providing AI-powered observability and progress tracking for large capital projects. Founded in 2015 by CEO Saurabh Ladha, the company combines 360-degree reality capture (via Insta360 X5 hardware partnership) with computer vision models that compare site video against BIM models to automatically quantify work-in-place by trade, system, and stage. The platform layers a "rules of credit" engine on top of those quantities to drive earned-value, schedule, and budget analytics — including 3D Progress View, Production Rates, Schedule (a visual Gantt replacement), Utilities Underground Tracking from drone imagery, and Portfolio-level dashboards. Doxel uses advanced language models to map schedule line items to physical progress and supports Procore-style construction management workflows, with deployments across data centers, healthcare, semiconductor fabs, and EV battery factories. Doxel has raised approximately $57M from Insight Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, and others, and counts 18 of the top 30 U.S. general contractors, 14 of the top 20 data center developers, and 3 of 4 hyperscalers as customers. There is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or GitHub organization — the platform is delivered as a managed SaaS application at app.doxel.ai with hardware-assisted capture and enterprise integrations arranged via direct engagement.

providers.name: Rapid Robotics
providers.description: Rapid Robotics was a San Francisco robotics-as-a-service (RaaS) company, founded in 2019 by Jordan Kretchmer, that rented pre-trained six-axis "Rapid Machine Operators" to small and mid-size manufacturers on a subscription — roughly $25,000 per robot per year — to cover repetitive machine-tending work such as pad printing, injection molding, heat staking, heat stamping, ultrasonic welding, pick-and-place and parts inspection. The robots shipped with grippers, computer-vision software and models pre-trained on CAD, and were set up and supervised through a proprietary no-code fleet console rather than through a developer interface. The company raised about $54.2M in total — a $12M Series A in 2021 and a $36.7M Series B co-led by Kleiner Perkins and Tiger Global — and announced partnerships with Universal Robots and Yaskawa Motoman in early 2023. Rapid Robotics subsequently wound down, and its assets — hardware, marquee customers and the US team — were acquired by Munich-based RaaS company RobCo, which used them to enter the US market and announced a new San Francisco headquarters on 9 September 2025. The company never published a public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification of any kind: 1,773 unique archived URLs on rapidrobotics.com contain no /api, /apis, /docs, /developer, /graphql or /sdk path. The domain is no longer operated by the company — it is delegated to ns1/ns2.atom.com and redirects to a brand-name marketplace listing. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a historical record; there is no API surface to catalog.

providers.name: Beyond Imagination
providers.description: Beyond Imagination, Inc. is a Los Angeles based robotics and artificial intelligence company founded in January 2018 by Dr. Harry Kloor and Dr. Ray Kurzweil, building general-purpose humanoid robots and the AI software stack that runs them. Its flagship platform is Beomni, a wheeled humanoid robot with an articulated upper body and dexterous hands that can be teleoperated through VR headsets and haptic gloves or run autonomously. The software side is marketed as four products: AURA (Adaptive Unified Robotic/Human Administrator), a universal operating system for coordinating robots, humans and infrastructure across manufacturing ecosystems; ARCANA, an LLM-free synthetic brain architecture for real-time perception, decision making and coordination; Expert Minds, modular AI job modules trained for specialized roles such as chemical handling, bio-reactor operation, surgical prep and warehouse logistics; and Hive Mind Intelligence, a fleet learning layer where robots upload new skills to a shared cloud memory. The company has run pilot programs in commercial kitchens, laboratory work, healthcare and pharmaceutical manufacturing, and announced a manufacturing partnership with Korean electronics manufacturer Dreamtech. As of this profiling pass Beyond Imagination publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, SDKs or MCP/agent surface; its public web presence is a marketing site only.

providers.name: RedWing Aerospace Laboratories
providers.description: RedWing Aerospace Laboratories (RedWing Labs, operated by Kitemaps AMS Pvt Ltd) is a Bangalore, India based, Techstars-backed company that designs, develops and deploys fully autonomous drones to transform logistics supply chains. It offers a fleet of long-range, urban and medium-range delivery aircraft plus an operations software suite, and runs an autonomous four-step delivery flow (order, handoff to flight operations, proof of delivery, return to hub) used to move healthcare products, food and other goods within the hour. The company reports operational milestones including 145,930+ kilometers flown and thousands of deliveries completed. RedWing does not publish a first-party developer API; its public agent surface is the platform-provided Wix Site MCP endpoint advertised in its llms.txt.

providers.name: RoboDock
providers.description: RoboDock is an autonomous robotics company (Y Combinator W2026) building the robotics layer that powers autonomous EV and AV depots, starting with charging and inspections. Its robots automate depot operations for electric and autonomous vehicle fleets, handling vision-guided plug insertion with verified connection, automated post-trip vehicle inspection, and closed-loop learning that improves efficiency with each charge event. The company targets live EV and AV depots, ports, and logistics yards where charging and core depot operations are still performed manually multiple times per day across mixed fleets. RoboDock is a hardware and robotics business rather than an API provider; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical documentation. Founded by Zinny Weli (CEO, ex-Zipline and Amazon robotics) and Celine Wang (CTO, ex-Plus autonomous systems).

providers.name: Cosmic Robotics
providers.description: Cosmic Robotics, Inc. designs and operates autonomous construction equipment that takes on the hardest, most dangerous jobs on a construction site, coordinated as a fleet by a single software layer. Its first market is utility-scale solar energy, with expansion planned into data center construction. The flagship Cosmic-1A is a purpose-built robotic platform for solar panel installation, and Constellation is the coordination and control layer that plans, dispatches, and monitors the robot fleet across a jobsite. Founded in 2023 and based in the Dogpatch neighborhood of San Francisco, the company is backed by Y Combinator. Cosmic Robotics is currently a hardware and fleet-software company with no public developer API; this profile tracks its identity and any agent-facing surfaces (such as its published llms.txt) as the API Evangelist network enrichment pipeline monitors it for a future API.

providers.name: Kyten Technologies
providers.description: Kyten Technologies is a Seattle, Washington hardware manufacturing startup building a factory to produce custom aerospace-grade battery packs. The founders spent six years at Starlink, where they put more than 5,000 battery packs into space, and are now bringing rapid development and volume production of aerospace-grade battery packs to the wider industry. The company positions itself against a legacy supply chain that cannot keep up with the 100,000+ drones, submarines, and satellites being built in the United States. Kyten Technologies is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company, classified under Industrials / Manufacturing and Robotics, and was an early-stage two-person team at the time of profiling. As a hardware manufacturer it publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: XtalPi
providers.description: XtalPi is an AI-and-quantum-physics drug discovery and materials research platform company with headquarters in Cambridge, Massachusetts and major operations in Beijing, Shanghai, and Shenzhen, publicly listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange under stock code 2228.HK. The company combines a hybrid AI plus quantum mechanics (QM) discovery engine with large-scale robotic laboratory automation to accelerate molecular research and development for pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials customers, including engagements with Pfizer, Eli Lilly, and Novartis. XtalPi's offering spans proprietary software platforms — PatSight for patent extraction, XFEP for free-energy perturbation binding-affinity prediction, XMolGen for generative chemistry, and XtalGazer for solid-state research — and intelligent automation hardware including the XmartChem intelligent synthesis workstation and ChemPlus desktop solid dispenser. Its drug discovery services cover hit discovery, hit/lead optimization, biology capabilities, focused library synthesis, and the PepiX peptide platform, complemented by sister brands Ailux (biology) and AiFChem (chemistry). XtalPi's products are delivered as enterprise collaborations, licensed software, and CRO-style services; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release.

providers.name: Smacktechnologies
providers.description: Smack Technologies is a frontier AI lab dedicated to national security, building domain-specific multimodal models trained via deep reinforcement learning in synthetic warfare environments to deliver decision dominance to the U.S. Department of War, its allies and partners. The company ships two product suites — Omega, a command-level AI stack pairing frontier models with customer-specific applications for strategic decision-making, and Alpha, an edge-level stack of lightweight models on proprietary hardware for tactical platforms and autonomous systems. Founded by MARSOC veterans Andrew Markoff and Clint Alanis and headquartered in El Segundo, California, Smack has raised $32M across Seed and Series A rounds led by Felicis. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs — a defense-domain vendor with no external developer surface.

providers.name: Amprius Technologies
providers.description: Amprius Technologies is a Fremont, California-based developer and manufacturer of high-energy density lithium-ion batteries built on a proprietary 100% silicon anode platform. Its flagship SiCore and SiMaxx cell families are marketed as among the industry's highest gravimetric and volumetric energy density rechargeable cells, enabling longer endurance, faster charging, and higher payload capacity than conventional graphite-anode chemistries. Amprius targets aviation and aerospace (high-altitude pseudo-satellites, unmanned aerial systems, electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft), defense (US Army soldier-worn power, BAE Systems), light electric vehicles, robotics, and AI hardware. Public references include AALTO's Airbus-derived Zephyr HAPS programs, Prismatic's PHASA-35 stratospheric aircraft, Nokia Drone Networks, and Matternet drone delivery. The company runs pilot manufacturing and R&D in Fremont and is scaling a GWh-scale Brighton, Colorado plant alongside contract manufacturing partnerships in Asia. Amprius is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker AMPX. It is certified to ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100:2016. Amprius sells cells, modules, and engineering services to OEMs and defense primes; it does not publish a developer API, SDK, or open-source battery telemetry interface, and has no public GitHub organization.

providers.name: Medra
providers.description: Medra builds an AI-powered robotic platform for autonomous laboratory work in the life sciences. Its "Physical AI Scientist" combines robotic hardware, computer vision, and scientific reasoning AI to design, execute, and continuously optimize experiments — gene editing, RNA/nucleic-acid work, antibody design, and cell-based assays — the way a human scientist would. Units are deployed at partner sites including Genentech and Addition Therapeutics, with a DARPA collaboration on its AI Experimentalist reasoning layer. Founded by Michelle Lee and headquartered in San Francisco, Medra raised a $52M Series A (Dec 2025) from investors including Lux Capital and Menlo Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Medra publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Anki
providers.description: Anki, Inc. was a consumer robotics and artificial-intelligence company based in San Francisco, founded in 2010 and backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Index Ventures, and J.P. Morgan. It was known for the Cozmo and Vector companion robots and the Anki Drive / Overdrive robotic racing system, which combined computer vision, on-device AI, and mapping/navigation. Anki debuted at Apple's WWDC in 2013, shipped Cozmo in 2016 and Vector in 2018, and published first-party Python and C# SDKs so developers could program the robots over a local connection. Anki ceased operations in May 2019 and its assets were later acquired by Digital Dream Labs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; the robot SDKs remain the company's public developer surface.

providers.name: Bionaut Labs
providers.description: Bionaut Labs is a clinical-stage medical robotics company headquartered in Los Angeles, California, developing "Bionauts" — remote-controlled, magnetically steered microscale robots roughly the size of a grain of rice that travel through tissue to deliver drugs, biologics and nucleic acids directly to targets deep in the brain and central nervous system. Founded in 2016 by CEO Michael Shpigelmacher, the company is pursuing treatments for malignant glioma, Dandy-Walker syndrome, Parkinson's disease and Huntington's disease, and has raised more than $80 million from investors including Khosla Ventures. Its product is a therapeutic device and navigation platform regulated as a medical device, not software sold to developers: Bionaut Labs operates no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Bioyond Robotics
providers.description: Bioyond Robotics (奔曜科技) is a life-sciences intelligent-automation company founded in 2021 and headquartered in Shanghai's Zhangjiang Science City. It combines robotics, machine vision, and artificial intelligence to build autonomous laboratory solutions for scientific research, drug discovery, applied chemistry, synthetic biology, multiomics, and clinical diagnostics. Its product line spans the LabGenius robot platform (liquid-handling and transport robots), the LabMate automation platform (material/liquid handling, stackers, and intelligent scheduling), the LabMind laboratory software platform for integrating external instruments and modules, and the BIOYOND AutoSeq genetic-analysis system. Bioyond is backed by Qiming Venture Partners. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — this record captures its identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Cencorp
providers.description: Cencorp (Zhuhai) Industrial Technology Co., Ltd. is a process-automation equipment manufacturer that designs and builds high-end laser processing, dispensing, automated optical inspection (AOI), and system-integration & automation systems for the consumer electronics, automotive electronics, semiconductor, and new-energy industries. Formed in 2020 and combining the acquired Finland-based Cencorp automation business with operations headquartered in Zhuhai, China, the company runs 12 offices worldwide with 400+ R&D engineers and 300+ patents, and is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — this is a physical automation-equipment business.

providers.name: Collaborative Robotics
providers.description: Collaborative Robotics (Cobot) is a Physical AI company founded by Brad Porter building AI-powered collaborative robots that work safely alongside people. Its flagship robot, Proxie, is a human-capable mobile manipulator designed to address labor shortages across warehousing, manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare. The company uses ScoutMap to analyze facility operations and identify automation opportunities, then deploys robots that learn real-world workflow patterns. Backed by General Catalyst, Collaborative Robotics is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it is a hardware / Physical AI provider with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: DeepWay 深向
providers.description: DeepWay (深向科技 / Shenxiang Technology) is a Chinese intelligent new-energy heavy-truck company, backed by Baidu and Qiming Venture Partners, that designs and manufactures electric autonomous freight trucks it calls RoboTrucks. Its vehicle line includes the Xingchen II (深向星辰 II) and Xingtu (深向星途) electric heavy trucks paired with the Tianji (天玑) driver-assistance and autonomous driving stack, an AI-based fleet management platform, and a vehicle-owner mobile app. DeepWay reports 7,500+ activated L2 vehicles, a 30%+ subscription rate, and 300M+ km of assisted-driving operation, and follows a roadmap from L2 assistance (2023) to L4 platooning (2025) to single-vehicle L4 autonomy (2028). Its business model progresses from vehicle sales to subscription services to large-scale autonomous logistics capacity. As of this enrichment pass DeepWay publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable specification — this profile captures company identity and a domain-security probe only.

providers.name: Fleetzero
providers.description: Fleetzero is a Houston-based maritime technology company, founded in 2021 and led by U.S. Navy veterans and shipping-industry experts, building battery-electric energy and robotics systems to decarbonize ocean shipping at cost parity with fossil fuels. Its Leviathan modular marine energy storage system, 3.8 MWh marine battery containers, and 55 MWh battery barges provide propulsion power and mobile charging infrastructure for cargo vessels. Backed by Obvious Ventures, Fleetzero was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it currently publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface, so this profile carries company identity and infrastructure signals only.

providers.name: Remedy Robotics
providers.description: Remedy Robotics is a medical robotics company developing what it describes as the world's first endovascular robot capable of performing entire cardiovascular and stroke procedures under onsite, remote, or autonomous control. Its stated mission is to expand timely access to life-saving vascular interventions for patients who cannot reach specialized stroke and cardiac care in time. Remedy Robotics is a portfolio company of DCVC. As a clinical-stage medical device developer, the company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Physical Intelligence
providers.description: Physical Intelligence (often styled "Pi" or "π") is a San Francisco-based research company building general-purpose foundation models for robotics with the stated goal of producing learning algorithms that can control any robot to do any task. The company has published a continuing line of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models: π0 (October 2024, first generalist multi-task multi-robot policy), π0-FAST (autoregressive variant via Real-time Action Chunking / FAST tokenization), π0.5 (April 2025, open-world generalization), π*0.6 (November 2025, reinforcement-learning from experience), and π0.7 (April 2026, steerable model with emergent capabilities). Physical Intelligence releases significant work as open source: the openpi repository (~12K stars) is the canonical home for π0 weights and code, with companion repos including real-time-chunking-kinetix, pi-data-sharing, aloha, augmax, and rlds_dataset_builder. The company does not yet offer a hosted commercial API; access to the platform is via open-weight models and research collaborations.

providers.name: Futurtec
providers.description: Futurtec (鑫君特) is a Chinese medical-device company founded in 2015 and recognized as a national high-tech enterprise, focused on orthopedic surgical robotics. Its flagship ORTHBOT surgical system combines navigation with automatic robotic execution — intelligent needle placement, non-invasive positioning, dual-camera navigation, and visual force-feedback pressure protection — and holds Chinese regulatory approval (Feb 2021) and EU MDR CE certification (May 2023). The company reports 251+ patents filed or granted, including 84+ invention patents and 25+ PCT applications. As of this enrichment pass, Futurtec publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or software surface: it is a clinical hardware manufacturer, so the enrichment pipeline found no API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Optimotive
providers.description: Optimotive is an autonomous-robotics company building a vertically integrated fleet of advanced robots for the toughest, most extreme environments across construction, mining, and oil and gas. Its robots take on the mundane, repetitive, and hazardous tasks that burden human workers, doing it cost-effectively.
