Two products are already deployed with major market players: IRIS, a wheeled autonomous robot that captures large-scale site data, and BOX, which provides a reliable home base and on-site infrastructure for entirely self-sufficient robots. Two more robots are joining the fleet: MULE for onsite material handling and SCRUBBLES for site cleanup. The company is vertically integrated from developing its own AI to 3D printing its robots, owning the full hardware and software stack. Founded by CEO Scott Fairley and based in Windsor, Ontario, Canada, Optimotive raised a 2M USD seed round led by Version One Ventures in September 2024, with participation from Garage and NewLab. As a physical robotics hardware business, Optimotive publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: Pitch Aeronautics
providers.description: Pitch Aeronautics provides AI-powered weather intelligence and drone-deployable line solutions for electric utilities, helping them boost grid capacity, increase reliability, and reduce wildfire risk. The company pairs aerial hardware that installs and inspects power-line equipment with software that turns real-time atmospheric and grid data into dynamic line-rating and operational intelligence. Pitch Aeronautics is a Techstars-backed company; this API Evangelist profile was enriched from the company's public website. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal was found during enrichment (July 2026).

providers.name: Medrobotics
providers.description: Medrobotics Corporation was a Raynham, Massachusetts surgical robotics manufacturer, founded as CardioRobotics, that built the Flex Robotic System — an articulating, steerable robotic endoscope platform cleared by the FDA in 2015 and CE-marked for minimally invasive procedures in otolaryngology, colorectal surgery and gastroenterology, and deployed at roughly thirty hospitals worldwide. The company was a medical device manufacturer, not a software vendor: its product was an operating-room capital robot and its single-use accessories, and it never operated a developer program, a public API, an SDK or a developer portal. Medrobotics filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Massachusetts on 2022-01-24 (case 1:22-bk-10077), following judgments in the Endobotics litigation, and in June 2024 the Chapter 7 trustee liquidated the entire 40,000-square-foot Raynham plant at auction — 23 complete Flex and Flex360 systems plus roughly 22 terabytes of technical specifications, customer lists and other intellectual property. The company is defunct. Its domain, medrobotics.com, is now a parked page served by a domain-parking network and its registry nameservers are NS1/NS2.PENDINGRENEWALDELETION.COM. This profile is retained as an honest zero: there is no API surface to catalog, and there never was one.

providers.name: AirQtel
providers.description: AirQtel is a Wellesley, Massachusetts aerial surveillance operator founded in 2021 by Vin Loccisano. It sells ultra-high-resolution real-time aerial imaging as a service, flown from its own fleet of manned aircraft and remotely piloted hardware carrying its proprietary "Looking-Glass" imaging systems, to military, government and commercial customers, and announced a $27M Series A in February 2025 following a prototype launch of the Looking Glass aerial network across four countries. Its only published domain, airqtel.com, hosted a three-page Squarespace brochure site (Home, About, Partner Portal login) with no developer program, API, SDK or machine-readable contract of any kind, and as of 2026-09-19 that domain is no longer registered (NXDOMAIN at every public resolver; Verisign RDAP 404).

providers.name: Briko Robotics
providers.description: Briko Robotics (Briko Robotica) was a Mexican educational technology startup founded in 2014 in San Luis Potosi, Mexico, that sold a modular programmable electronics kit paired with an online learning platform teaching robotics and programming to children from roughly age eight. The company was accelerated by 500 Startups LatAm (batch 7) and raised a small seed amount. Third-party company databases now classify Briko Robotics as deadpooled, and its former domain brikorobotics.com has been hijacked and serves unrelated SEO spam. No developer portal, documentation, API, or machine-readable specification was ever published, so this profile carries identity and provenance only.

providers.name: Kespry
providers.description: Kespry was an industrial drone and aerial-intelligence company founded in the San Francisco Bay Area that paired automated fixed-perimeter drones with a cloud analytics platform to turn aerial imagery into measurable data. Its product was used for stockpile and inventory volumetrics in mining and aggregates, construction-site progress monitoring and earthworks, and insurance roof inspection. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Kespry was acquired by Firmatek in 2020 and the brand has since been retired; the former developer and marketing domain kespry.com now issues a 301 redirect to firmatek.com. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for lineage and portfolio mapping, but Kespry publishes no live, standalone developer surface, API, documentation, or client SDKs of its own.
